She is also a fellow of the American Academy of Pediatrics. Dr. Jaskiewicz's research interests include evaluation and management of febrile infants as well as impact of night shift work on pediatric residents.

creators.name: Dr. Mark A. Miller
creators.description: Mark A. Miller, MD, is the chief of the department of microbiology and head of the division of infectious diseases at the Jewish General Hospital in Montreal, Quebec. He is also an adjunct professor of medicine at McGill University. Dr. Miller’s primary research is focused on prevention and treatment of hospital-acquired infections.

creators.name: Dr. Max Hamilton
creators.description: Max Hamilton, MD, FRCP, (d. 1988) was a senior lecturer in psychiatry at the University of Leeds in England. He was also president of the British Psychological Society and received the Paul Hoch Prize for Distinguished Psychiatric Research from the American Psychopathological Association in 1980. Dr. Hamilton’s research focused primarily on psychometrics and clinical statistics.

creators.name: Dr. Nuria Ruíz-Giménez Arrieta
creators.description: Nuria Ruíz-Giménez Arrieta, MD, practices internal medicine at Hospital Universitario de La Princesa, Madrid, Spain. She is also an associate professor at the Universidad Autónoma de Madrid. Dr. Arrieta’s research interests include venous thromboembolism and geriatrics.

creators.name: Dr. Sharon Hunt
creators.description: Sharon Hunt, MD, is a professor of medicine at Stanford University as well as the Med Center Line. She is a member of the Cardiovascular Institute. Dr. Hunt's research focuses on cardiovascular diseases including heart failure and myocardial infarction and is a co-author on many ACC/AHA guidelines.

creators.name: Dr. Dirk Timmerman
creators.description: Dirk Timmerman, MD, PhD is a professor in obstetrics and gynecology at KU Leuven in Leuven, Belgium. He is also a member of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology. Dr. Timmerman’s primary research is focused on gynecology, early pregnancy, oncology, ultrasonography, minimally invasive surgery, and early detection of ovarian cancer.

creators.name: Dr. Todd W. Rice
creators.description: Todd W. Rice, MD, MSc, is a professor of medicine in the division of allergy, pulmonary and critical care medicine at Vanderbilt University Medical Center. He directs Vanderbilt’s medical ICU and medical ECMO program. Dr. Rice is a prolific researcher focused on sepsis, ARDS, acute respiratory failure, and conducting large clinical trials in critically ill patients.

creators.name: Dr. Carl R. Boyd
creators.description: Carl R. Boyd, M.D., is a professor of surgery at Mercer University School of Medicine and Memorial Health University Medical Center in Georgia. He was chief of trauma surgery and surgical critical care at Memorial Health’s trauma center in Savannah for twenty-five years. Dr. Boyd’s primary research is focused on injury and major trauma.

creators.name: Dr. Josep Llovet
creators.description: Josep Llovet, MD, is a professor of medicine and founder and director of the Liver Cancer Program at Mount Sinai Hospital. He was the president, secretary and founder of the International Liver Cancer Association (ILCA) and Chairman of the European Clinical Practice Guidelines of management of liver cancer (EASL-EORTC). He is an active researcher investigating the pathogenesis and treatment of liver cancer.

creators.name: Dr. Jesus Eric Piña-Garza
creators.description: Jesus Eric Piña Garza, MD, is a professor of neurology and pediatrics at Children's Hospital at Centennial Medical Center in Tennessee. He is also the director of the department of pediatric epilepsy. Dr. Piña-Garza's primary research is focused on the management of pediatric seizure disorders.

creators.name: Dr. Ceri Battle
creators.description: Ceri Battle, PhD, is an associate professor of emergency medicine research at the Swansea University School of Medicine in Wales. She is also the director of epidemiology at the Welsh Center for Emergency Medicine Research. Dr. Battle’s primary research is focused on trauma and emergency medicine epidemiology.

creators.name: Dr. Ewout W. Steyerberg
creators.description: Ewout W. Steyerberg, PhD, is a professor at Leiden University Medical Center and Erasmus Medical Center in the Netherlands. He is also the head of the department of medical statistics and bioinformatics. Dr. Steyerberg’s research focuses primarily on biostatistics, clinical epidemiology, and medical decision making.

creators.name: Dr. Frederick Wolfe
creators.description: Frederick Wolfe, MD, is a rheumatologist and clinical professor of medicine at the University of Kansas School of Medicine. He is also the director of the National Data Bank for Rheumatic Disease. Dr. Wolfe’s primary research is focused on outcomes of rheumatic diseases.

creators.name: Dr. James M. Neuberger
creators.description: James M. Neuberger, MD, is an honorary consultant physician at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in Birmingham, UK. He was the associate medical director for Organ Donation and Transplantation at NHS Blood and Transplant. Dr. Neuberger's primary research is focused on liver transplantation planning and outcomes.

creators.name: Dr. Joseph Caprini
creators.description: Joseph A. Caprini, MD, is a senior clinician educator at the Pritzker School of Medicine at the University of Chicago. He is also an emeritus physician at NorthShore University HealthSystem in Evanston, Illinois. Dr. Caprini has authored or co-authored more than 420 articles, book chapters, and abstracts on the study and treatment of venous thromboembolism, venous insufficiency, and related topics.

creators.name: Dr. Lee Goldman
creators.description: Lee Goldman, MD, MPH, is a professor and executive vice president for Health and Biomedical Sciences at Columbia University. He is also the dean of the Faculties of Health Sciences and Medicine at Columbia University Medical Center. Previously, he was a professor, department chair and associate dean at UCSF. Dr. Goldman researches the costs and effectiveness of diagnostic and therapeutic strategies and is well-known for applying the latest methods of multivariate analysis, cost-effectiveness, quality-of-life, and computer-simulation models to key topics in clinical medicine.

creators.name: Dr. Paolo Muratori
creators.description: Paolo Muratori, MD, is an active researcher and clinician, specifically in the Department of Surgery at the University of Bologna in Italy.

creators.name: Douglas D. DeCarolis, PharmD
creators.description: Douglas D. DeCarolis, PharmD, is a research pharmacist at the Minneapolis VA Health Care System in Minneapolis, MN. His primary research is focused on clinical pharmacotherapy.

creators.name: Dr. Donald F. Gleason
creators.description: Donald F. Gleason, MD, PhD, (d. 2008) was former chief of pathology at the Minneapolis VA Medical Center. After completing his medical education, he spent time as a lieutenant in the Army Medical Corps. Though best known for creating the Gleason Score, he practiced urology and pathology many years, and for his accomplishments, he received both the American Urological Association's Presidential Citation Award and an Outstanding Achievement Award from the University of Minnesota.

creators.name: Dr. Eva A. Rocha
creators.description: Eva A. Rocha, MD, PhD, completed this study as a neurology research fellow at Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston. She is now a practicing neurologist at Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein in Brazil and professor of Neurology at Centro Universitario São Camilo. Dr. Rocha's primary research is focused on the treatment of cerebrovascular diseases.

creators.name: Dr. Hilton Mirels
creators.description: Hilton Mirels, MD, is an orthopaedic surgeon and has been in practice for almost 40 years. He completed his training at the University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg, South Africa. Dr. Mirels is best known for his eponymous criteria for long bone fracture.

creators.name: Dr. Martin Than
creators.description: Martin Than, MD, is an emergency medicine specialist at Christchurch Public Hospital. He is the co-director and co-founder of the Clinical Decision Support Unit and is involved in creating a National Trauma Audit Database and reviewing emergency air ambulance and helicopter services. He has trained and worked in Emergency Medicine in the UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand.

creators.name: Dr. Dawn K. Smith
creators.description: Dawn K. Smith, MD, MS, MPH, was a medical officer for the CDC’s Department of HIV Prevention. She was also the CDC’s lead investigator for the first PrEP safety study and she helped develop the CDC’s PrEP guidelines for clinical use. Dr. Smith’s primary research was focused on public health issues, health equity, HIV prevention, and women’s health.

creators.name: Dr. Giancarlo M. Liumbruno
creators.description: Giancarlo M. Liumbruno, MD, is a clinical pathologist specializing in immunohematology, director of the Italian National Blood Centre, and professor of transfusion medicine at University of Florence in Florence, Italy. He previously served as a medical officer in the navy. Dr. Liumbruno's research interests include transfusion therapy, blood management, and bleeding disorders.

creators.name: Dr. Gordon P. Buzby
creators.description: Gordon P. Buzby, MD, (d. 2003) was director of the Surgical Metabolic Unit at the Philadelphia Veteran's Administration Medical Center in Pennsylvania. He also served on the faculty of the Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania. Dr. Buzby’s primary research was focused on total parenteral nutrition in surgical patients.

creators.name: Dr. Himani Gupta
creators.description: Himani Gupta, MD, is an internist at the Methodist Germantown Hospital in Germantown, Tennessee. Dr. Gupta’s primary research is focused on outcomes after surgical procedures.

creators.name: Dr. J. Claude Hemphill, III
creators.description: J. Claude Hemphill, III, MD, MAS, is a professor of medicine and clinician in the Department of Neurology at the University of California, San Francisco. He is also the director of the Neurocritical Care Program at San Francisco General Hospital Medical Center. Dr. Hemphill cares for patients with stroke and traumatic brain injury and has a special research interest in intracerebral hemorrhage.

creators.name: Dr. Janis Fox
creators.description: Janis H. Fox, MD, is an assistant professor in obstetrics, gynecology and reproductive biology at Harvard Medical School. She is also an attending reproductive endocrinologist in the Center for Infertility and Reproductive Surgery at Brigham and Women’s Hospital. Her clinical practice focuses primarily on infertility and assisted reproductive technologies. Dr. Fox has published on factors contributing to success and failure following in vitro fertilization.

creators.name: Dr. Kathryn A. Oakland
creators.description: Kathryn A. Oakland, MD, MBBS, is head of surgery at HCA Healthcare UK in London, United Kingdom. She is also working on the NHS COVID-19 response for the North and Central London Sustainability and Transformation Partnerships. Dr. Oakland’s research focuses primarily on gastrointestinal bleeding.

creators.name: Dr. Timothy W. Menza
creators.description: Timothy W. Menza, MD, PhD, is an assistant professor in the division of infectious diseases at Oregon Health & Science University. He is also the medical director of the HIV/STD/TB section of the public health division at the Oregon Health Authority. Dr. Menza’s primary research is focused on epidemiology and the prevention and treatment of HIV, sexually transmitted infections, and hepatitis C.

creators.name: Dr. Ehud Chorin
creators.description: Ehud Chorin, MD, PhD, is a physician in the cardiology department at Tel Aviv Medical Center in Israel. Dr. Chorin’s primary research is focused on treatment of coronary heart disease.

creators.name: Dr. Fletcher B. Taylor
creators.description: Fletcher B. Taylor, MS, MD, is a Distinguished Career Scientist at the Oklahoma Medical Research Foundation in Oklahoma City. He was previously the H.A. and Mary K. Chapman Chair in Medical Research. Dr. Taylor’s primary research is focused on diagnosis and treatment of sepsis.

creators.name: Dr. Frédéric Lapostolle
creators.description: Frédéric Lapostolle, MD, PhD, is an emergency physician at Avicenne Hospital in Bobigny, France. He is deputy medical director of Samu 93 Emergency Rescue Service. Dr. Lapostolle is a professor of emergency medicine and has authored or co-authored over 100 papers in his specialty.

creators.name: Dr. Jaana Lindström
creators.description: Jaana Lindström, PhD, MSC, is a researcher in the department of chronic disease prevention at the National Public Health Institute in Helsinki, Finland. Her research interests are centered around the prevention and prediction of diabetes. She has also published on nutrition and obesity.

creators.name: Dr. Pierre-Marie Roy
creators.description: Pierre-Marie Roy, MD, PhD, is an emergency physician at the University Hospital of Angers in France. He is also a professor of medicine at the University of Angers and a scientist member of the MitoVasc Institute and the F-CRIN InnoVTE Research Network. Dr. Roy's primary research topics include clinical risk prediction, venous thromboembolism, antithrombotic treatments, and care organization in emergency medicine. He especially focused on the Right Care in emergency medicine and reducing the overuse and misuse of care.

creators.name: Dr. Fumihiko Miura
creators.description: Fumihiko Miura, MD, is a physician in the department of surgery at the Teikyo University School of Medicine in Tokyo, Japan. Dr. Miura's primary research is focused on the grading and management of acute cholangitis.

creators.name: Dr. Janusz Kaczorowski
creators.description: Janusz Kaczorowski, MA, PhD, is a professor and research director at the Department of Family and Emergency Medicine at the Université de Montréal. Dr. Kaczorowski is an influential researcher investigating optimal use of therapeutics in primary care, primary prevention of cardiovascular disease and stroke, knowledge transfer, health services research, and population health.

creators.name: Dr. Jens Kondrup
creators.description: Jens Kondrup, MD, is a senior physician at Rigshospitalet in Copenhagen, Denmark. He is the chair of the Danish Society of Clinical Nutrition. Dr. Kondrup is a former professor in the department of nutrition at the University of Copenhagen.

creators.name: Dr. Bradley C. Leibovich
creators.description: Bradley C. Leibovich, MD, is a professor of urology at the Mayo Clinic College of Medicine. He is also a consultant in the Department of Urology at Mayo Clinic and the medical director of the Center of Digital Health. Dr. Leibovich’s primary research is focused on renal and testicular cancer.

creators.name: Dr. Julie R. Brahmer
creators.description: Julie R. Brahmer, MSc, MD, is the co-director of the upper aerodigestive department at Johns Hopkins Medicine in Baltimore, MD. She is also a professor of oncology at Johns Hopkins Medicine. Dr. Brahmer’s primary research is focused on treatment of lung cancer and mesothelioma.

creators.name: Dr. Katharine Bradley
creators.description: Katharine Bradley, MD, MPH, is a senior Investigator at the Group Health Research Institute and concentrates on identifying and addressing unhealthy alcohol use in primary care. She is currently leading the NIH's Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism Study. Formerly, Dr. Bradley worked at the Veterans Affairs (VA) Puget Sound Health Care System, where she practiced primary care for over 15 years.

creators.name: Dr. Lise Nigrovic
creators.description: Lise E. Nigrovic, MD, MPH, is an associate professor of pediatrics and emergency medicine at Harvard Medical School. She serves as co-director of Population Science for the Institutional Centers for Clinical and Translational Research (ICCTR) and the Boston Children’s Hospital Medical Research Office for Harvard Catalyst. Dr. Nigrovic’s research focus has been in the approach to diagnosis and management of children with infectious and traumatic emergencies.

creators.name: Dr. Luca Malcovati
creators.description: Luca Malcovati, MD, is a hematologist at the IRCCS Policlinico San Matteo Foundation in Pavia, Italy. He is also an associate professor of hematology in the department of molecular medicine at University of Pavia Medical School. Dr. Malcovati’s research interests include myeloid neoplasms, the prognosis of myelodysplastic syndrome, and providing evidence-based guidelines.

creators.name: Dr. Manuel Mutschler
creators.description: Manuel Mutschler, MD, is a practicing physician in the Department of Trauma and Orthopedic Surgery at the Cologne-Merheim Medical Center, affiliated with University of Witten/Herdecke. He is an active researcher with interests including hypovolaemic and hemorrhagic shock.

creators.name: Dr. Silvia Schönenberger
creators.description: Silvia Schönenberger, MD, is a professor in the department of neurology at the Heidelberg University Hospital in Germany. She is also the medical director of the neurological intensive care unit (NICU) at the hospital. Dr. Schönenberger’s primary research is focused on airway management and ventilation therapy in patients with severe strokes.

creators.name: Dr. Furio Colivicchi
creators.description: Furio Colivicchi, MD, is a practicing cardiologist in Rome, Italy. He is Director of Cardiology at San Filippo Neri Hospital. Dr. Colivicchi’s research interests include syncope risk stratification and the use of statins in acute coronary syndrome.

creators.name: Dr. Shamai A. Grossman
creators.description: Shamai A. Grossman, MD, MS, is an associate professor of medicine and emergency medicine at Harvard Medical School and an emergency physician at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center. He serves as vice chair for health care quality with Harvard Medical Faculty Physicians and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center. Dr. Grossman is an applied clinical researcher investigating diagnostic safety and quality improvement in emergency care, including strategies to reduce critical cardiac misdiagnoses.

creators.name: Dr. Henry Gault
creators.description: Henry Gault, MD, MSc, (d. 2003) was named professor emeritus in 1993 after nearly 20 years as a physician and professor at Memorial University of Newfoundland. He was also director for the Division of Nephrology at the General Hospital and of the Renal Laboratory. Dr. Gault was a pioneer in the field of nephrology and his work on urine enzymology was a major influence on the discovery of the diagnosis of the rejection of kidney transplants.

creators.name: Dr. Les Vertesi
creators.description: Les Vertesi, MD, is the executive director of British Columbia's Health Services Purchasing Organization and a part-time emergency room physician. He is on the faculty of Simon Fraser University's Institute for Health Research and Education and is associate director of Health Research with the Fraser Health Authority of British Columbia. Dr. Vertesi published a book in 2003: Broken Promises: The Trouble with Canadian Medicare...and How to Fix it.

creators.name: Dr. Gregory Lip
creators.description: Gregory Lip, MD, is the David A. Price-Evans Chair in Cardiovascular Medicine at the University of Liverpool and an honorary consultant cardiologist at Liverpool Heart and Chest Hospital. He is also a researcher in the Aalborg Thrombosis Research Unit at Aalborg University in Denmark. Dr. Lip is one of the world’s leading experts in risk stratification of atrial fibrillation, with his research directly informing the widely-used CHA₂DS₂-Vasc and HAS-BLED Scores.

creators.name: Dr. Thomas Moumneh
creators.description: Thomas Moumneh, MD, is an emergency physician at Université d’Angers, France. Dr. Moumneh is an applied clinical researcher focusing on emergency cardiovascular and thromboembolic care, including diagnostic strategies and risk stratification in the emergency department.

creators.name: Dr. J. P. Flatt
creators.description: J. P. Flatt, PhD, is a professor emeritus of Biochemistry and Molecular Pharmacology at the University of Massachusetts. His research focuses on metabolic processes of fat breakdown, obesity and physical activity.

creators.name: Dr. Jordi Rello
creators.description: Jordi Rello, MD, PhD, is a professor of medicine at the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona in Spain. He is also the director of the Clinical Research and Innovation in Pneumonia and Sepsis Group at the Vall d'Hebron Research Institute. Dr. Rello’s primary research is focused on the prevention and treatment of hospital and community-acquired pneumonia as well as critical cases of sepsis and infection.

creators.name: Dr. Laurent Mandelbrot
creators.description: Laurent Mandelbrot, MD, is head of the department of obstetrics and gynecology and professor of medicine at the Louis Mourier Hospital in Colombes, France. Dr. Mandelbrot's primary research interest is HIV in pregnancy.

creators.name: Dr. Lenna L. Liu
creators.description: Lenna L. Liu, MPH, MD, is a professor of pediatrics at the University of Washington School of Medicine and Seattle Children's Hospital. She is also a practicing pediatrician at the Odessa Brown Children's Clinic in Seattle, WA. Dr. Liu’s primary research is focused on obesity in youth with diabetes.

creators.name: Dr. Marinos Elia
creators.description: Marinos Elia, MD, BSc Hon, FRCP, is a professor of clinical nutrition and metabolism at the University of Southampton in UK. He was previously the editor-in-chief of Clinical Nutrition and chair of the British Association for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (BAPEN). Dr. Elia’s primary research is focused on nutritional screening and health economics of malnutrition.

creators.name: Dr. Robert A. Hegele
creators.description: Robert A. Hegele, MD, is a professor of medicine and biochemistry at Western University in London, Ontario and the director of the London Regional Genomics Centre at the Robarts Research Institute. He also holds the Jacob J. Wolfe Distinguished Medical Research Chair in Human Gene Function and the Martha G. Blackburn Chair in Cardiovascular Research. Dr. Hegele’s primary research is focused on the genetic basis of several human disorders, including dyslipidemia and type 2 diabetes.

creators.name: Dr. Jeffrey L. Saver
creators.description: Jeffrey L. Saver, MD, is a professor and vice-chair of neurology at the University of California, Los Angeles. He is also the director of the UCLA Comprehensive Stroke and Vascular Neurology Program and has published over 1030 peer-reviewed articles. Dr. Saver’s research interests include stroke prevention, diagnosis, and treatment, as well as outcomes after stroke.

creators.name: Dr. Henry Cuthbert Bazett
creators.description: Henry Cuthbert Bazett, MD, (d. 1950) was the head of the Department of Physiology at the University of Pennsylvania and was a leader of the American Society of Physiology. He served in the British Medical Corps in World War I. Dr. Bazett is best known for his work with electrocardiogram interpretation and contributed greatly to the study of circulation in humans by using invasive catheterization.

creators.name: Dr. John Macfarlane
creators.description: John Macfarlane, MD, is a consultant respiratory physician at Nottingham City Hospital in the United Kingdom. He is an active researcher in the field of thoracic medicine with a special focus on bacterial and community acquired infections.

creators.name: Dr. Kimberly Van Zee
creators.description: Kimberly J. Van Zee, MS, MD, is a surgical oncologist exclusively practicing and primarily researching topics within the realm of breast cancer treatment. She sees outpatients in the new Evelyn H. Lauder Breast Center and performs surgeries regularly. She has received the American Cancer Society's Clinical Oncology Career Development award, and is frequently in the New York Magazine's 'Best Doctors in New York.'

creators.name: Dr. Madan Samuel
creators.description: Madan Samuel, MD, is a pediatric surgeon and urologist, currently at the Al Zahra Hospital in Dubai. He has been awarded by the Prime Minister of India and the United Kingdom for his accomplishments in his field. Dr. Samuel is an active researcher, having published over 66 articles in peer reviewed journals and book chapters in ten pediatric surgical textbooks.

creators.name: Dr. Seema Mital
creators.description: Seema Mital, MD, is a Professor of Pediatrics and Head of Cardiovascular Research at The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids) at the University of Toronto. She is also the Heart and Stroke Foundation of Ontario/Robert M Freedom Chair of Cardiovascular Science and Scientific Lead of the Cardiac Precision Medicine Program of the Ted Rogers Centre for Heart Research. Dr. Mital’s primary research is focused on precision medicine approaches for childhood onset heart disease. The development and implementation of PRIMaCY was funded by the Ted Rogers Centre for Heart Research and the Canadian Institutes of Health Research.

creators.name: PREVENT™ Team
creators.description: The Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events (PREVENT TM ) calculator was a collaborative research and publishing effort between many academic and professional groups. Collaborative workgroups and studies include the American Heart Association Risk Prediction Workgroup for the Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Science Advisory Group, Chronic Kidney Disease Prognosis Consortium, Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) study, Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults Study (CARDIA), Cardiovascular Health Study (CHS), Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort Study (CRIC), Framingham Heart Study, Geisinger Health System, Jackson Heart Study (JHS), Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA), Rancho Bernardo Study, and Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke Study (REGARDS). Please see the original paper for a full list of authors and their affiliations.

creators.name: Rev. Thomas Bayes
creators.description: Reverend Thomas Bayes (d. 1761) was an 18th century English statistician. He is best known today for developing the eponymous theorem on which much of modern biostatistics and epidemiology is based. Rev. Bayes was also a minister and a philosopher.

creators.name: Dr. Jacques-Louis Binet
creators.description: Jacques-Louis Binet, MD, is a retired hematologist at the Hôpital de la Pitié-Salpétrière in Paris, France. During his time practicing medicine, he was also a professor of medicine at the Pierre and Marie-Curie University in Paris, France. Dr. Binet’s primary research was focused on immunology, blood transfusion, and leukemia.

creators.name: Dr. Lesley A. Inker
creators.description: Lesley A. Inker, MD, MS, is an associate professor at Tufts University School of Medicine, an attending physician in the William B. Schwartz, MD Division of Nephrology at Tufts Medical Center, and medical director of the Kidney And Blood Pressure Center at Tufts Medical Center in Massachusetts. Dr. Inker's primary research interests are in GFR measurement and estimation, alternative endpoints for clinical trials of kidney disease progression, and epidemiology and outcomes related to CKD.

creators.name: Dr. Menno Huisman
creators.description: Menno Huisman, MD, PhD, FESC, is a professor of medicine in the department of medicine - thrombosis and hemostasis at Leiden University Medical Center in The Netherlands. He is an internist with specialty in cardiovascular medicine. Dr. Huisman’s primary research is focused on the clinical diagnosis and treatment of venous and arterial thromboembolic disorders.

creators.name: Dr. Mohamed Sorror
creators.description: Mohamed Sorror, MD, is an associate professor of medicine at the University of Washington. He is also an associate member of the clinical research division at Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center. Dr. Sorror’s research interests are focused on hematological malignancies.

creators.name: Dr. Robert H. Bartlett
creators.description: Robert H. Bartlett, MD, is Professor Emeritus of General Surgery at the University of Michigan. As Professor of Surgery in the Sections of General and Thoracic Surgery, he developed a Surgical Critical Care Fellowship and the Extracorporeal Life Support Program. Dr. Bartlett’s cutting edge research includes the development of an artificial liver system for use in patients awaiting liver transplant.

creators.name: Ted Rogers Centre for Heart Research
creators.description: Founded in 2014, the Ted Rogers Centre for Heart Research’s mission is to transform and dramatically improve the future of heart health for children, adults, and families across Canada and around the world, through an integrated program of outstanding research, education, and clinical care. At the Ted Rogers Centre for Heart Research, pre-eminent experts in a variety of disciplines including cardiology, bioengineering, computer science, cell biology, pediatrics, nursing, genomic medicine, and immunology work together to accelerate the discovery of new approaches to treating heart failure. A model for collaborative medicine, it has reaffirmed Toronto as a global hub for cutting-edge cardiovascular research.

creators.name: Dr. Charles R. Westley
creators.description: Charles R. Westley, MD, is affiliated with the Department of Allergy and Asthma at Kaiser Permanente in Denver, CO. Dr. Westley’s primary research is focused on allergy and immunology conditions, such as coccidioidomycosis, croup, and asthma.

creators.name: Dr. Heejung Bang
creators.description: Heejung Bang, PhD, is a professor of biostatistics at the University of California, Davis. She has authored or co-authored over 100 peer-reviewed papers in epidemiology and statistics. Dr. Bang's research interests include clinical trials and observational studies, medical cost and cost-effectiveness analysis, and prediction and screening modeling.

creators.name: Dr. Hein Janssens
creators.description: Hein J. E. M. Janssens, MD, is a researcher in the Department of Primary and Community Care, Radboud University Nijmegen Medical Center, in Nijmegen, the Netherlands. He practices in the fields of internal medicine, primary care and rheumatology.

creators.name: Dr. John F. Kurtzke
creators.description: John F. Kurtzke, MD, (d. 2015) was professor emeritus of neurology at Georgetown University. He was a leading expert in the study of multiple sclerosis (MS) and a contributor in the creation of the field of neuroepidemiology. Dr. Kurtzke authored over 200 peer-reviewed articles and received multiple awards for MS research including the Charcot Award from the MS International Federation.

creators.name: Dr. Michael J. Palchak
creators.description: Michael J. Palchak, MD, is an emergency medicine physician at Sutter Davis Hospital in Emeryville, California. He has been in practice for 20 years. Dr. Palchak’s primary research interest is management of pediatric blunt head trauma.

creators.name: Dr. Jeffrey Hyams
creators.description: Jeffrey Hyams, MD, is a professor of pediatrics at the University of Connecticut School of Medicine. He currently serves on the Rome Committee, an international research organization that investigates the course and treatment of functional GI disorders. Dr. Hyams' research focuses on pediatric digestive diseases, and he is a co-author of Pediatric Gastrointestinal and Liver Disease , now in its 5th edition.

creators.name: Dr. Joel S. Tieder
creators.description: Joel S. Tieder, MD, MPH is a Professor of Pediatrics in the Division of Hospital Medicine at Seattle Children’s Hospital and the University Of Washington School Of Medicine. He is a pediatric hospitalist with scholarly focus on improving the delivery of quality care for hospitalized children, particularly through overcoming healthcare disparities and the use of evidence-based and family-centered care. Nationally, he is the Chair for the American Academy of Pediatrics’ Council for Quality Improvement and Patient Safety.

creators.name: Dr. Leslie J. Witts
creators.description: Leslie J. Witts, CBE FRCP, (d. 1982) was a gastroenterologist and hematologist in Oxford, UK. He became the first Nuffield professor of clinical medicine at the University of Oxford and was the co-founder of the British Society of Gastroenterology. Dr. Witts' primary research was focused on treatment of iron-deficiency anemia.

creators.name: Dr. Magdy Selim
creators.description: Magdy Selim, MD, PhD, is chief of the Division of Stroke and Cerebrovascular Diseases at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center. He is also a professor of neurology at Harvard Medical School. His current research interests include cerebrovascular disease, brain imaging, and thrombolysis. His field of interest is advancing the diagnosis and improving the treatment of stroke, with a specific focus on developing new therapies for patients with a brain hemorrhage.

creators.name: Dr. Marika Hohol
creators.description: Marika Hohol, MD, is an associate professor in the division of neurology at the University of Toronto. Previously, she was the Neurology Residency Program Director and co-director for the Brain and Behavior course. Dr. Hohol’s academic interests include clinical trials for multiple sclerosis (MS) and the management and education of MS patients.

creators.name: Dr. Mark Hlatky
creators.description: Mark A. Hlatky, MD, is a professor of cardiovascular medicine and health research and policy at Stanford University. He is also a Fellow of the Center on Health Policy (CHP) and the Center on Primary Care and Outcomes Research (PCOR) at Stanford. Dr. Hlatky’s research interests include improved outcomes and cost effectiveness of cardiovascular treatments through the application of evidence-based medicine.

creators.name: Dr. Ramnath Misra
creators.description: Ramnath Misra, MD, FRCP, is a professor and head of the immunology department at Sanjay Gandhi Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences in Lucknow, India. He is also the former president of the Indian Rheumatology Association. Dr. Misra’s primary research is focused on arthritis, undifferentiated spondyloarthropathy, and systemic lupus erythematosus.

creators.name: Dr. Norbert Schmitz
creators.description: Norbert Schmitz, MD, is the head of the department for hematology and stem cell transplantation at Asklepios Klinik St. Georg in Hamburg, Germany. He is also a member of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology and the European Group for Blood and Marrow Transplantation. Dr. Schmitz’s primary research is focused on hematopoietic chimerism, lymphoma and immunotherapy, and autologous and allogenic bone marrow transplantation.

creators.name: Dr. Jason S. Haukoos
creators.description: Jason S. Haukoos, MD, is the research director of the emergency medicine department at Denver Health Medical Center. He is also an associate professor of emergency medicine at the University of Colorado Denver. Dr. Haukoos' primary research is focused on hospital and infectious disease epidemiology, and HIV/AIDS screening.

creators.name: Dr. Lucien Campeau
creators.description: Lucien Campeau, MD, (d. 2010) was both a clinician and cardiology professor at the Université de Montréal in Quebec, Canada. He was also a co-founder of the Montreal Heart Institute in Quebec and was president of the Montreal Cardiac Society. Dr. Campeau’s research focused primarily on aortocoronary bypass grafts and coronary angiographies.

creators.name: Dr. Neal Jacobs
creators.description: Neal Jacobs, MD, FRCS, is a consultant orthopaedic surgeon at the Salisbury NHS Foundation Trust and New Hall Hospital in Salisbury, UK. He served as a medical officer in the Royal Air Force for over 16 years before retiring with the rank of wing commander in 2015. Dr. Jacobs' work has been published in numerous peer-reviewed publications in the orthopedic medical literature, and he has also co-authored a book chapter.

creators.name: Dr. Ognjen Gajic
creators.description: Ognjen Gajic, MD, is a professor of medicine at the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota. He is also the chair of the U.S. Critical Illness and Injury Trials Network Prevention of Organ Failure Study Group. Dr. Gajic’s primary research is focused on the epidemiology and management of critical care conditions with an emphasis on acute lung injury and multiorgan dysfunction.

creators.name: International Non-Hodgkin’s Lymphoma Prognostic Factors Project
creators.description: The International Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma Prognostic Factor Project was undertaken to develop a model for predicting outcomes in patients with aggressive non-Hodgkin's lymphoma on the basis of the patients' clinical characteristics before treatment.

creators.name: Dr. Jon M. Hanifin
creators.description: Jon M. Hanifin, MD, is a board-certified dermatologist and professor of dermatology at the Oregon Health and Science University School of Medicine in Portland, Oregon. Dr. Hanifin’s primary research is focused on treatment of atopic dermatitis.

creators.name: Dr. Karen Alexander
creators.description: Karen Alexander, MD, is cardiologist at Duke University Hospital and Durham Veterans Affairs Medical Center. She is also co-director of Integrated Clinical Event and Safety Surveillance (ICE-SS) and associate professor of cardiology at the Duke Clinical Research institute (DCRI). Dr. Alexander's research focuses on cardiovascular disease management and outcomes in special populations, specifically women and the elderly.

creators.name: Dr. Luzius A. Steiner
creators.description: Luzius A. Steiner, MD, PhD, is a professor and the head of anesthesiology at University Hospital Basel in Switzerland. He has authored or co-authored dozens of studies in neurocritical care on cerebral perfusion pressure. Dr. Steiner is a member of the European Society of Intensive Care Medicine and the European Society of Anesthesiology.

creators.name: Dr. Manne Andersson
creators.description: Manne Andersson, MD, is a vascular surgeon in the department of clinical and experimental medicine and the division of surgery, orthopedic and oncology at Linköping University in Linköping, Sweden. Dr. Andersson’s research interests include gangrenous appendicitis and acute appendicitis diagnostic tools.

creators.name: Dr. Margaret M. Hoehn
creators.description: Margaret M. Hoehn, MD, (d. 2005) was a professor of neurology at Columbia University. She also served as director of the Parkinson's Disease and Movement Disorders Program at the University of Colorado School of Medicine in Denver. Her research centered on Parkinson's disease and the effects of Parkinson’s treatments. Dr. Hoehn was the first to build a rating scale for neurological assessment of Parkinson’s patients.

creators.name: Dr. Matthew M. Churpek
creators.description: Matthew M. Churpek, MD, PhD, MPH, is an assistant professor of medicine at the University of Chicago Medical Center. He has been awarded the American Heart Association Young Investigator Award. Dr. Churpek’s research focuses primarily on clinical prediction models, inpatient hospital deaths, and clinical deterioration.

creators.name: Dr. Melissa Austin
creators.description: Melissa Austin, PhD, MS, is a professor emeritus of epidemiology at the University of Washington. Her research spans many areas including genetic epidemiology of chronic diseases, lipoprotein metabolism and pancreatic cancer.

creators.name: Dr. Rajiv Jalan
creators.description: Rajiv Jalan, MBBS, MRCP, is a professor of hepatology at the Institute for Liver and Digestive Health at University College London in UK. Dr. Jalan’s primary research is focused on acute-on-chronic liver failure.

creators.name: Dr. Jan Claassen
creators.description: Jan Claassen, MD, is Associate Professor of Neurology at Columbia University Medical College in New York. He is currently the Head of Neurocritical Care and Medical Director of the Neurological Intensive Care Unit. He has numerous publications in many journals focusing on neurointensive care, cerebrovascular diseases, encephalopathy, and coagulopathy, among other topics.

creators.name: Dr. Joon Y. Lee
creators.description: Joon Y. Lee, MD, is an orthopedic surgeon at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center. He is also a professor in the orthopedic surgery department at the University of Pittsburgh. Dr. Lee’s primary research is focused on cervical, thoracic, and lumbar spine surgery.

creators.name: Dr. Mitchell Gail
creators.description: Mitchell Gail, MD, PhD, is an adjunct professor at Johns Hopkins University and a principal investigator at the National Cancer Institute Division of Cancer Epidemiology & Genetics, Biostatistics Branch. He is a former president of the American Statistical Association. He has won numerous awards, most notably the American Cancer Society Award for Research Excellence in Cancer Epidemiology and Prevention. His research focuses on creating models for determining absolute risk of diseases.

creators.name: Dr. Rahul Aggarwal
creators.description: Rahul Aggarwal, MD, is a cardiology fellow at Brigham and Women's Hospital, Harvard Medical School. He is an active clinician, physician-scientist, and educator, skilled in advanced data analytics and statistics with large medical health data repositories. Dr. Aggarwal is a distinguished researcher focused on clinical trials, risk prediction, model development, outcomes, health services, and health policy.

creators.name: Dr. Jamie L. Waldron
creators.description: Jamie L. Waldron, MD, is an allergist–immunologist at Massachusetts General Hospital and an instructor in medicine at Harvard Medical School. Dr. Waldron’s research focuses on drug allergy, including the evaluation and management of antibiotic allergies, risk stratification, and safe delabeling strategies that support antimicrobial stewardship.

creators.name: Dr. Mary Charlson
creators.description: Mary Charlson, MD, is the William Foley Professor of Medicine, Chief of General Internal Medicine and the Program Chairperson for the Master of Science Program in Clinical Epidemiology and Health Services Research at Weill Cornell Medical College. She is also a clinical epidemiologist and methodologist. Dr. Charlson has also developed new methods of improving prognostic stratification in acute and chronic illness.

creators.name: Dr. Michael J. Fine
creators.description: Michael J. Fine, MD, MSc, is a professor in the Division of General Internal Medicine at the University of Pittsburgh. He is also the director of the Center for Health Equity Research and Promotion (CHERP) at the VA Pittsburgh Healthcare System. Dr. Fine’s research focuses on improving healthcare equity for patients with common medical conditions, such as community-acquired pneumonia, venous thromboembolism, and diabetes, especially in vulnerable patient populations.

creators.name: Dr. R. Andrew Taylor
creators.description: Andrew Taylor, MD, MHS, is an associate professor of emergency medicine at Yale University in Connecticut. He is also the Director of Clinical Informatics and Analytics at Yale New Haven Hospital. Dr. Taylor’s primary research is focused on machine learning and big data in the context of emergency medicine.

creators.name: Dr. Robert G. Hart
creators.description: Robert G. Hart, MD, is a professor of medicine and neurology at McMaster University in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada. He also serves as co-director of the McMaster/Hamilton Health Sciences Stroke Fellowship Program and previously directed the stroke program at the University of Texas Health Sciences Center for 25 years. Dr. Hart's research interests include stroke prevention, stroke risk in atrial fibrillation, and novel stroke therapies.

creators.name: Dr. Robin T. Vollmer
creators.description: Robin T. Vollmer, MD, MS, is an associate clinical professor and director of surgical pathology at the Durham Veterans Affairs Hospital. He is a board certified dermatopathologist and anatomic and clinical pathologist. Dr. Vollmer is also affiliated with the pathology department at Duke University Medical Center.

creators.name: Dr. Roxana Mehran
creators.description: Roxana Mehran, MD, FACC, FACP, FCCP, FESC, FAHA, FSCAI, is a professor in the department of medicine, cardiology, and population health science and policy at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai. She is also the director of the Center for Interventional Cardiovascular Research and Clinical Trials at the Zena and Michael A. Wiener Cardiovascular Institute. Dr. Mehran’s primary research is focused on angioplasty and stent placement, cardiac catheterization, and acute coronary syndromes.

creators.name: Dr. Stephen D. Wiviott
creators.description: Stephen D. Wiviott, MD, is an associate professor of cardiovascular medicine at Harvard Medical School. He is also a practicing physician in the Lown Cardiovascular Intensive Care Unit at Brigham and Women's Hospital in Massachusetts. Dr. Wiviott is a senior investigator in the TIMI Study Group and has published over 100 peer-reviewed articles and multiple chapters in major cardiovascular textbooks.

creators.name: Dr. Andrew T. Kunzmann
creators.description: Andrew T. Kunzmann, PhD, is an epidemiologist in evidence synthesis and classification at the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC). He trained in cancer epidemiology and public health at Queen’s University Belfast. Dr. Kunzmann’s primary research is focused on cancer epidemiology, evidence synthesis, and identifying individuals at high risk of gastrointestinal cancers to better target screening and prevention.

creators.name: Dr. Marie Åsberg
creators.description: Marie Åsberg, MD, PhD, is a psychiatrist and professor in the department of clinical sciences at the Danderyd Hospital in Sweden. Dr. Åsberg’s primary research is focused on depression and suicide prevention.

creators.name: Dr. Marion Smits
creators.description: Marion Smits, MD, is an associate professor and neuroradiologist at Erasmus University Medical Center in Rotterdam, Netherlands. She is the principal investigator of applied physiological MR neuroimaging, focusing on the non-invasive, in vivo visualization of brain function. Dr. Smits is also an honorary consultant and reader at University College London Hospital NHS Foundation Trust in London.

creators.name: Dr. Miles J. Belgrade
creators.description: Miles J. Belgrade, MD, is the medical director of Fairview Pain and Palliative Care Center. He is also an adjunct professor in the neurology department at University of Minnesota Medical School. Dr. Belgrade's primary research is focused on neuropathy, pain medicine, and treatment planning.

creators.name: Dr. Peiman Nazerian
creators.description: Peiman Nazerian, MD, is an internist in the emergency department at the Careggi University Hospital in Florence, Italy. He is an instructor in emergency ultrasound and has taught multiple courses in Italy and internationally. Dr. Nazerian's primary research interests are in pulmonary embolism and aortic dissection in the emergency setting.

creators.name: Dr. Nuhad K. Ibrahim
creators.description: Nuhad K. Ibrahim, MD, is a professor of oncology in the department of breast medical oncology at the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center in Houston, TX. He is also the vice chair of the university’s Institutional Review Board and a member of the U.S.-Middle East Breast Cancer Awareness & Research Committee. Dr. Ibrahim’s primary research is focused on vaccines for breast cancer, breast geriatric oncology, and treatment of resistant breast cancer.

creators.name: Dr. Mohamad Jawhar
creators.description: Mohamad Jawhar, MD, is a hematologist in the Department of Hematology and Oncology at the Medical Faculty Mannheim, Heidelberg University. He contributes extensively to international systemic mastocytosis registries such as the ECNM, and has authored numerous papers on myeloid neoplasms and mast cell disorders. Dr. Jawhar is an influential researcher investigating prognostic modeling, molecular risk stratification, and disease biology in systemic mastocytosis and related myeloid neoplasms.

creators.name: Dr. Markus Leitinger
creators.description: Markus Leitinger, MD, is a neurologist and neurophysiologist in the department of neurology at Paracelsus Medical University in Salzburg, Austria. He is also board certified for electroencephalography and electromyography. Dr. Leitinger’s primary research is focused on status epilepticus, specifically non-convulsive status epilepticus.

creators.name: Dr. Michael Von Korff
creators.description: Michael Von Korff, ScD, is a senior investigator at Kaiser Permanente Washington Health Research Institute. He is also the co-founder of Physicians for Responsible Opioid Prescribing, an organization that promotes selective opioid prescribing. Dr. Von Korff’s primary research is focused on chronic pain management.

creators.name: Dr. Peter W.F. Wilson
creators.description: Peter W. F. Wilson, MD, is professor of medicine in the cardiology division of Emory University and a professor of public health at the Rollins School of Public Health. He is currently the director of epidemiology and genomic medicine at the Atlanta VA Medical Center. Dr. Wilson researches metabolic and cardiovascular population issues, focusing on determinants of CAD, including diabetes mellitus, hormonal factors, inflammatory markers, and genetics.

creators.name: Dr. Ravindra L. Mehta
creators.description: Ravindra L. Mehta, MD, is a nephrology professor and associate chair for clinical affairs in the department of medicine at the University of California, San Diego. He is also the president of the Acute Dialysis Quality Initiative and the Acute Kidney Injury Network (AKIN). Dr. Mehta’s primary research focuses on kidney disease and its underlying causes.

creators.name: Dr. Richard L. Gamelli
creators.description: Richard L. Gamelli, MD, FACS, is professor emeritus at the Stritch School of Medicine at Loyola University Chicago. He has served as the director of the Burn and Shock Trauma Research Institute, chairman of the department of surgery, and chief of the burn center at Loyola University Medical Center. Dr. Gamelli has published over 175 peer-reviewed manuscripts and abstracts, written 30 book chapters, and edited 10 books.

creators.name: Dr. Robert W. Steiner
creators.description: Robert W. Steiner, MD, is co-director of Transplant Nephrology and the medical director of Kidney and Pancreas Transplantation at UC San Diego. He is also the medical director of Lifesharing Community Organ and Tissue Donation of San Diego. He completed his medical degree, residency and fellowship at Harvard/Mass Gen. He currently researches steroid use in kidney transplantation.

creators.name: Dr. Roland du Bois
creators.description: Roland M. Dubois, MD, is a professor of respiratory medicine and senior research investigator at Imperial College in London. Previously, he was a professor at National Jewish Health in Denver and Consultant Physician at the Royal Brompton Hospital. Dr. du Bois advises on studies of innovative therapy for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and conducts research on genetics, pathogenesis and treatment of interstitial lung diseases.

creators.name: Dr. Suzanne McDiarmid
creators.description: Suzanne McDiarmid, MD, is the chief of pediatric gastroenterology and the director of the UCLA Intestinal Transplant Program and Intestinal Failure Center at UCLA Medical Center. She is also a professor of pediatrics at the UCLA School of Medicine. Dr. McDiarmid researches liver and pancreatic transplantation.

creators.name: Dr. Marinos Elia
creators.description: Marinos Elia, MD, BSc (Hons), FRCP, is a professor of clinical nutrition and metabolism at the University of Southampton in the UK. He was previously the editor-in-chief of Clinical Nutrition and chair of the British Association for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (BAPEN). Dr. Elia’s primary research is focused on nutritional screening and health economics of malnutrition.

creators.name: Dr. Peter Greenberg
creators.description: Peter Greenberg, MD, is professor emeritus of hematology at Stanford University. He is also director of the Stanford Myelodysplastic Syndrome (MDS) Center, coordinator of the International Working Group for Prognosis in MDS and chair of the National Comprehensive Cancer Network MDS Practice Guidelines Panel. Dr. Greenberg’s research focuses on evaluating molecular and genetic abnormalities in myelodysplastic syndromes.

creators.name: Dr. Robert A. Balk
creators.description: Robert A. Balk, MD, is a professor and practicing physician in pulmonology, internal medicine and critical care at Rush University Medical Center. His research interests include septic shock, acute lung injury, acute respiratory distress syndrome and ventilator-associated pneumonia.

creators.name: Dr. Oanh K. Nguyen
creators.description: Oanh K. Nguyen, MD, MAS, is an assistant professor in residence at the University of California, San Francisco. She is also an associate editor for the Journal of Hospital Medicine . Dr. Nguyen’s primary research is focused on improving delivery of health care.

creators.name: Dr. Pauline Brice
creators.description: Pauline Brice, MD, is a hematologist at Hopital Saint-Louis in Paris, France. She is a member of the scientific council for GELA (Groupe d'Etude des Lymphomes de l'Adulte).

creators.name: Dr. Wayne C. Levy
creators.description: Wayne C. Levy, MD, is a professor of medicine and cardiology at the University of Washington in Seattle. He is also the medical director of the university’s Regional Heart Center Cardiology Clinic and the program director of the Advanced Heart Failure/Transplant Cardiology Fellowship. Dr. Levy’s primary research is focused on risk modeling in heart failure, identifying patients who may derive greater benefit from implantable cardioverter-defibrillators, and identifying patients and timing for left ventricular assist device implantation.

creators.name: Dr. John S. Fordtran
creators.description: John S. Fordtran, MD, is the director of gastrointestinal physiology at Baylor University Medical Center (BUMC), Texas. Previously, he was chief of internal medicine at BUMC and president of the Baylor Research Institute. Dr. Fordtran is an accomplished author of over 180 peer-reviewed articles on gastrointestinal pathophysiology, diagnosis and management and won the Janssen Award in Gastroenterology for Lifetime Achievement in Digestive Sciences.

creators.name: Dr. Mark P. Callery
creators.description: Mark P. Callery, FACS, MD, is a professor of surgery at Harvard Medical School in Boston, MA. He is also the chief of general and gastrointestinal surgery at the Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center. Dr. Callery’s primary research is focused on clinical outcomes in pancreaticobiliary surgery.

creators.name: Dr. Masamichi Yokoe
creators.description: Masamichi Yokoe, MD, is a physician in the internal medicine department at Nagoya Daini Red Cross Hospital in Honshu, Japan. Dr. Yokoe's primary research is focused on management of acute cholangitis and cholecystitis.

creators.name: Dr. Rashmikant Kothari
creators.description: Rashmikant Kothari, MD, is an associate professor of emergency medicine and clerkship director at Western Michigan University. He is currently the chair of the Stroke Task Force of the American Heart Association National ACLS Subcommittee and is on the scientific advisory board of Neuron Therapeutics, Inc. His research interests include emergency response to acute stroke.

creators.name: Dr. Richard F. Harvey
creators.description: Richard F. Harvey, MD, is a consultant gastroenterologist at Frenchay Hospital in Bristol, UK. He is also the principal investigator of the Bristol Helicobacter Project. Dr. Harvey’s research focuses primarily on duodenal ulcer epidemiology and helicobacter eradication, and he is best known in the literature as co-creator of the Harvey-Bradshaw Index.

creators.name: Dr. Rick Body
creators.description: Rick Body, MB ChB, MRCSEd(A&E), FRCEM, PhD, is an emergency medicine professor and honorary consultant in emergency medicine at the University of Manchester in UK. He is also the founder of the Manchester Acute Coronary Syndromes (MACS) Academic Group and the Manchester Emergency Medicine and Intensive Care Research Group (EMERGING). Dr. Body’s primary research is focused on early diagnosis of acute coronary syndromes.

creators.name: Dr. Stephen Smith
creators.description: Stephen W. Smith, MD, is an emergency physician at Hennepin County Medical Center (HCMC) in Minneapolis. He is also a professor of emergency medicine at the University of Minnesota School of Medicine and runs Dr. Smith's ECG Blog . Dr. Smith's research focuses include ECG and troponin in acute myocardial infarction and health issues related to gamma hydroxybutyrate (GHB).

creators.name: Dr. Thomas J. Sitzman
creators.description: Thomas J. Sitzman, MD, MPH, is a pediatric plastic surgeon specializing in cleft lip, palate, and hand surgeries. He leads National Institutes of Health-funded research aimed at improving outcomes for cleft lip and palate surgery and provides evidence-based care tailored to meet patient and family goals. Dr. Sitzman is a dedicated clinician and researcher, driven by his passion for helping children reach their fullest potential through transformative surgeries.

creators.name: Dr. Michael A. Kass
creators.description: Michael A. Kass, MD, is a professor of ophthalmology and chairman of the Department of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences at Washington University in St. Louis. He is also the director of the Heed Ophthalmic Foundation. Dr. Kass’ primary research is focused on glaucoma, ocular hypertension, and esotropia.

creators.name: Dr. Nancy Bergstrom
creators.description: Nancy Bergstrom, PhD, RN, FAAN, is a retired associate dean of research at UTHealth School of Nursing and director of the Center on Aging at the University of Texas Health Science Center. She was also inducted into the Nursing Research Hall of Fame. Dr. Bergstrom’s research was focused primarily on pressure ulcer reduction.

creators.name: Dr. Per Bech
creators.description: Per Bech, MD, trained in psychiatry at the University of Copenhagen. He is an active lecturer and researcher in psychiatry and psychometrics. He was recently appointed Professor of Applied Psychometrics at the University of Copenhagen. He has won many awards both within Denmark and abroad for his research and prowess within the field.

creators.name: Dr. Phyo Kyaw Myint
creators.description: Phyo Kyaw Myint, MBBS, MD, FRCP, is the clinical chair in old age medicine at the University of Aberdeen. He is also on the Council of the Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network (SIGN) and a member of the NIHR Dementias Clinical Studies Portfolio Development Group. Dr. Myint’s research interests include cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases, physical and mental aging, and clinical geriatrics.

creators.name: Dr. Roger R. Williams
creators.description: Roger R. Williams, MD, (d. 1998) was a professor of internal medicine at the University of Utah School of Medicine. He was the founder and director of the University of Utah Cardiovascular Genetics Research Clinic. Williams was an active researcher helping develop effective tools for evaluating and helping families with strong familial predisposition to early coronary disease, stroke, hypertension, diabetes, breast cancer and morbid obesity

creators.name: Dr. Samer A. M. Nashef
creators.description: Samer A. M. Nashef, MB ChB, FRCS, PhD, is a cardiothoracic surgeon at the Papworth Hospital in Cambridge, UK. Dr. Nashef’s primary research is focused on atrial fibrillation and risk stratification in cardiac surgery.

creators.name: Dr. Steven D. Wexner
creators.description: Steven D. Wexner, MD, PhD (Honorary) FACS, FRCS, is the chairman of the department of colorectal surgery and the director of the Digestive Disease Center at Cleveland Clinic Florida. He also led the development of the American College of Surgeons Commission on Cancer National Accreditation Program for Rectal Cancer (NAPRC). Dr. Wexner’s primary research is focused on laparoscopic and robotic colorectal surgery, surgical oncology, and inflammatory bowel disease.

creators.name: Dr. Stuart Pocock
creators.description: Stuart Pocock, PhD, is a professor of medical statistics at the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine. Dr. Pocock is a director of multiple research groups investigating epidemiology and pharmacoepidemiology. He has published many papers on major trials he has conducted, especially in cardiovascular disease.

creators.name: Dr. Terry Klassen
creators.description: Terry Klassen, MD, is the CEO and Scientific Director for the Children’s Hospital Research Institute of Manitoba. He is also head of the Department of Pediatrics and Child Health and scientific director of the George and Fay Yee Centre for Healthcare Innovation at the University of Manitoba. Dr. Klassen co-founded StaR Child Health to improve child-focused randomized control trial design, implementation and publication.

creators.name: Dr. Matthew A. Borgman
creators.description: Matthew A. Borgman, MD, is a pediatric critical care physician at the Brooke Army Medical Center, Fort Sam Houston. He was previously an assistant professor in the pediatrics department at the Uniformed Services University of the Health Sciences. Dr. Borgman's research interests include pediatric trauma and trauma resuscitation simulation.

creators.name: Dr. Micelle J. Haydel
creators.description: Micelle J. Haydel, MD, is the residency director of emergency medicine and associate professor of clinical medicine at Louisiana State University Health Sciences Center. She began her career in medicine as a nurse, completing her training at LSU School of Nursing and then later attended Tulane School of Medicine for her medical degree. Dr. Haydel currently researches head and facial injury/trauma.

creators.name: Dr. Rachel Meyers
creators.description: Rachel S. Meyers, PharmD, is a clinical assistant professor in the Department of Pharmacy Practice and Administration at Rutgers University. She also practices pediatrics and pediatric critical care at Saint Barnabas Medical Center in New Jersey. Dr. Meyers' research focuses on pediatric infectious disease, hypertension and outpatient pharmaceutical care.

creators.name: Dr. Kevin R. Murphy
creators.description: Kevin R. Murphy, MD, is an allergist and immunologist affiliated with the Boys Town National Research Hospital in Nebraska. He is actively involved in developing medical response protocols for allergy and asthma reactions in local and state-wide school systems. Dr. Murphy’s primary research is focused on allergy, asthma, and pulmonology.

creators.name: Dr. David Thaler
creators.description: David Thaler, MD, PhD is neurologist-in-chief at Tufts Medical Center and chairman of the Department of Neurology at Tufts University School of Medicine. He directed the Comprehensive Stroke Center at Tufts Medical Center from 1998 to 2017. His clinical and research interests include stroke in the young and patent foramen ovale.

creators.name: Dr. Rupert Fincke
creators.description: Rupert Fincke, MD, is a cardiologist at Northern Light Health in Bangor, ME. Dr. Fincke’s primary research is focused on interventional cardiology.

creators.name: Dr. Robert A. Kyle
creators.description: Robert A. Kyle, MD, is a professor of medicine and laboratory medicine and pathology at the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota. He is widely regarded as a pioneer in multiple myeloma research, having published numerous critical papers on topics including monoclonal gammopathies, multiple myeloma, amyloidosis, and macroglobulinemia.

creators.name: Dr. Robert J. Motzer
creators.description: Robert J. Motzer, MD, is a medical oncologist at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center. He received the Career Development Award from the National Institutes of Health and the Schonfeld Award from the Kidney Cancer Association . Dr. Motzer’s research focuses on renal cell carcinoma, germ-cell tumors, and bone marrow and blood cell transplantation.

creators.name: Ms. Janet Elizabeth Sansoni
creators.description: Janet Elizabeth Sansoni, BA, MSc, is a neuropsychologist and clinical psychologist at the University of Wollongong, Australia. Her primary areas of research are psychometrics and measurements for cognitive impairment.

creators.name: Poorana Priya
creators.description: Poorana Priya is a postgraduate pathologist practicing in India at Sree Balaji Medical College & Hospital.

creators.name: Dr. W. Ray Kim
creators.description: W. Ray Kim, MD, is Professor of Medicine at Mayo Clinic College of Medicine and Science and Founding Director of the Center for Policy and Outcomes Research in Transplantation (CPORT). He formerly studied in Seoul, South Korea, and completed fellowships in gastroenterology and hepatology at the Mayo Clinic. He has served as Chief of GI at Stanford University School of Medicine and President of AASLD. His research expertise is in disease prognostication in liver disease, as exemplified in the Model for Endstage Liver Disease (MELD).

creators.name: Dr. John C. Marshall
creators.description: John C. Marshall, MD, FRCSC, FACS, FCAHS, is a professor of surgery at the University of Toronto. He is also affiliated with St. Michael’s Hospital in Toronto as a trauma surgeon, intensivist, and co-director of the Critical Illness and Injury Research Centre. Dr. Marshall's primary research interests include sepsis, trauma, and nosocomial infections.

creators.name: Dr. Paul W. Sperduto
creators.description: Paul W. Sperduto, MD, is a radiation oncologist in Waconia, MN and is affiliated with multiple hospitals in the area. He is also the director of Minneapolis Radiation Oncology at MRO Ridgeview Regional Therapy Center in Waconia. Dr. Sperduto’s primary research is focused on radiation therapy and radiation oncology technology.

creators.name: Dr. Martine Extermann
creators.description: Martine Extermann, MD, is a professor of oncology and medicine at the University of South Florida and program leader in the senior adult oncology program at Moffitt Cancer Center in Tampa, Florida. She has been presented with the B.J. Kennedy Award for Scientific Excellence in Geriatric Oncology from the American Society of Clinical Oncology in 2009. Dr. Extermann’s primary research is focused on cancer in older patients.

creators.name: Dr. Mark I. Neuman
creators.description: Mark Neuman, MD, MPH is an associate professor of pediatrics and emergency medicine at Harvard Medical School. He also works in the emergency department at Boston Children’s Hospital. Dr. Neuman’s primary research is focused on identifying the optimal diagnostic strategy for the identification of pediatric pneumonia, with the goal of reducing radiography and targeted antibiotic treatment for children with bacterial pneumonia.

creators.name: Dr. Pierre Amarenco
creators.description: Pierre Amarenco, MD, is a professor of neurology at Paris-Diderot Sorbonne University in Paris, France. He is also the chairman of the department of neurology and stroke center at the Bichat University Hospital in Paris, France. Dr. Amarenco's primary research is focused on prognosis and treatment of stroke.

creators.name: Dr. Rhett M. Schiffman
creators.description: Rhett M. Schiffman, MD, MS, MHSA, is an associate clinical professor of ophthalmology at the University of California, Irvine. He is also president and CEO of Vision Ophthalmic Development International. Dr. Schiffman’s research focuses primarily on glaucoma treatment.

creators.name: Dr. Robert Uzzo
creators.description: Robert Uzzo, MD, is chair of surgical oncology at Fox Chase Cancer Center in Philadephia and professor of surgery at Temple University Health System. His clinical interests include minimally invasive urological oncology and renal malignancies. Dr. Uzzo has has authored over 300 peer-reviewed articles and chapters that have been cited over 3,500 times.

creators.name: Dr. Stamatis P. Efstathiou
creators.description: Stamatis P. Efstathiou, MD, PhD, is an internal medicine physician in private practice and senior consultant at the Center for the Prevention of Cardiovascular Diseases of Hygeias Melathron, in Athens. He has been co-investigator on five clinical trials and has published 40 papers. Dr. Efstathiou's research interests include hypertension and prediction models, and he has received the Alberto Ferrari Award from the European Society of Hypertension for his work.

creators.name: Dr. Richard B. Lipton
creators.description: Richard B. Lipton, MD, is a professor of neurology, psychiatry and behavioral sciences, and epidemiology and population health at the Albert Einstein College of Medicine in New York. He is also the director of the Montefiore Headache Center and was the president of the American Headache Society from 2000-2002. Dr. Lipton’s primary research is focused on headache disorders, Alzheimer's disease, and other cognitive degenerative disorders.

creators.name: Dr. Caroline Mariano
creators.description: Caroline Mariano, MD, is a clinical assistant professor at Royal Columbian Hospital in British Columbia, Canada. She was a speaker at the Canadian Association of Medical Oncologists (CAMO) Annual Scientific Meeting in 2015. Dr. Mariano’s primary research is focused on geriatric and medical oncology.

creators.name: OTHER
creators.description: Other creator.

creators.name: Dr. Susan J. Tofte
creators.description: Susan J. Tofte, DNP, MS, is an assistant professor of dermatology at the Oregon Health & Science University School of Medicine in Portland, Oregon and a nurse practitioner specializing in dermatology. She is also affiliated with the OHSU Intercultural Psychiatric Program. Dr. Tofte’s primary research is focused on atopic dermatitis.

creators.name: Dr. Rogier Heide
creators.description: Rogier Heide, MD, PhD, is a dermatologist in the Department of Dermatology and Venereology at Erasmus MC, University Medical Center-Sophia Children’s Hospital in Rotterdam, and a consultant dermatologist at ACIBADEM International Medical Center. He has led and coauthored multiple influential studies and consensus papers on childhood mastocytosis, cutaneous mastocytosis scoring, and management protocols.

creators.name: Dr. Shuhan He
creators.description: Shuhan He, MD, is a professor of medicine at Harvard Medical School, as well as the director of growth for the Center for Innovation in Digital HealthCare at Massachusetts General Hospital. He is also an attending physician at the hospital’s emergency department and a member of the lab of computer science. Dr. He’s primary research is focused on the use of technology to solve problems in the healthcare system.

creators.name: Dr. Simon P. L. Travis
creators.description: Simon P. L. Travis, MD, is a professor of clinical gastroenterology at the University of Oxford in England. He was the president of the European Crohn’s and Colitis Organization (ECCO) and is an elected member of the International Organization of Inflammatory Bowel Disease. Dr. Travis’s primary research is focused on novel therapy, endoscopic assessment, and clinical prediction in inflammatory bowel disease.

creators.name: Dr. Paul E. Wischmeyer
creators.description: Paul E. Wischmeyer, MD, EDIC, FCCM, FASPEN, is a tenured professor of anesthesiology and surgery at Duke University School of Medicine. Dr. Wischmeyer is an internationally recognized researcher focused on perioperative and critical care nutrition, recovery after surgery and critical illness, and strategies to optimize patient outcomes.

creators.name: Dr. Pearl W. Chang
creators.description: Pearl W. Chang, MD, is a pediatrics specialist, currently practicing at Seattle Children’s Hospital in Washington. She graduated with honors from Stanford University School of Medicine in 2011. Dr. Chang’s primary research is focused on urinary tract infections and neonatal jaundice.

creators.name: Dr. Jason B. Hack
creators.description: Jason B Hack, MD is currently a professor of emergency medicine, Chief, Division of Medical Toxicology, Vice Chair of Research at East Carolina University, in Greenville, NC. He was awarded the University Emergency Medicine Foundation’s (UEMF) Mid-Career Academic Development Award for development and investigation of a novel alcohol intoxication assessment tool. Dr. Hack’s primary research is focused on alcohol intoxication and withdrawal, drug abuse, innovative approaches towards clinical issues, and medicinal and poisonous plants.

creators.name: Dr. Kevin M. Sherin
creators.description: Kevin M. Sherin, MD, is a clinical professor of family medicine at Florida State University College of Medicine in Orlando, FL. He was aware the American College of Preventive Medicine Distinguished Service Award in Chicago in 2018. Dr. Sherin’s primary research is focused on preventive healthcare and family medicine.

creators.name: Dr. Kanti R. Rai
creators.description: Kanti R. Rai, MD, is a principal investigator and professor at The Feinstein Institute for Medical Research in Manhasset, New York. He is also chief of the Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia Research and Treatment Program at the North Shore-LIJ Cancer Institute. His primary research is focused on clinical leukemia and molecular therapy.

creators.name: Dr. Jorge A. Aldrete
creators.description: Jorge A. Aldrete, MD, MS, (d. 2025) was an anesthesiologist and associate professor at the University of Colorado School of Medicine. Over his career, he published more than 480 articles and abstracts in medical journals and contributed 80 chapters to textbooks. Dr. Aldrete’s work in anesthesiology and pain management was considered groundbreaking and his contributions have had a lasting impact on perioperative care worldwide.

creators.name: Dr. Judith B. Brown
creators.description: Judith B. Brown, PhD, is a professor in the Centre for Studies in Family Medicine at the Schulich School of Medicine and Dentistry at Western University in London, Ontario. She was made an honorary member of the College of Family Physicians of Canada in 1996 and was a co-recipient of the organization’s Best Original Research Article Award in 2009. Dr. Brown’s primary research is focused on patient-centered care and health system change.

creators.name: Dr. Judith McFarlane
creators.description: Judith McFarlane, DrPH, RN, is a professor of nursing at Texas Woman’s University in Houston, TX. She also works with UNICEF in Zimbabwe to measure the impact of micro-finance and was selected as a consultant for a gender based violence prevention initiative in Africa and Asia. Dr. McFarlane’s primary research is focused on the health effects of violence against women and children and the effectiveness of interventions to prevent further violence.

creators.name: Dr. Hardip Sohal
creators.description: Hardip Sohal, MD, is a psychiatrist at the Department of Psychiatry at Fortis Hospital in Mohali, Punjab, India, which he established in 2001. He is credited with a vast study on the alcohol opiate dependent population and has given multiple lectures on the topic. Dr. Sohal’s primary research is focused on diagnosis and treatment of mental disorders in adults, adolescents, and children.

creators.name: Dr. Morton Bosniak
creators.description: Morton Bosniak, M.D., (d. 2016) was a professor of radiology at New York University Langone School of Medicine. He was the founder of NYU Langone’s abdominal imaging section and established a yearly radiology course. Dr. Bosniak’s primary research focused on visceral angiography.

creators.name: Dr. Susan Lipsett
creators.description: Susan Lipsett, MD is an assistant professor of pediatrics and emergency medicine at Harvard Medical School. She also works in the emergency department at Boston Children’s Hospital. Dr. Lipsett’s primary research is focused on identifying the optimal diagnostic strategy for the identification of pediatric pneumonia, with the goal of reducing radiography and targeted antibiotic treatment for children with bacterial pneumonia.

creators.name: Dr. Carine A. Bellera
creators.description: Carine A. Bellera, PhD, is a senior biostatistician at the Institute Bergonié in Bordeaux, France. She is a part of EUropean CLInical Trials Platform & Development (EUCLID) and SIRIC-BRIO, Bordeaux’s integrated cancer research site. Dr. Bellera’s primary research is focused on geriatric oncology.

creators.name: Dr. Stanley R. Kay
creators.description: Stanley R. Kay, PhD, (d. 1990) was a research psychologist at the Albert Einstein College of Medicine in the Bronx, New York. He was chief of the schizophrenia research program in the Department of Psychiatry at the medical school and director of physiological research at the Bronx Psychiatric Center. Dr. Kay’s primary research focused on schizophrenia with special emphasis on phenomenological and therapeutic studies.

creators.name: Dr. Abid D. Khan
creators.description: Abid D. Khan, MD, is a general surgeon and intensive care medicine doctor in Colorado Springs, Colorado. He is a participant in the Medicare Physician Quality Reporting System (PQRS) Incentive Program and is committed to heart health through the Million Hearts initiative. Dr. Khan’s primary research is focused on trauma and critical care.

creators.name: Dr. Sharon M. Watanabe
creators.description: Sharon M. Watanabe, MD, is a professor of oncology at the University of Alberta in Canada. She is also the Director of the Department of Symptom Control and Palliative Care at the Cross Cancer Institute and of the Division of Palliative Care Medicine in the university’s Department of Oncology. Dr. Watanabe’s primary research is focused on palliative care for cancer patients.

creators.name: Dr. Richard A.C. Hughes
creators.description: Richard A.C. Hughes, MD, is an emeritus professor of neurology at King’s College London and a visiting professor of neurology at University College London. He was awarded the Fellowship of the Academy of Medical Sciences in 2000 and the Medal of the Association of British Neurologists in 2006. Dr. Hughes’s primary research is focused on the pathogenesis and treatment of Guillain-Barré syndrome, chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy, and systematic reviews of treatment for neuromuscular disease.

creators.name: Dr. Stephen F. Butler
creators.description: Stephen F. Butler, PhD, is a psychologist currently practicing in Amherst, NH. Dr. Butler’s primary research is focused on prescription opioid misuse.

creators.name: Dr. Mark H. Wener
creators.description: Mark H. Wener, MD, is a professor of laboratory medicine and administration at the University of Washington School of Medicine. He is also the co-director of the university’s scleroderma clinic and director of immunology at the university’s medical centers. Dr. Wener’s primary research is focused on autoimmune rheumatic diseases with complex and unusual manifestations.

creators.name: Utah Department of Health
creators.description: The Utah Department of Health works closely with 13 local health departments and numerous community partners across the state of Utah to ensure access to health care. With over 1100 employees, the department of health is instrumental in managing the Covid-19 pandemic across the state, promoting healthy living, and ensuring health equity.
