The department created the Covid-19 Risk Score that enables clinicians to determine eligibility for Covid-19 therapeutic treatments.

creators.name: Dr. William A. Grobman
creators.description: William A. Grobman, MD, is a professor of obstetrics and gynecology at The Ohio State College of Medicine and the vice chair of clinical operations for the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology. He is an elected member of the National Academy of Medicine and previously served on the faculty of Northwestern University’s Feinberg School of Medicine. Dr. Grobman’s primary research is focused on predicting and preventing adverse obstetric outcomes.

creators.name: Dr. Nassr Nama
creators.description: Nassr Nama, MD, MSc, FRCPC, FAAP is a Clinical Assistant Professor of Pediatrics in the Division of General Pediatrics at British Columbia Children’s Hospital and the University of British Columbia. He is a pediatric hospitalist with research interests focused on improving care for hospitalized children, particularly by expediting evidence synthesis and providing risk stratification tools that allow physicians to safely allocate precious clinical resources to high-risk patients.

creators.name: Dr. Matt Hall
creators.description: Matt Hall , PhD is a principal biostatistician affiliated with the Children’s Hospital Association (CHA) and the Director of their Health Services Research Academy and Children’s Hospitals Institute of Pediatric Research (CHIPR) SM . He provides statistical support to all CHA divisions with a particular focus on health services and policy research. His statistical interests lie in multi- level modeling, nonparametric statistics, and graphical representations of large datasets. He has co-authored over 300 papers in peer-reviewed medical journals and is on the editorial board for Hospital Pediatrics. He is an ex officio board member of Pediatric Research in Inpatient Settings (PRIS) and is the research mentor for faculty members in the Division of Hospital Medicine at Children’s Mercy Hospital in Kansas City, MO.

creators.name: Dr. Ching-Piao Chien
creators.description: Ching-Piao Chien, MD, was a professor in the Department of Psychiatry at Albany Medical College in Albany, New York. He played a key role in the founding of the Pacific Rim College of Psychiatrists in 1980. Dr. Chein’s primary research was focused on tardive dyskinesia.

creators.name: Dr. Johan Bjureberg
creators.description: Johan Bjureberg, PhD, is an assistant professor in the Department of Clinical Neuroscience at the Karolinska Institutet in Stockholm, Sweden. He was nominated for the Outstanding Young Research in Psychology Award in 2020. Dr. Bjureberg’s primary research is focused on maladaptive behaviors and their underlying mechanisms from a psychotherapeutic and epidemiological perspective.

creators.name: Dr. Habib Dakik
creators.description: Habib Dakik, MD, FACC, is a tenured professor of medicine and chief of cardiology at the American University of Beirut Medical Center, Lebanon. He is board certified in cardiology and interventional cardiology, is a fellow of the American College of Cardiology, and has received numerous international awards in recognition of his excellence in clinical research. Dr. Dakik’s primary research is focused on the risk stratification of patients with acute coronary syndromes and the development of new risk indices for the preoperative evaluation of patients undergoing noncardiac surgery.

creators.name: Rachel H. Swift
creators.description: Rachel H. Swift is an academic researcher in Pfzier's g lobal research and development department.

creators.name: Dr. Daniel Turner
creators.description: Daniel Turner, MD, PhD, is an associate professor of pediatrics at the The Hebrew University of Jerusalem and the head of the Pediatric Gastroenterology and Nutrition Unit at Shaare Zedek Medical Center. He is also a visiting professor at Mount Sinai Hospital and the University of Toronto. Dr. Turner’s research interests include Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, and other pediatric inflammatory bowel diseases.

creators.name: Dr. Anastasia Miron
creators.description: Anastasia Miron, MD, is associated with the The Hospital for Sick Children in Toronto, Ontario.

creators.name: Dr. Henry Burch
creators.description: Henry Burch, MD, is an endocrinologist at the National Naval Medical Center in Bethesda, Maryland. He is one of two doctors at National Naval Medical Center who specialize in Endocrinology, Diabetes & Metabolism. His research interests include diagnosis and treatment of thyroid disorders.

creators.name: Dr. Lei Chen
creators.description: Lei Chen, MBBS, MMed, MD, PhD, is an endocrinologist and researcher. Her Ph.D is in epidemiology and she has over 15 years of experience in epidemiological and clinical studies in obesity, diabetes and co-morbidities.

creators.name: Dr. Carolina A.M. Schurink
creators.description: Carolina A.M. Schurink, MD, is a professor of medicine and practicing physician at the Erasmus University Medical Center in Rotterdam, Netherlands.

creators.name: Dr. Eric J. Lavonas
creators.description: Eric J. Lavonas, MD, is a practicing emergency physician and medical toxicologist. He is a professor of emergency medicine at the University of Colorado School of Medicine, and has served as the interim director of the emergency department at Denver Health. His research interests include envenomation and antidote development, carbon monoxide poisoning, and health care quality.

creators.name: Dr. Louis S. Fridericia
creators.description: Louis S. Fridericia, MD, (d. 1947) was a professor of hygiene at the Hygienic Institute of the University of Copenhagen in Denmark. He was also the president of the Medical Society of Copenhagen. Dr. Fridericia’s primary research was focused on duration of systole in an electrocardiogram in heart disease.

creators.name: Dr. Brian Schonewald
creators.description: Brian Schonewald, MD, is a chief internal medicine resident at Sidney Kimmel Medical College at Thomas Jefferson University. His professional interests revolve around medical education, point-of-care ultrasound, and global health.

creators.name: Dr. Paul Angulo
creators.description: Paul Angulo, MD, (d. 2015) was a professor of medicine at the University of Kentucky after spending 12 years at the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota, where he worked as associate professor of medicine. He specialized in general hepatology, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, cholestatic liver disease, and autoimmune hepatitis. Dr. Angulo was on the editorial board of numerous medical journals and has authored more than 240 articles, abstracts, book reviews, and editorials.

creators.name: Dr. Marlene Dominguez
creators.description: Marlene Dominguez, MD, is a physician in the hepatology department at the Hospital Clinic of Barcelona and a researcher at the August Pi i Sunyer Biomedical Research Institute in Barcelona, Spain. Dr. Dominguez's primary research is focused on prognosis of alcoholic hepatitis.

creators.name: Dr. Matthew R. Cooperberg
creators.description: Matthew R. Cooperberg, MD, MPH, is an associate professor of urology and epidemiology/biostatistics at UCSF. He practices on the urologic oncology team of the UCSF Helen Diller Family Comprehensive Cancer Center, Mount Zion Medical Center and also operates at San Francisco General Hospital. Dr. Cooperberg researches primarily prostate cancer with a focus on effectiveness of emerging biomarkers on diagnosis and risk assessment, and relative benefits of treatment strategies on cost effectiveness and quality of life.

creators.name: Dr. Philip J. Johnson
creators.description: Philip J. Johnson, MD, FRCP, is a professor in translational oncology at the University of Liverpool. He is also the deputy director of the North West Cancer Research Centre, University of Liverpool. Dr. Johnson’s primary research is focused on diagnosis and prognosis of hepatobiliary and pancreatic cancer.

creators.name: Dr. Rebecca N. Ichord
creators.description: Rebecca N. Ichord, MD, is a professor of neurology and an attending neurologist at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia in Pennsylvania. She is also the director of the Pediatric Stroke Fellowship Program and section chief of the ICU Neurology Consultation Service at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia. Dr. Ichord’s primary research is focused on pediatric cardiac arrest and stroke.

creators.name: Dr. Stuart Montgomery
creators.description: Stuart Montgomery, BSC, MD, FRC Psych, is a retired psychiatrist. He was an emeritus professor of psychiatry at London University School of Medicine and served as president of the European College of Neuropsychopharmacology and the British Association of Psychopharmacology. Dr. Montgomery's research interests include depression, anxiety disorders, schizophrenia, and bipolar disorder.

creators.name: Dr. William C. Dement
creators.description: William C. Dement, MD, PhD, is a professor of psychiatry and behavioral sciences at the Stanford University School of Medicine. He is also the chief of the Stanford University Division of Sleep. Dr. Dement’s research interests include sleep disorders, REM, and the neurochemistry of sleep.

creators.name: Dr. Kristen M. Sanfilippo
creators.description: Kristen M. Sanfilippo, MD, MPHS, is an associate professor in the department of hematology at the Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis. She is also a member of the Hemostasis and Thrombosis Research Society, the International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis, and the American Society of Hematology. Dr. Sanfilippo’s primary research is focused on venous thromboembolism, cancer-associated thrombosis, and anticoagulant-related bleeding.

creators.name: Dr. Khalid Mumtaz
creators.description: Khalid Mumtaz, MBBS, is a hepatologist and gastroenterologist at the Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center. He is also an associate professor of medicine at the Ohio State University. Dr. Mumtaz's primary research is focused on hepatitis, cirrhosis, and fatty liver disease.

creators.name: Dr. Man S. Oh
creators.description: Man S. Oh, MD, is a professor of medicine and the director of fluid and electrolytes in the Department of Nephrology at SUNY Downstate Medical Center.

creators.name: Dr. Mark D. Miller
creators.description: Mark D. Miller, MD, is a professor of psychiatry at the University of Pittsburgh. He is also the medical director of the Late-Life Depression Program. Dr. Miller’s research interests include pyschiatric and psychotherapeutic approaches in geriatric medicine.

creators.name: SCORE2 Working Group
creators.description: In collaboration with the European Society of Cardiology, the SCORE2 Working Group developed SCORE2 and SCORE2-OP, two models to estimate 10-year risk of cardiovascular disease in Europe.

creators.name: Dr. Rebecca K. Grant
creators.description: Rebecca Grant, MBChB, BSc (Hons), MA (Hons), MSc currently works as a clinical fellow in gastroenterology in NHS Lothian (Western General Hospital, Edinburgh and the Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh), Scotland. Her research interests include quality improvement in upper GI endoscopy, capsule endoscopy, and inflammatory bowel disease.

creators.name: Dr. Loretta P. Finnegan
creators.description: Loretta P. Finnegan, MD, is the executive officer of the College on Problems of Drug Dependence in Philadelphia, PA. She is also the president of Finnegan Consulting. Dr. Finnegan's primary research is focused on women's health and perinatal addiction.

creators.name: Dr. Richard Sterling
creators.description: Richard K. Sterling, MD, is a professor and the chief of hepatology at Virginia Commonwealth University. His research interests include liver transplantation, HIV-HCV coinfection, acute and chronic liver disease, viral hepatitis C and B, and other hepatic pathologies.

creators.name: Dr. Ron Dagan
creators.description: Ron Dagan, MD, is a distinguished professor of pediatrics and infectious diseases at the Ben-Gurion University of the Negev in Beer-Sheva, Israel. He also created the pediatric infectious disease unit at the Soroka University Medical Center, where he was director until 2014. Dr. Dagan is an active researcher, primarily focusing on new conjugate vaccines, epidemiology of vaccine-preventable diseases, and other infectious disease topics.

creators.name: Dr. Srikant Rangaraju
creators.description: Srikant Rangaraju, MBBS, MSc is a board certified neurologist with specialty training in vascular neurology. His clinical research focuses on accurate prognostication of patient outcomes after ischemic stroke especially in those with large vessel occlusion. Dr. Rangaraju also runs a basic science lab that studies microglia mediated neuroinflammation within the brain after stroke and in neurodegenerative diseases. He works clinically at Emory University Hospital and Grady Memorial Hospital in Atlanta, Georgia.

creators.name: Dr. Toni Choueiri
creators.description: Toni Choueiri, MD, is a medical oncologist and the director of the Lank Center for Genitourinary Oncology at the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute/Brigham and Women’s Hospital in Boston, Massachusetts. He is also co-leader of the Kidney Cancer Program at Dana-Farber/Harvard Cancer Center and the Jerome and Nancy Kohlberg Professor of Medicine at Harvard Medical School. Dr. Choueiri's research interests include novel therapies and biomarkers in genitourinary malignancies.

creators.name: Dr. Torsten Fredriksson
creators.description: Torsten Fredriksson, MD, is a physician in the department of dermatology at the Karolinska Institute in Sweden. Dr. Fredriksson’s primary research is focused on topical treatments for conditions like psoriasis, dermatomycosis, and tinea versicolor.

creators.name: Dr. Waleed Alhazzani
creators.description: Waleed Alhazzani, MBBS, MSc, FRCPC, is an assistant professor in the division of critical care at McMaster University and a physician in intensive care at St. Joseph’s Healthcare Hamilton in Ontario, Canada. He is also chair of international critical care guidelines, such as the surviving sepsis campaign. Dr. Alhazzani’s primary research is focused on clinical trials for GI disorders in critically ill patients.

creators.name: Dr. Evan S. Dellon
creators.description: Evan S. Dellon, MD, MPH, is a professor of medicine and adjunct professor of epidemiology at the University of North Carolina School of Medicine in Chapel Hill. He is also the director of the UNC Center for Esophageal Diseases and Swallowing (CEDAS) and serves as an associate editor for Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology. Dr. Dellon’s primary research is focused on epidemiology, pathogenesis, diagnosis, treatment, and outcomes of eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) and eosinophilic GI diseases (EGIDs).

creators.name: Dr. Kelly Posner
creators.description: Kelly Posner, PhD, is a professor of psychiatry at the Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons at Columbia University in New York. She is also the founder and director of the Columbia Lighthouse Project. Dr. Posner’s primary research is focused on depression and suicide risk.

creators.name: Dr. Laurie H. Sehn
creators.description: Laurie H. Sehn, MD, is a medical oncologist at the British Columbia Cancer Agency and a clinical associate professor at the University of British Columbia. She is on the Board of Directors and is the director of research fellowships for the Lymphoma Foundation Canada (LFC). Dr. Sehn is an active researcher studying aspects of lymphoid cancers.

creators.name: Dr. Ronald B. Melles
creators.description: Ronald B. Melles, MD, is an ophthalmologist and researcher at Kaiser Permanente Redwood City Medical Center in Redwood City, California. Dr. Melles has published extensively on hydroxychloroquine retinopathy.

creators.name: Dr. Teresa A. Hillier
creators.description: Teresa A. Hillier, MD, MS, was a practicing endocrinologist and senior investigator at the Kaiser Permanente Center for Health Research. Her research included how modifiable risk factors earlier in life can affect future risk of endocrine diseases, including gestational diabetes, obesity, metabolic syndrome, type 2 diabetes, and osteoporosis. Dr. Hillier was also the principal investigator of the Study of Osteoporotic Fractures (SOF). She passed away in 2023.

creators.name: Dr. Sidney C. Truelove
creators.description: Sidney C. Truelove, MD, (d. 2002) was a gastroenterologist and lecturer in Oxford, UK. He founded the International Organization for the Study of Inflammatory Bowel Disease and was the first president of the British Society of Digestive Endoscopy. Dr. Truelove is best known for his research in ulcerative colitis, leading the first clinical trial in the field that demonstrated effectiveness of cortisone in ulcerative colitis.

creators.name: Dr. Romain Chopard
creators.description: Romain Chopard, MD, PhD, is a physician in the Department of Cardiology at the University Hospital Jean Minjoz in Besançon, France.

creators.name: Dr. Simon A. Mahler
creators.description: Dr. Simon A. Mahler, MD, is an associate professor of emergency medicine at Wake Forest Baptist Health in Winston-Salem, North Carolina. He is board certified in emergency medicine and is also the chief medical officer of Decision Point Informatics, LLC. Dr. Mahler’s research interests include decision support in chest pain patients presenting to the emergency department.

creators.name: Dr. Will Brindle
creators.description: Will Brindle MBChB, MPhil, BSc (Hons) is currently employed as a consultant gastroenterologist at the Department of Gastroenterology at the Victoria Hospital in Kirkcaldy, Scotland.

creators.name: Dr. Susan A. Fuhrman
creators.description: Susan A. Fuhrman, MD, is a practicing clinical and anatomic pathologist in Columbus, Ohio. She is Director of Pathology and Lab at OhioHealth Central Laboratories. Dr. Fuhrman is best known in the scientific medical community for developing the Fuhrman Nuclear Grade for Clear Cell Renal Carcinoma.

creators.name: ESC Cardiovascular Risk Collaboration
creators.description: The European Society of Cardiology (ESC) is a leading medical society in the discovery and dissemination of best practices in cardiovascular medicine. In collaboration with the SCORE2 Working Group, the ESC Cardiovascular Risk Collaboration developed SCORE2 and SCORE2-OP, two models to estimate 10-year risk of cardiovascular disease in Europe.

creators.name: Dr. Karl L. Yang
creators.description: Karl L. Yang, MD, is an associate professor clinical medicine at the Indiana University School of Medicine. He is a practicing physician in sleep medicine and pulmonary critical care. Dr. Yang's primary contributions to the medical literature have been in optimal management of mechanical ventilation.

creators.name: Dr. Laurence Fardet
creators.description: Laurence Fardet, MD, PhD, is a professor at Paris XII University in France. She is also a practicing physician at the Henri Mondor University Hospital in Paris, France. Dr. Fardet’s research focuses primarily on the epidemiologic use of glucocorticoids in the general population.

creators.name: Dr. Nedim Yücel
creators.description: Nedim Yücel, MD, is a professor and practicing physician in the Department of Trauma and Orthopedic Surgery at the University of Witten/Herdecke and Cologne Merheim Medical Center in Germany.

creators.name: Dr. Thomas N. Tozer
creators.description: Thomas N. Tozer, PhD, PharmD, BS, is professor emeritus of biopharmaceutical sciences and pharmaceutical chemistry at School of Pharmacy at UCSF. He is the co-author of Clinical Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics: Concepts and Applications . Prior to retirement, Dr. Tozer researched colon-specific drug delivery, toxicokinetics, kinetics of potential contrast agents for magnetic resonance imaging and nonlinear pharmacokinetics.

creators.name: Dr. Melvin L. Selzer
creators.description: Melvin L. Selzer, MD, was on the faculty of the University of Michigan Medical School until 1978, when he joined the faculty at UC San Diego. He was also the first director of the drug and alcohol treatment programs at the University of Michigan. Dr. Selzer’s primary research was focused on alcoholism and drunk driving.

creators.name: Dr. Rinaldo Bellomo
creators.description: Rinaldo Bellomo, MBBS, MD, FRACP, is a professor of intensive care medicine at the University of Melbourne and an honorary faculty of medicine at Monash University in Australia. His work in publishing over 1,300 scientific papers has earned him over 60 national and international awards and grants. Dr. Bellomo is involved in many areas of research involving intensive care, including traumatic brain injury, sepsis, transfusion, and acute lung injury.

creators.name: Dr. Evelyn Hsu
creators.description: Evelyn Hsu, MD, is a professor of pediatrics at the University of Washington School of Medicine. She is also the division chief of pediatric gastroenterology and hepatology at Seattle Children’s. Dr. Hsu’s primary research is focused on pediatric liver transplant, childhood cholestasis, autoimmune liver disease, and viral hepatitis.

creators.name: Dr. Richard W. Light
creators.description: Richard W. Light, MD, is a professor in the Division of Allergy, Pulmonary, and Critical Care Medicine at Vanderbilt University School of Medicine. He was formerly chief of the pulmonary diseases section and associate chief of staff at the VA Hospital in Long Beach. Dr. Light is best known for his research on pleural disease for which he has published numerous papers and written in several textbooks.

creators.name: Dr. Robert W. Yeh
creators.description: Robert W. Yeh, MD, is an associate professor of medicine at Harvard Medical School. He is also director of the Richard and Susan Smith Center for Outcomes Research in Cardiology at the Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center. Dr. Yeh’s primary research interests revolve around improving the value of coronary and vascular devices and therapies in clinical practice.

creators.name: Dr. Roy Purssell
creators.description: Roy Purssell, MD, is an emergency doctor at Vancouver General Hospital and a professor in the Department of Emergency Medicine at the University of British Columbia. He is also the medical director of the BC Drug and Poison Information Centre and the president of the Canadian Association of Poison Control Centres. Dr. Purssell's areas of research include impaired driving, substance abuse, laboratory testing and adverse drug reactions.

creators.name: Dr. Stephen J. Wolf
creators.description: Stephen J. Wolf, MD, is a professor of emergency medicine at the University of Colorado School of Medicine in Denver, CO. He is also the director of service at Denver Health Emergency Medicine. Dr. Wolf’s primary research is focused on evaluation of adult patients presenting to the ED with suspected acute venous thromboembolic disease.

creators.name: Dr. Susan Baker
creators.description: Susan Baker, MPH, is an professor and epidemiologist specializing in injury prevention at Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health and was the first director of the Center for Injury Research and Policy. She is well known for authoring the Injury Fact Book. Professor Baker's teaching and research is aimed at influencing policy changes that will reduce the likelihood of injury for thousands of people.

creators.name: Dr. Gurjit K. Khurana Hershey
creators.description: Gurjit K. Khurana Hershey, MD, PhD, is a Professor of Pediatrics at Cincinnati Children’s Hospital and the Department of Pediatrics at University of Cincinnati College of Medicine. She is an allergist and immunologist and directs the Division of Asthma Research at Cincinnati Children’s Hospital Medical Center. Dr. Khurana Hershey leads several large NIH research studies in asthma, atopic dermatitis, food allergy, and allergic disorders.

creators.name: Dr. George Ntaios
creators.description: George Ntaios, MD, PhD, is an assistant professor of internal medicine at the University of Thessaly in Larissa, Greece. He is co-chair of the Guidelines Committee of the European Stroke Organization and Secretary General of the Hellenic Stroke Organization. Dr. Ntaios is an active researcher, focusing mainly on secondary stroke prevention and stroke prognosis.

creators.name: Dr. Gregory Schmidt
creators.description: Gregory Schmidt, MD, is a professor of medicine and the director of critical care medicine at the University of Iowa. He researches ICU ultrasound, sepsis therapy, ARDS, and judging the adequacy of volume replacement in patients in shock. Dr. Schmidt’s clinical interests include ECMO, septic shock, fluid management techniques, and analysis of ventilator waveforms on treatment course.

creators.name: Dr. Jean-François Payen
creators.description: Jean-François Payen, MD, PhD, is a professor of anesthesia and critical care medicine and head of the anesthesiology and critical care department at the Grenoble Alpes University Hospital in France. He is also the director of the European Committee Site of Education in Anesthesiology. Dr. Payen is an active researcher investigating traumatic brain injuries through detailed imaging and pharmacological neuroprotective mechanisms.

creators.name: Dr. S. Balasubramanian
creators.description: S. Balasubramanian, MD, is head of the Department of Pediatrics and a senior consultant at Kanchi Kamakoti CHILDS Trust Hospital in Chennai, India. Dr. Balasubramanian actively researches child asthma and child nutrition.

creators.name: Dr. Sharon K. Inouye
creators.description: Sharon K. Inouye, MD, MPH, is director of the Aging Brain Center and a professor of medicine at Harvard Medical School and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center. She received her medical degree at University of California San Francisco, and her MPH from Yale University. Her research focuses on delirium and functional decline in hospitalized older patients, resulting in more than 200 peer-reviewed original articles.

creators.name: Dr. Matthew R. Grossman
creators.description: Matthew R. Grossman, MD, is an associate professor of pediatrics at the Yale School of Medicine. He is also the quality and safety officer at the Yale New Haven Children's Hospital. Dr. Grossman’s primary research is focused on neonatal abstinence syndrome.

creators.name: Dr. Richard N. Pugh
creators.description: Richard N. Pugh, MD, was a distinguished researcher who worked for the liver unit and department of radiology at King's College Hospital and Medical School in London and was a faculty of medicine and health sciences at UAE University.

creators.name: Dr. James E. Tisdale
creators.description: James E. Tisdale, PharmD, is a researcher and professor of pharmacy specializing in cardiovascular pharmacotherapy at Purdue University in West Lafayette, IN. Dr. Tisdale’s primary research is focused on the mechanisms, risk factors, and management of drug-induced arrhythmias.

creators.name: Dr. James F. Holmes
creators.description: James F. Holmes, MD, MPH, is a professor in the department of emergency medicine at the University of California, Davis. He is the Vice Chair for Research and his research interests include pediatric trauma, head and spine trauma, and selective use of head CT. Dr. Holmes has been involved in the development of emergency medicine in several countries, including Fiji.

creators.name: Dr. Jaume Canet
creators.description: Jaume Canet, MD, PhD, is chair of the anesthesiology department at Hospital Universitari Germans Trias i Pujol in Barcelona, Spain. He is also chief investigator of the European Society of Anaesthesiology Clinical Trial Network. Dr. Canet's primary research involves postoperative risk of surgical procedures, intraoperative care, and pulmonary complications.

creators.name: Dr. Jay M. Ginsberg
creators.description: Jay M. Ginsberg, MD is a practicing nephrologist in Connecticut. Dr. Ginsberg graduated from Jefferson Medical College of Thomas Jefferson University in 1977 and has been in practice for 40 years. He completed a residency at Rhode Island Hospital and also specializes in internal medicine.

creators.name: Dr. Nadim Mahmud
creators.description: Nadim Mahmud, MD, MS, MPH, MSCE, is an assistant professor of medicine (gastroenterology), biostatistics, and epidemiology at the University of Pennsylvania. He is also a transplant hepatologist at the University of Pennsylvania and the Veterans Administration Medical Center. Dr. Mahmud is a clinical epidemiologist whose work focuses on advanced risk prediction and outcomes research to improve decision-making for patients with chronic liver disease.

creators.name: Dr. Ewen A. Griffiths
creators.description: Ewen A. Griffiths, MD, FRCS, is an upper gastrointestinal specialist at Queen Elizabeth Hospital in Birmingham, England. He is also an honorary senior clinical lecturer at the University of Birmingham. Dr. Griffiths' research focuses primarily on hypoxia-associated factors and minimally invasive general surgery procedures.

creators.name: Dr. Florence Dumas
creators.description: Florence Dumas, MD, PhD, is a professor of emergency medicine at the University of Paris in France. She is also deputy chief of the pre-hospital and in-hospital emergency department at the Cochin and Hotel Dieu Hospital and has been a researcher on the Paris Sudden Death Expertise Center research team centered on cardiac arrest research. Dr. Dumas’ primary research is focused on prognostic factors and outcome prediction for cardiac arrest patients.

creators.name: Dr. Frederick W. Endorf
creators.description: Frederick W. Endorf, MD, is a general surgeon affiliated with Hennepin County Medical Center in Minneapolis and the American Burn Association. His research interests include burns, trauma, and reconstructive surgery.

creators.name: Dr. James Forrester
creators.description: James Forrester, MD, is professor emeritus and former chief of cardiology at Cedars-Sinai Hospital. He is also a professor of medicine at the David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA. Dr. Forrester was a key participant in the development of hemodynamic monitoring using the Swan-Ganz catheter as well as studying patient outcomes.

creators.name: Dr. Jean Klastersky
creators.description: Jean Klastersky, MD, is a professor of medicine at the University of Brussels. He is also currently the chief of medicine services at the Institut Jules Bordet. Dr. Klastersky's research focuses on treatment and prognosis in neutropenic fever and novel therapies in cancer patients.

creators.name: Dr. Michael P. Stern
creators.description: Michael P. Stern, MD, is an endocrinologist in San Antonio, Texas. He is part of the division of clinical epidemiology in the department of medicine at the University of Texas Health Science Center. Dr. Stern’s research interests include diabetes and cardiovascular disease.

creators.name: Dr. Hilary A. Calvert
creators.description: Dr. Hilary A. Calvert is an oncologist and cancer drug-development researcher. He played a major role in the clinical development of carboplatin and other anticancer therapies, including pemetrexed and PARP inhibitors. He received the 2009 lifetime achievement award in the excellence in oncology awards.

creators.name: Dr. Richard Reid
creators.description: Richard Reid, MD, is a medical professional in the field of gynecology. Dr Reid’s primary research is focused on cervical screening and early detection and treatment protocols for cervical cancer and HPV.

creators.name: Dr. Karen M. Puopolo
creators.description: Karen M. Puopolo, MD, PhD, is a professor of pediatrics at the University of Pennsylvania’s Perelman School of Medicine and the medical director of newborn medicine at Pennsylvania Hospital. She received the Pennsylvania Pediatrician of the Year Award from the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) in 2022. Dr. Puopolo’s primary research is focused on quantifying the risk for neonatal infection.

creators.name: Dr. Francine Ducharme
creators.description: Francine Ducharme, MD, is a professor of pediatrics and an affiliate professor in the Department of Social and Preventive Medicine at the University of Montreal. She currently practices as a pediatrician and epidemiologist at CHU Sainte-Justine. Her research focus is on educational and drug interventions and improved pediatric respiratory guideline compliance.

creators.name: Dr. Graham Copeland
creators.description: Graham Copeland, MBBS, is a consultant general surgeon at Broadgreen Hospital in Liverpool. Graham has been an advisor to the Healthcare Commission and the National Institute of Clinical Effectiveness in the United Kingdom. Dr. Copeland's research focuses on clinical audits and outcome measures in surgical settings.

creators.name: Dr. H. Ronald Wexler
creators.description: H. Ronald Wexler, MD, FRCP(C), is a retired anesthesiologist. He practiced at the University of Western Ontario in Canada and served as the president of the Ontario Medical Association. Dr. Wexler was also an associate editor of the Medical Journal of the University of Western Ontario.

creators.name: Dr. Jacques D. Donzé
creators.description: Jacques D. Donzé, MD, MSc, is an internist at Brigham and Women's Hospital in Boston. He is also a research associate with the Harvard Clinical and Translational Science Center. Dr. Donzé’s research focuses primarily on hospital readmission and transition of care, venous thromboembolism, and antithrombotic therapy.

creators.name: Dr. Marco Ranucci
creators.description: Marco Ranucci, MD, FESC, is an anesthesiologist at IRCCS Policlinico San Donato in Milan, Italy. He is also the director of clinical research for cardiothoracic and vascular anaesthesia at the IRCCS Policlinico San Donato. Dr. Ranucci’s research interests include cardiothoracic and critical care anaesthesia.

creators.name: Dr. Martin Dolgin
creators.description: Martin Dolgin, MD, (d. 2006) was an attending physician at the Bellevue Hospital and Tisch Hospital. He also served as a member of the American College of Cardiology and American Heart Association. Dr. Dolgin’s primary research was focused on diagnosis and treatment of heart failure.

creators.name: Dr. Matthieu Schmidt
creators.description: Matthieu Schmidt, MD, PhD, is an assistant professor in Sorbonne Université and in medical intensive care at the Pitié-Salpêtrière Hospital in Paris, France. With more than 100 peer-review publications referenced in PubMed, Dr. Schmidt’s primary research is focused on extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, severe acute respiratory distress syndrome, patient-ventilator interactions, and refractory cardiogenic shock.

creators.name: Dr. Philippe Solal-Céligny
creators.description: Philippe Solal-Céligny, MD, Ph.D, is a professor and principal investigator at Laboratoire Central d’Hematologie at Centre Jean Bernard in Le Mans, France.

creators.name: Dr. R. Brian Payne
creators.description: R. Brian Payne is a retired chemical pathologist. He has published extensively in the literature on clinical biochemistry. Dr. Payne is perhaps best known for his contributions on serum calcium correction for hypoalbuminemia.

creators.name: Dr. Robert Marshall
creators.description: Robert Marshall, MD, was a physician and researcher in the department of physiology and pharmacology at the University of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia. Dr. Marshall’s primary research is focused on the physical properties of lungs and pulmonary mechanics.

creators.name: Dr. Eric J. DeMaria
creators.description: Eric J. DeMaria, MD is a chair, professor, and chief of the general and bariatric surgery department at the Brody School of Medicine, East Carolina University (ECU). Dr. DeMaria is internationally recognized for his contributions to bariatric surgery, advanced laparoscopic surgery, and minimally invasive surgery. He is a renowned researcher in the field of obesity and metabolic surgery and the author of more than 200 publications.

creators.name: Dr. Elaine Kaptein
creators.description: Elaine M. Kaptein, MD, is a professor of medicine at University of Southern California Keck School of Medicine in Los Angeles. She is a board certified endocrinologist and nephrologist and a member of the American Society of Nephrology. Dr. Kaptein’s primary research is currently focused on bedside inferior vena cava ultrasound to assess volume management in hospitalized patients.

creators.name: Dr. Michael Gossop
creators.description: Michael Gossop, PhD, is an emeritus professor of addiction and a leading researcher at the Institute of Psychiatry at King’s College London. Dr. Gossop’s primary research is focused on addiction treatment.

creators.name: Dr. Emily C. O’Brien
creators.description: Emily C. O’Brien, PhD, is an assistant professor in population health sciences and neurology at Duke University in Durham, North Carolina. She is also a researcher in the Duke Clinical Research Institute. Dr. O’Brien’s primary research is focused on outcomes in cardiovascular and pulmonary disease.

creators.name: Dr. Michelle A. Petri
creators.description: Michelle A. Petri, MD, is a professor of medicine at the Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine in Baltimore, Maryland. She is also the director of the Hopkins Lupus Center and co-director of the Hopkins Lupus Pregnancy Center. Dr. Petri’s primary research is focused on diagnosis of SLE.

creators.name: Dr. Michel Duval
creators.description: Michel Duval, MD, is the medical director of the hematopoietic transplantation and Cell Therapy Program at the Charles-Bruneau Cancer Center, at the Sainte-Justine University Hospital Center in Montreal, Canada. He is also the co-chief of the hemato-oncology department at the Centre Hospitalier Universitaire Sainte-Justine. Dr. Duval’s research focuses primarily on immunotherapy of childhood cancers and cord blood transplant immunology.

creators.name: Dr. Natalia S. Rost
creators.description: Natalia S. Rost, MD, is a professor of neurology at Harvard Medical School. She is also the chief of the stroke division at the Massachusetts General Hospital. Dr. Rost’s research interests and expertise include neuroimaging of cerebrovascular disease, genetics and genomics of stroke, and outcome prediction in patients with acute stroke.

creators.name: Dr. Paul Little
creators.description: Paul Little, MD, MBBS, is a clinical professor and practicing general clinician at the University of Southampton, UK. He was the first general practitioner to be awarded a Wellcome HSR training fellowship, and the first to be awarded an MRC Clinician Scientist Fellowship. His two main areas of research are health promotion and the management of common self-limiting illnesses.

creators.name: Dr. Tuhina Neogi
creators.description: Tuhina Neogi, MD, PhD, is an associate professor at Boston University School of Medicine. She is also affiliated with the BUSPH Department of Epidemiology. Dr. Neogi’s research focuses on epidemiology and management of various musculoskeletal/rheumatic diseases, such as osteoarthritis and gout.

creators.name: Dr. Clay C. Burlew
creators.description: Clay C. Burlew, MD, FACS, is a professor of surgery in the division of GI, trauma, and endocrine surgery at the University of Colorado School of Medicine and a trauma surgeon at Denver Health Medical Center. She directs the surgical critical care and trauma and acute care surgery fellowship programs and has been recognized for her mentorship of women in surgery. Dr. Burlew is an influential trauma and acute care surgery researcher investigating hemorrhage control, resuscitation strategies, and complex injury management.

creators.name: Dr. Mark E. Brecher
creators.description: Mark E. Brecher, MD, is a pathologist by training and was chief medical officer and senior vice president at Laboratory Corporation of America (LabCorp) until 2017. He is editor in chief of the American Association of Blood Banks Technical Manual 14th and 15th editions, one of the most cited references in blood banking and transfusion medicine. Dr. Brecher's research interests include research design and analysis, apheresis, and thrombocytopenia.

creators.name: Dr. Martin Rudwaleit
creators.description: Martin Rudwaleit, MD, is a rheumatologist at University Hospital Charité, Campus Benjamin Franklin, in Berlin, Germany. He is the principal coordinator of the German Spondyloarthritis Inception Cohort, a prospective longitudinal study on early spondyloarthritis. Dr. Rudwaleit's research interests include clinical aspects of ankylosing spondylitis and other spondyloarthritides.

creators.name: Dr. Meyer Saklad
creators.description: Meyer Saklad, MD, (d. 1979) was chief of anesthesiology at Rhode Island Hospital. He also served as part of the Unitarian Service Committee’s medical missions in Japan. Dr. Saklad’s primary research was focused on pharmacology of anesthetics, inhalation anesthesia, endotracheal anesthesia, spinal anesthesia, and oxygen therapy.

creators.name: Dr. Sidney Katz
creators.description: Sidney Katz, MD, MA, was a professor emeritus of gerontology and geriatrics at Columbia University and a co-director of the Stroud Program on the Science of Quality of Life in Aging. He was also Benjamin Rose Institute on Aging’s distinguished scholar and helped shape long-term care policy and programs focused on quality of life for older adults. Dr. Katz was an influential health services researcher investigating rehabilitation, the natural course of aging and chronic disease, long-term care, and quality of life measurement.

creators.name: Dr. Gustavo A. Ospina-Tascón
creators.description: Gustavo A. Ospina-Tascón, MD, PhD, is an internist-intensivist and professor at Universidad Icesi in Colombia. He also works in the department of intensive care at Fundación Valle del Lili and is affiliated with the translational research laboratory in critical care medicine (TransLab-CCM). Dr. Ospina-Tascón is an influential critical care researcher investigating septic shock, tissue perfusion, vasopressor timing, and hemodynamic resuscitation.

creators.name: Dr. Kenneth W. Schroeder
creators.description: Kenneth W. Schroeder, MD, is an associate professor of medicine, specifically in gastroenterology and hepatology the Mayo Clinic. Dr. Schroeder researches endoscopic diagnosis/treatment of GI diseases and inflammatory bowel disease.

creators.name: Dr. Natalia Pérez de la Ossa
creators.description: Natalia Pérez de la Ossa, MD, PhD, is a neurologist and researcher at the Germans Trias Hospital in Catalonia. Among her main research topics of interest are diagnosis through multimodal neuroimaging and neurosonology, treatment of stroke in the acute phase, and prehospital organization in the treatment of stroke.

creators.name: Dr. Nathan Shapiro
creators.description: Nathan Shapiro, MD, is an attending physician in the Department of Emergency Medicine at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center. He is also a director at the Center for Vascular Biology Research and an assistant professor at Harvard Medical School. Dr. Shapiro conducts translational and clinical research with a particular focus on endothelial cell dysfunction in sepsis.

creators.name: Dr. Patrik Michel
creators.description: Patrik Michel, MD, is a professor in the department of neurology at the University of Lausanne in Switzerland. He is chief of the Cerebrovascular Center there, which he also established. Dr. Michel is active in many professional organizations, including the European Stroke Organization and the World Stroke Organization.

creators.name: Dr. Phil Wells
creators.description: Phil Wells, MD, MSc, is a professor and chief of the Department of Medicine at The University of Ottawa. He is also on the faculty of medicine and a senior scientist at the Ottawa Hospital Research Institute. Dr. Wells researches thromboembolism, thrombophilia and long term bleeding risk in patients on anticoagulants.

creators.name: Dr. Steven Weiss
creators.description: Steven Weiss, MS, MD FACP, FACEP, is a professor of medicine at University of New Mexico. He is presently the medical director of the Critical Care Transport Team for AAS. Dr. Weiss is the creator of both the CEDOCS , NEDOCS , and the more recent PEDOCS , and he is an avid researcher in Emergency Medicine, working towards ways to improve efficiency and efficacy of ED workflow.

creators.name: Dr. Tarek Mekhail
creators.description: Tarek M. Mekhail, MD, MSc, is an associate professor of medicine at the University of Central Florida and the medical director of the Thoracic Oncology Program at the Florida Hospital Cancer Institute. Dr. Mekhail has been voted one of the Best Doctors in America in 2007-2008, 2008-2009 and 2009-2010. His research focuses on novel therapies and risk stratification in lung, kidney, and head/neck cancers.

creators.name: Dr. Thomas Cerny
creators.description: Thomas Cerny, MD, is the former chief of hematology and oncology at Kantonsspital St Gallen and also a professor of medical oncology at the University of Berne. He is president of the Swiss Cancer Foundation and Oncosuisse. Dr. Cerny researches multiple types of cancer including sarcoma and lung cancer.

creators.name: Dr. William Knaus
creators.description: William Knaus, MD, is a Professor Emeritus of The University of Virginia School of Medicine and a member of The National Academy of Medicine. Dr. Knaus is an active researcher in many areas including cancer genomics, sepsis, and outcomes of seriously ill patients.

creators.name: Dr. Nathan Kuppermann
creators.description: Nathan Kuppermann, MD, MPH, is the Executive VP, Chief Academic Officer, and Chair of Pediatrics at Children's National Hospital in Washington, DC. He chaired the first research network in pediatric emergency medicine (the Pediatric Emergency Medicine Collaborative Research Committee of the AAP) and was the founding chair of the Pediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network (PECARN). Dr. Kuppermann is a leading national investigator for studies focusing on infectious emergencies in children including the laboratory evaluation of young febrile children, the evaluation of children at risk of diabetic ketoacidosis-related cerebral injury, and the laboratory and radiographic evaluation of the pediatric trauma patient. He has been the lead or senior investigator on several research studies developing and validating clinical prediction rules.

creators.name: Dr. Paula Jiménez Fonseca
creators.description: Paula Jiménez Fonseca, MD, PhD, is a medical oncologist at the Hospital Universitario Central de Asturias in Oviedo, Spain. She has authored or co-authored dozens of studies in solid tumor oncology, particularly in the area of febrile neutropenia. Dr. Jiménez Fonseca is a member of the Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM).

creators.name: Dr. Agnieszka Młynek
creators.description: Agnieszka Młynek, MD, is a dermatologist and associate faculty member in the department of dermatology and allergy at the Charité-Universitätsmedizin Berlin in Germany. Dr. Młynek’s primary research is focused on chronic urticaria.

creators.name: Dr. Prateek K. Gupta
creators.description: Prateek K. Gupta, MD, is a vascular surgeon at Methodist University Hospital in Memphis, Tennessee. He is also an assistant professor of surgery at the University of Tennessee. Dr. Gupta's primary research is focused on surgical outcomes.

creators.name: Dr. M. J. Maxwell
creators.description: M. J. Maxwell is a clinician in the department of anaesthesia at the University of Nottingham (Queen’s Medical Centre Campus) and is affiliated with Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust. His published work centers on perioperative anaesthesia and outcomes risk prediction in the setting of hip fracture surgery.

creators.name: Dr. T. Duckett Jones
creators.description: Thomas Duckett Jones, MD, (d. 1954) was the director of research in rheumatic fever and rheumatic heart disease at the House of the Good Samaritan in Boston for 20 years. He worked clinically at Massachusetts General Hospital and was on faculty at Harvard Medical School. Dr. Jones was appointed to the inaugural National Advisory Heart Council and also served as vice-president of the American Heart Association, chairman of the AHA's Council on Rheumatic Fever, and president-elect of the National Health Council.

creators.name: Dr. William Chong
creators.description: William Chong, MD, MBBS, BSc, is a cardiothoracic surgeon at RIPAS Hospital in Bandar Seri Begawan in Brunei. He is an active researcher in his field as well as in general surgery.

creators.name: Dr. William R. Mower
creators.description: William R. Mower, MD, PhD, is a physician at the UCLA Emergency Medical Center. He is also a professor of medicine at the University of California Geffen School of Medicine. Dr. Mower’s primary research is focused on computed tomography and diagnostic radiology.

creators.name: Dr. Zeph Okeke
creators.description: Zeph Okeke, MD, is a practicing urologic surgeon, specializing in endourology, minimally invasive surgery and laparoscopy, at North Shore-LIJ Medical Group. He is also an assistant professor at Hofstra North Shore-LIJ School of Medicine and co-director of the Smith Institute for Urology endourology and laparoscopy fellowship training programs. Dr. Okeke's research interests include surgical outcomes of kidney stone patients and grading, and characterizing complex kidney stones to guide surgery.

creators.name: Dr. Ziad S. Nasreddine
creators.description: Ziad S. Nasreddine, MD, FRCP(C), is an assistant clinical professor at both McGill University and the University of Sherbrooke in Quebec, Canada. He is also director of the MoCA Clinic and Institute in Quebec. Dr. Nasreddine’s research focuses primarily on Alzheimer's and cognitive impairment diseases.

creators.name: Dr. Randi Goldman
creators.description: Dr. Randi Goldman is a reproductive health and infertility specialist at Northwell Health Fertility and the program director for the Reproductive Endocrinology and Infertility fellowship program at Northwell Health. She completed her residency training in Obstetrics and Gynecology at Brigham and Women's Hospital/Massachusetts General Hospital in 2015 and her fellowship in REI at Brigham and Women's Hospital in 2018. Dr. Goldman’s clinical and research interests span a broad range of reproductive health topics, including fertility treatment outcomes, fertility care for the LGBTQ+ community, and oncofertility/fertility preservation.

creators.name: Dr. Marc A. Probst
creators.description: Marc A. Probst, MD, MS, is an associate professor of emergency medicine and director of general emergency medicine research at Columbia University Medical Center in New York, NY. Dr. Probst’s primary research focuses on risk stratification and shared decision-making in emergency care, particularly for syncope and chest pain.

creators.name: Dr. Paul W. Jones
creators.description: Paul W. Jones, MD, PhD, is the global medical expert for the respiratory franchise at GSK. He was previously a professor of respiratory medicine and a consultant physician at St George's, University of London in London, UK. Dr. Jones’ primary research is focused on symptom measurement and cognitive outcome of COPD.

creators.name: Dr. Philip Greipp
creators.description: Philip Greipp, MD, is a professor laboratory medicine and pathology at the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota. He is practices primarily in the Hematology Department, but has a joint appointment in the Laboratory Medicine and Pathology Department. He has been a supporting author on over 100 publications in numerous peer-reviewed journals on topics ranging from cardiac enzymes to hematologic cancers and novel treatment methods.

creators.name: Dr. Victor Tapson
creators.description: Victor Tapson, MD, is a pulmonologist at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in Los Angeles. He is currently the director of the Venous Thromboembolism and Pulmonary Vascular Disease Program and the director of clinical research at the Women's Guild Lung Institute.

creators.name: Dr. William Friedewald
creators.description: William Friedewald, MD, is professor of biostatistics and epidemiology at the Columbia University Medical Center. His research focuses on mainly cardiovascular disease though he has begun to research how diabetes can affect traumatic brain injury.

creators.name: Dr. Thomas Olsson
creators.description: Thomas Olsson, MD, PhD, is a researcher at the internal medicine department of the Uppsala University Hospital in Sweden. He is also a consultant in cardiology, a PCI-operator, and author of the book Emergency Medicine (Liber). Dr. Olsson’s primary research is focused on mortality prediction in ED patients.

creators.name: Dr. Timothy Rockall
creators.description: Timothy Rockall, MD, is a consultant surgeon at the Royal Surrey County Hospital in Guildford. He specializes in gastrointestinal surgery and the management of colorectal disease. He has a particular interest in the development and practice of laparoscopic surgery and has developed an international reputation in the practice of laparoscopic resection for colorectal disease including bowel cancer. Dr. Rockall is also the creator of the Complete Rockall Score for Upper GI Bleeding .

creators.name: Dr. Veena K. Ranganath
creators.description: Veena K. Ranganath, MD, MS, is an associate clinical professor in the rheumatology division at the David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA. She is also the co-director of the UCLA Masters in Clinical Research program. Dr. Ranganath’s primary research is focused on general rheumatology and rheumatoid arthritis.

creators.name: Dr. Wanling Xie
creators.description: Wanling Xie, PhD, is a biostatistician at the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute in Boston, Massachusetts. She has published and co-published dozens of peer-reviewed studies. Dr. Xie's research is mainly focused on genitourinary cancers, particularly metastatic renal cell carcinoma and prostate cancer.

creators.name: Dr. Wendy Zondag
creators.description: Wendy Zondag, MD, PhD, is a physician in the section of Vascular Medicine in the Department of General Internal Medicine-Endocrinology at Leiden University Medical Center in the Netherlands.

creators.name: Dr. Yuman Fong
creators.description: Yuman Fong, MD, is the Sangiacomo Chair in Surgical Oncology, Chair of the Department of Surgery at the City of Hope Hospital and former Murray Brennan Chair in Surgery at Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center. He is an expert in hepatobiliary cancers and is leading the research effort to employ genetically modified viruses to destroy cancer cells.

creators.name: Jeffrey B. Gross, MD
creators.description: Jeffrey B. Gross, MD, is a professor of medicine and and chair of the department of anesthesiology at the the University of Connecticut. He is currently the chairman of the Task Force on Perioperative Management of Patients with Obstructive Sleep Apnea for the American Society of Anesthesiologists. Dr. Gross is an active researcher investigating novel methods in management in anesthesia.

creators.name: Dr. Ikuo Hirano
creators.description: Ikuo Hirano, MD, (d. 2024) was a professor of medicine at Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine and a globally respected leader in the study of eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE). He was a primary investigator on landmark clinical trials that led to FDA-approved therapies, including topical steroids and biologics for EoE. Dr. Hirano also co-developed the EREFS endoscopic scoring system, now widely used in both research and clinical settings. With over 200 peer-reviewed publications, his legacy lives on in the standard of care he helped establish and the many lives his work continues to improve.

creators.name: Dr. Peter Ferenci
creators.description: Peter Ferenci, MD, is a professor of medicine at the Medical University of Vienna, Austria. He practices within the department of internal medicine, gastroenterology and hepatology. He is Dr. honoris causae at the University of Cluj Napoca, Romania and the Semmelweis University, Budapest. Dr. Ferenci has published over 600 articles and abstracts on subjects including treatment of chronic viral hepatitis, inherited liver diseases and liver failure.

creators.name: Dr. Philippe Mathurin
creators.description: Philippe Mathurin, MD, PhD, is professor of hepatology and head of the research program on liver disease in the Department of Hepatology and Gastroenterology at the University Hospital of Lille, France. He has been an associate editor of the Journal of Hepatology since 2009. Dr. Mathurin has published extensively on research topics including alcoholic liver disease, viral hepatitis, non alcoholic fatty liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma.

creators.name: Dr. Vinod K. Bhutani
creators.description: Vinod K. Bhutani, MD, is a professor of pediatrics (neonatology) at Stanford University School of Medicine and a researcher at the Maternal and Child Health Research Institute in Stanford, CA. He is also the chair and founder of the Global Prevention of Kernicterus. Dr. Bhutani’s primary research is focused on neonatal jaundice biology and management.

creators.name: Dr. William R. Best
creators.description: William R. Best, MD, was a faculty member and assistant dean in the College of Medicine at the University of Illinois Chicago Professional Colleges. He was later appointed Chief of Staff at Hines VA Hospital and the associate dean for Veterans Affairs at Loyola University Chicago.

creators.name: Dr. Tomisaku Kawasaki
creators.description: Tomisaku Kawasaki, MD is a pediatrician and formerly served as the director of the department of pediatrics at the Red Cross Hospital. He was also the director of the Japan Kawasaki Disease Research Center, chairman of the Kawasaki Disease Research Committee and the director of the Kawasaki Disease Research Center in Tokyo. He has won several awards, including the first Japanese Pediatric Society Prize.

creators.name: Dr. Virginia Apgar
creators.description: Virginia Apgar, MD, (d. 1974) was an obstetrical anesthesiologist. Her eponymous score was the first to rate baby health at the time of birth. Through work at the March of Dimes, she was the first to shine light on the problem of premature birth. She was the first woman to be named Full Professor at Columbia University’s College of Physicians and Surgeons and is famously credited as saying that “women are liberated from the time they leave the womb.”

creators.name: Dr. Wolfgang Kruis
creators.description: Wolfgang Kruis, MD, has practiced as an internist and professor of medicine at the Clinic for Gastroenterology, Pulmonology and General Internal Medicine at the Evangelical Hospital Kalk, teaching hospital of the University of Cologne, Germany. He has published more than 240 original articles in multiple international journals and has contributed to over 20 German textbooks for internal medicine and gastroenterology.

creators.name: Dr. Wong Chin Ho
creators.description: Wong Chin Ho, MD, is a plastic surgeon accredited by the Ministry of Health of Singapore and head of W Aesthetic Plastic Surgery. He complete advanced surgical training at the Department of Plastic Reconstructive and Aesthetic Surgery at Singapore General Hospital. Dr. Wong is actively involved in clinical research with interests in facial anatomy, anatomical changes of the aging face and aesthetic surgery.

creators.name: Janet Tate, M.P.H., Sc.D.
creators.description: Janet Tate, M.P.H., Sc.D., is the director of the biostatistics core of the Veterans Aging Cohort Study (VACS) at the Yale School of Medicine in Connecticut. Her work includes structural modeling, imputation, longitudinal analyses, and competing risk analyses.

creators.name: Dr. Vincent Auffret
creators.description: Vincent Auffret, MD, PhD, is a cardiologist at Rennes University Hospital, France. Dr. Auffret is an active researcher focusing on interventional cardiology, including percutaneous treatment of coronary artery disease and heart valve disease, and clinical outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve replacement.

creators.name: Dr. Frank Cole
creators.description: Frank Cole, MD, was director and later chairman of the department of anesthesiology at Lincoln General Hospital in Lincoln, Nebraska, and served as a clinical associate in surgery at the University of Nebraska College of Medicine. He is best known for introducing the Cole Tracheal Tube in 1945 and for publishing “Pediatric Formulas for the Anesthesiologist” in 1957, a paper that helped popularize age-based pediatric endotracheal tube sizing.

creators.name: Dr. Phillip A. Barber
creators.description: Phillip A. Barber, MD, FRCPC, is an associate professor of neurology at the University of Calgary and is also the co-director of the Stroke Prevention Clinic. He has been awarded the New Investigator Award by the CIHR, Heart and Stroke Foundation of Canada, and the Alberta Heritage Foundation of Medical Research. Dr. Barber's primary research revolves around dementia, infarct maturation and stroke.

creators.name: Dr. V. Marco Ranieri
creators.description: V. Marco Ranieri, MD, is a professor in the department of medical and surgical sciences at Università di Bologna in Italy. Previously, he was a professor of anesthesia and chair of the residency program in anesthesia and reanimation at the University of Turin. Dr. Ranieri’s primary research is focused on pharmacological interventions for the treatment of ARDS.

creators.name: Nadia Awad, PharmD
creators.description: Nadia Awad, PharmD, BCPS is a pediatric pharmacist at Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital in New Jersey. She is also a contributor/editor of blogs including Academic Life in Emergency Medicine (ALiEM) and Emergency Medicine PharmD .

creators.name: Dr. Sean J. Barbour
creators.description: Sean J. Barbour, MD, is an associate professor in the division of nephrology at the University of British Columbia’s department of medicine. He is also the medical lead and chair of the BC Renal Glomerulonephritis Committee and GN Registry. Dr. Barbour’s primary research is focused on health outcomes and health services delivery in glomerulonephritis and using prediction modeling techniques to improve risk stratification in glomerular diseases.

creators.name: Dr. Timothy S. Chang
creators.description: Timothy S. Chang, MD, PhD, is a neurology resident at UCLA. He received his PhD in Clinical Investigation with a concentration in biomedical informatics in the Institute for Clinical and Translational Research from the University of Wisconsin. He has published many papers on topics including Alzheimer’s treatment and respiratory disease diagnosis.

creators.name: Dr. Warren McIsaac
creators.description: Warren McIsaac, MD, MSc, is a family physician and an associate professor in the department of family and community medicine at the University of Toronto. He is also the research director of the Granovsky Gluskin Family Medicine Centre. Dr. McIsaac’s research interests include antibiotic resistance, antimicrobial stewardship, and prescribing decisions in primary care.

creators.name: Dr. Wenhua Liang
creators.description: Wenhua Liang, MD, is an associated professor in the department of thoracic oncology at the First Affiliated Hospital Guangzhou Medical University in China. He is also secretary general and chairman of the Immunotherapy Committee of Guangdong Association of Thoracic Disease. Dr. Liang's primary research is focused on lung cancer case management and clinical data mining.

creators.name: Dr. David M. Kent
creators.description: David Kent, MD, MS is a professor at Tufts University School of Medicine and director of the Tufts Predictive Analytics and Comparative Effectiveness (PACE) Center. He also directs the Tufts University MS/PhD Graduate Program in Clinical and Translational Science. His research program seeks to better understand and address the limitations of using group-derived evidence as the basis for decision making in individual patients. He was PI of both the NIH-funded RoPE study and the PCORI-supported SCOPE Consortium, which developed and validated the PASCAL Classification Index. He has approximately 300 peer-reviewed articles and has received over 20 grants from PCORI and the NIH.

creators.name: Dr. Yogesh N.V. Reddy
creators.description: Yogesh N.V. Reddy, MBBS, MSc, is a heart failure specialist in the division of cardiovascular diseases at Mayo Clinic in Minnesota. Dr. Reddy’s primary research is focused on diagnosis and treatment of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, pulmonary hypertension and exercise physiology.

creators.name: Dr. Zhonghua Lin
creators.description: Zhonghua Lin, MD, is a practicing physician specializing in digestive disorders.

creators.name: James S. Yoon
creators.description: James S. Yoon is a third year medical student at Yale School of Medicine in Connecticut. His research focuses on value-based healthcare aimed at improving patient experiences through policy reforms, delivery system innovation, and outcomes research that informs safe, evidence-based clinical practices.

creators.name: Dr. Lisa B. VanWagner
creators.description: Lisa B VanWagner, MD, MSc, is an associate professor in the Department of Internal Medicine at UT Southwestern Medical Center and serves as director of clinical research for the division of digestive and liver diseases. She has been awarded from the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases, the European Association for the Study of the Liver, the American Society of Transplantation, and the American Heart Association. Her clinical work focuses on patients with diseases of the heart-liver axis, particularly those with metabolic dysfunction associated steatotic liver disease.

creators.name: Dr. Tomas Corcoran
creators.description: Tomas Corcoran, MD, is a clinical professor and research director in the department of anesthesia and pain medicine at Royal Perth Hospital in Perth, Australia. He was, notably, the chief investigator of a global study on the effects of dexamethasone on post-surgical emesis. Dr. Corcoran's clinical research focuses on surgical outcomes and anesthetics.

creators.name: Dr. Vincenzo Stanghellini
creators.description: Vincenzo Stanghellini, MD, is a professor of medicine at the University of Bologna in Italy. He is also chair of internal medicine at the Sant’Orsola-Malpighi University Hospital of Bologna and is a recipient of the Master Award for Sustained Achievement in Digestive Sciences from the American Gastroenterological Association. Dr. Stanghellini’s primary research is focused on the pathophysiology, diagnosis, and treatment of functional GI disorders and digestive syndromes.

creators.name: Jean-Yves Dupuis, MD
creators.description: Jean-Yves Dupuis, MD, is a staff anesthesiologist of the Division of Cardiac Anesthesiology and an associate professor at the University of Ottawa. He is a regular contributor as a principal or co-investigator to single and multicenter randomized trials assessing new drugs and therapies in the perioperative setting of cardiac surgery. Dr. Dupuis’ research interests are perioperative epidemiology and the analysis of medical practice in the cardiac surgical population.

creators.name: Dr. William J. Taylor
creators.description: William J. Taylor, MBChB, PhD, is an associate professor of rheumatology at Wakefield Hospital as well as the University of Otago in Wellington, New Zealand. He is also president of the New Zealand Rehabilitation Association. Dr. Taylor’s research focuses primarily on osteoporosis, adult rheumatology, and gout.

creators.name: Dr. Asgher Champsi
creators.description: Asgher Champsi, MD, is a clinical research fellow and cardiology specialist registrar at the University of Birmingham. He specializes in using big data, machine learning, and artificial intelligence to improve care for patients with atrial fibrillation and heart failure.

creators.name: Dr. Simon J. Griffin
creators.description: Simon J. Griffin, DM, is professor of general practice at the University of Cambridge, Group Leader in the MRC Epidemiology Unit and an assistant general practitioner at Lensfield Medical Practice in Cambridge, UK. He leads the Prevention of Diabetes and Related Metabolic Disorders Programme. Professor Griffin’s research interests include prevention and early detection of chronic conditions such as diabetes.

creators.name: Dr. Fulvio Morello
creators.description: Fulvio Morello, MD, PhD, is an associate professor of internal medicine at the University of Turin in Turin, Italy, and an attending physician in the emergency medicine unit at A.O.U. Città della Salute e della Scienza di Torino. Dr. Morello’s primary research focuses on acute cardiovascular emergencies, diagnostic risk stratification, and emergency department clinical decision-making.

creators.name: Dr. Stephen J. Lewis
creators.description: Stephen J. Lewis, MD, MB ChB (Aber), BSc(Hons), FRCP, is a gastroenterologist at Derriford Hospital in Plymouth, United Kingdom and an affiliate of the Bristol Nutrition Biomedical Research Unit in Bristol. He trained in infectious diseases at the Hospital for Tropical Diseases in London and worked with medical charities in West Africa. Dr. Lewis’ primary research interests include perioperative nutrition, infectious disease, irritable bowel syndrome, malabsorption, and intestinal infections.

creators.name: Dr. Willis Maddrey
creators.description: Willis Maddrey, MD, is professor of internal medicine and assistant to the president at The University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center at Dallas. Previously, he directed the liver unit at The Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine and was chairman of the Department of Medicine at Jefferson Medical College. Dr. Maddrey has authored numerous publications based on research interests in chronic viral hepatitis, drug-induced liver disease, alcohol-induced liver disease, liver transplantation, and primary biliary cirrhosis.

creators.name: Frank A. Gotch, MD
creators.description: Frank Gotch, MD is an associate professor at the University of California, San Francisco. He is best known for his extensive research in dialysis adequacy, including the development of Kt/V. Dr Gotch's current research interests are primarily concerned with modeling dialysis technology.

creators.name: Ms. Jennifer Abbey
creators.description: Jennifer Abbey, RN, PhD is a professor of nursing, specializing in aged care at the School of Nursing of Queensland University of Technology and The Prince Charles Hospital Health Service District. She was formerly the director of the Dementia Collaborative Research and Training Centre for Consumers, Carers and Social Research as well as the Deputy Director of the Eastern Australia Dementia Training and Study Centre.

creators.name: Ms. Victoria Warden, RN
creators.description: Victoria Warden, RN, is a nursing research health scientist at the Geriatric Research Education Clinical Center at Edith Nourse Rogers Memorial Veterans Medical Center in Bedford, Massachusetts.

creators.name: Dr. Vincenzo Mazzaferro
creators.description: Vincenzo Mazzaferro, MD, is a professor of medicine and director of the Gastrointestinal and Hepato-Pancreatic Surgery and Liver Transplantation Unit at the Istituto Nazionale dei Tumori in Milan, Italy. He is an avid researcher of liver transplantation and studies treatment of metastatic cancers to the liver and novel treatments of tumors. Dr. Mazzaferro’s research group was responsible for the development of the Milan Criteria, which has been adopted as a transplant guideline in many countries.

creators.name: Dr. Marco Daperno
creators.description: Marco Daperno, MD, is a gastroenterologist at AO Ordine Mauriziano in Turin, Italy. He has contributed to European Crohn’s and Colitis Organisation (ECCO) consensus work and publishes widely on inflammatory bowel disease care, with a strong focus on endoscopic assessment and related clinical outcomes.

creators.name: Dr. Shannon N. Acker
creators.description: Shannon N. Acker, MD, is a pediatric surgeon at the University of Colorado. Dr. Acker’s primary research is focused on trauma and surgical complications in adolescents.

creators.name: Dr. William E. Hunt
creators.description: William E. Hunt, MD (d. 1999) retired in 1991 as a professor emeritus of surgery after 37 years at Ohio State College of Medicine. He received a Lifetime Achievement Award and Gold Medal from the Neurological Society of America. While best known for the Hunt-Hess classification, he also defined the Tolosa-Hunt syndrome of ophthalmoplegia, a painful paralysis of the eye muscles.

creators.name: Dr. Sheldon Magder
creators.description: Sheldon Magder, MD, is a critical care physician at Royal Victoria Hospital and a professor in the Department of Physiology at McGill University in Montreal, Canada. His research is in cardiovascular physiology, specifically regulation of vascular tone in sepsis, the effects of the estrogens on the vascular wall and control and distribution of peripheral blood flow in exercise, heat stress and shock.

creators.name: Peter Lok
creators.description: Peter Lok, RRT, is best known in literature as the co-author of the Wexler and Lok formula for PCO₂. He was a respiratory therapist in the department of anesthesia at the University of Western Ontario in Canada at the time of publication.

creators.name: Dr. Stefan Bösner
creators.description: Stefan Bösner, MD, MPH, is a professor of general practice and family medicine at Philipps University of Marburg in Marburg, Germany. He is active clinically as a general practitioner. Dr. Bösner has published multiple studies on coronary artery disease, specifically chest pain in primary care and medical decision making.

creators.name: Dr. Steve Goodacre
creators.description: Steve Goodacre, MB, ChB, MRCP, DipIMC, FRCEM, MSc, PhD, is a professor of emergency medicine at the University of Sheffield in England. He is also the senior associate editor of the Annals of Emergency Medicine journal and chair of the NIHR Clinical Trials Unit Standing Advisory Committee. Dr. Goodacre's primary research is focused on emergency care organization, clinical risk prediction, and economic analysis.

creators.name: Dr. Sundararajan V. Rajkumar
creators.description: Sundararajan V. Rajkumar, MD, is a hematologist and oncologist at the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota. He is also the editor-in-chief of the Blood Cancer Journal and the associate editor of the European Journal of Hematology . Dr. Rajkumar’s primary research is focused on myeloma and related disorders.

creators.name: Dr. Tom van der Hulle
creators.description: Tom van der Hulle, MD, is an internist in the department of thrombosis and hemostasis at Leiden University Medical Centre in Leiden, Netherlands. His primary research interests involve hematology, oncology, and pulmonology.

creators.name: Professor Alasdair MacLullich
creators.description: Alasdair MacLullich, BSc, MB ChB, MRCP(UK), PhD, FRCPE, is a professor of geriatric medicine at the University of Edinburgh in Scotland. He also leads the Edinburgh Delirium Research Group working to improve the understanding, detection and treatment of delirium. Dr. MacLullich's primary reseach is focused on the pathophysiology, neuropathology, and clinical assessment of delirium.

creators.name: Dr. G.I. Wolfe
creators.description: Gil I. Wolfe, MD, FAAN, is a board-certified neurologist and chair of the Department of Neurology at the University at Buffalo Jacobs School of Medicine and Biomedical Sciences. In 2004, he was named to the Dr. Bob and Jean Smith Foundation Distinguished Chair in Neuromuscular Disease Research. Dr. Wolfe's clinical and research interests focus on myasthenia gravis and other disorders of neuromuscular transmission, complementing his broader work on idiopathic and immune-mediated peripheral neuropathies. His research has been supported by the National Institutes of Health/NINDS, the Muscular Dystrophy Association, the Myasthenia Gravis Foundation of America, and the Food and Drug Administration.

creators.name: Dr. Sherman A. Lee
creators.description: Sherman A. Lee, PhD, is an associate professor of psychology at Christopher Newport University in Virginia. He is actively researching COVID-19 associated anxiety and has developed the first medical screening tools for the condition. Dr. Lee’s primary research is focused on negative feeling states and the influence of personality and religion on those experiences.

creators.name: Dr. Sherri M. Donat
creators.description: Sherri M. Donat, MD, FACS, is a urologic surgeon at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center and professor of urology at Weill Cornell Medical College in New York, NY. She also serves as an advisor to the European Association of Urology and the International Minimally Invasive Society. Dr. Donat's research interests include tumor growth in bladder cancers, ablative therapies, imaging approaches for diagnosing genitourinary cancers, and patient outcomes.

creators.name: Dr. Sofia Barbar
creators.description: Sofia Barbar, MD, is a physician at Civic Hospital of Cittadella (Padua) in Italy. She graduated with honors from Medical School at Padua University, where she also completed Internal Medicine training, subsequently majoring in Emergency Medicine. She is an active researcher studying prevalence and treatment of venous thromboembolism. Her scientific interests particularly focus on clinical research in the field of venous thromboembolism (VTE), with special regards to prevention of VTE in medical ill patients and diagnosis and treatment of VTE even in unusual sites.

creators.name: Ms. Kerri M. Barber
creators.description: Ms. Kerri M. Barber, MSc, is the senior principal biostatistician at PRA Health Sciences and was previously the principal biostatistician at NHS Blood and Transplant in Bristol, UK. Ms. Barber’s primary research is focused on liver transplantation outcomes and planning.

creators.name: Dr. Sripal Bangalore
creators.description: Sripal Bangalore, MD, MHA, FACC, FAHA, FSCAI, is a professor of medicine at NYU Grossman School of Medicine and director of research for the Cardiac Catheterization Laboratory at NYU Langone Health. He is an interventional cardiologist and a widely published investigator in cardiovascular outcomes and coronary disease.

creators.name: Ms. Margaret Odhner
creators.description: Margaret Odhner, RN, BSN, CCRN, is an adult nurse practitioner at the University of Rochester.

creators.name: Dr. Alberto Tosetto
creators.description: Alberto Tosetto, MD, is the director of the Hemophilia and Thrombosis Center at the San Bortolo Hospital, Vicenza, Italy. He is a hematologist with a long-lasting interest in benign hematology, hemostasis, and clinical epidemiology.

creators.name: Dr. Alexander Kutikov
creators.description: Alexander Kutikov, MD, is an attending surgeon and professor of urologic oncology at Fox Chase Cancer Center in Philadelphia. He is an active investigator in kidney, prostate, bladder, and adrenal disease. Dr. Kutikov is a co-founder of VisibleHealth, Inc., a digital health company with flagship products that include the app suite drawMD and Ureteral/Endoscopic Stent Trackers.

creators.name: Dr. Alfredo Alvarado
creators.description: Alfredo Alvarado, MD, is a retired general surgeon, formerly at Plantation General Hospital in Florida. He previously held staff positions at Florida Medical Center and Westside Regional Hospital. Dr. Alvarado completed medical training at the National University of Colombia and residencies in general and thoracic surgery.

creators.name: Dr. Alpesh A. Patel
