creators.description: Alpesh A. Patel, MD, FACS, is a professor of orthopaedic surgery at Feinberg School of Medicine, Northwestern University. He is also the director of orthopaedic spine surgery at Northwestern University. Dr. Patel’s research focuses primarily on cervical spine surgery, minimally invasive spine surgery, motion preserving spine surgery, and disc replacement.

creators.name: Dr. Amelia O. Clive
creators.description: Amelia O. Clive, PhD, MBBS, BSc, works in the Academic Respiratory Unit at the University of Bristol in the United Kingdom. Dr. Clive's research interests include infection and malignant pleural effusion.

creators.name: Dr. James Feghali
creators.description: James Feghali, MD, is a neurosurgery resident at Johns Hopkins Hospital. He received his MD from the American University of Beirut Faculty of Medicine and has published on cerebrovascular neurosurgery, neurosurgical outcomes, and patient-specific risk prediction. Dr. Feghali’s research focuses on applying clinical data and predictive modeling to improve neurosurgical decision-making.

creators.name: Bryan D. Hayes, PharmD
creators.description: Bryan D. Hayes, PharmD, FAACT, FASHP, is an assistant professor of emergency medicine and clinical pharmacist at Harvard Medical School/Massachusetts General Hospital. He is also an associate editor and the creator of the CAPSULES series of Academic Life in Emergency Medicine (ALiEM) . His research interests include toxicology, medication safety and emergency preparedness.

creators.name: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
creators.description: The CDC is the leading national public health agency in the US. It focuses on infectious disease, food borne pathogens, environmental health, occupational safety and health, health promotion, injury prevention, and educational activities designed to improve public health. More information can be found on the CDC website .

creators.name: Dr. Adam Cuker
creators.description: Adam Cuker, MD, MS, is a board certified physician in Internal Medicine and Hematology and an assistant professor of medicine at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania. His clinical expertise is in clotting, bleeding and platelet disorders. Dr. Cuker's research interests include heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, immune thrombocytopenia, thrombosis and anti-coagulation.

creators.name: Dr. Robert M. Centor
creators.description: Robert M. Centor, MD, is the retired regional dean for the Huntsville Regional Medical and professor of medicine in the Division of General Internal Medicine at the University of Alabama at Birmingham. He researches medical decision-making and has published widely in the diagnosis and management of adult sore throats. Dr. Centor is also Chair Emeritus of the Board of Regents for the American College of Physicians.

creators.name: Dr. Robert Ohle
creators.description: Robert Ohle, MD, is an emergency physician and director of emergency medicine research at Health Sciences North (HSN), and an assistant professor at the Northern Ontario School of Medicine University. As vice-president of research and academic affairs at Health Sciences North Research Institute, Dr. Ohle leads a multidisciplinary team and oversees a $13 million research and education portfolio. His work is driven by a passion for research, education, and advancing evidence-based care in Canada.

creators.name: Dr. Alan J. Thompson
creators.description: Alan J. Thompson, MD, FMedSci, FRCP, FRCPI, is the dean of the Faculty of Brain Sciences and the Garfield Weston Professor of Clinical Neurology and Neurorehabilitation at the University College London in London, England. He is also a senior investigator and faculty member at the National Institute for Health Research. Dr. Thompson’s primary research is focused on predicting outcomes in multiple sclerosis using MRI techniques.

creators.name: Dr. Usoa E. Busto
creators.description: Usoa E. Busto, PharmD, (d. 2018) was a clinical neuroscientist and pharmacology researcher affiliated with the University of Toronto and the Centre for Addiction and Mental Health in Toronto. She served as head of the clinical neuroscience section and published widely on benzodiazepine withdrawal, psychopharmacology, nicotine dependence, and reward circuitry in mood and substance use disorders.

creators.name: Dr. Aneesh B. Singhal
creators.description: Aneesh B. Singhal, MD, is the vice-chair of quality and safety for the department of neurology and director of the Comprehensive Stroke Center at Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston. He is also on the board of trustees of Spaulding Rehabilitation Hospital and the Mass General Brigham Continuing Care Network. Dr. Singhal's primary research is focused on the treatment of advanced stroke, imaging of acute stroke, and stroke present in young adults.

creators.name: Dr. Ravi Korabathina
creators.description: Ravikiran Korabathina, MD, FACC, is an interventional cardiologist at Florida Medical Clinic Orlando Health in St. Petersburg, Florida. He is board-certified in cardiovascular disease and interventional cardiology, with additional certification in echocardiology and vascular ultrasound interpretation. Dr. Korabathina is a clinically active researcher whose published work has focused on hemodynamics, right ventricular dysfunction, heart failure, and mechanical circulatory support.

creators.name: Dr. Charles R. Baxter
creators.description: Charles R. Baxter, MD, (d. 2005) was the director of the emergency department at Parkland Memorial Hospital in Dallas, Texas. He founded the Parkland Hospital Burn Unit and was an active researcher, making advances in the treatment of burn victims and trauma procedures. Dr. Baxter was also one of the physicians who unsuccessfully tried to save John F. Kennedy after he was shot in 1963.

creators.name: Dr. Christopher Seymour
creators.description: Christopher Seymour, MD, is Assistant Professor of Critical Care and Emergency Medicine at the University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine. His research focus is on the organization of critical care during pre-hospital care, particularly the development of early diagnostic and prognostic models to facilitate allocation of patients and early treatments for those with acute illness. Dr. Seymour works clinically in the Medical Intensive Care Unit at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center Mercy Hospital.

creators.name: Dr. David Karnofsky
creators.description: David A. Karnofsky, MD, (d. 1969) was an oncologist at Sloan-Kettering Institute for Cancer Research. He specialized in cancer chemotherapy and affiliated with the division of experimental chemotherapy.

creators.name: Dr. Emanuele Foca
creators.description: Emanuele Foca, MD, PhD, is a medical doctor and researcher at the Clinic of Infectious and Tropical Diseases at the University of Brescia in Italy. Dr. Foca's primary research is focused on infectious diseases, specifically HIV infections.

creators.name: Dr. Ewen M. Harrison
creators.description: Ewen M. Harrison, PhD, MBChB, FRCS, MSc, is a professor of surgery and data science at the University of Edinburgh in Scotland. He is also the lead of the surgical informatics group in the Centre for Medical Informatics at the University of Edinburgh. Dr. Harrison's primary research is focused on the crowd-sourcing of patient level data, wearable technology, and global surgery.

creators.name: Dr. George Bush
creators.description: George Bush, MD, is an associate professor of psychiatry at Harvard Medical School in Boston, Massachusetts. He is also the the chief medical officer of MagnetiCare TMS of Long Island. Dr. Bush’s primary research is focused on anxiety, depression, and transcranial magnetic stimulation.

creators.name: Dr. Brian Gage
creators.description: Brian F. Gage, MD, MSc, is a professor of medicine at Washington University in St. Louis where he teaches Designing Outcomes & Clinical (DOC) Research and practices at Barnes-Jewish Hospital, where he directs the Clinical-Scientist Teaching And Research (C-STAR) program for medical residents. He directs the Washington University Fellowship in General Medical Sciences (GMS). Dr. Gage studies antithrombotic therapy and thrombosis, including cardioembolic stroke.

creators.name: Dr. Amnon Zisman
creators.description: Amnon Zisman, MD, is professor of urologic surgery at Sackler School of Medicine affiliated Tel Aviv University. He is currently head of urology department at Assaf Harofeh Medical Center. Dr. Zisman’s research focuses on increased accuracy of diagnosis and prognosis of RCC as well as novel treatment strategies in renal disease.

creators.name: Dr. Bartolome R. Celli
creators.description: Bartolome R. Celli, MD, is a professor of medicine at Brigham and Women's Hospital, associated with Harvard Medical School. He specializes in pulmonary and critical care medicine. Dr. Celli’s main research interest is scoring systems in management of COPD.

creators.name: Dr. Carlos Espinel
creators.description: Carlos Espinel, MD, is a cardiologist in Arlington, Virginia and is affiliated with Virginia Hospital Center. In addition to developing the FENa test, his research is the scientific basis for the US Food Labeling Law, which stipulates that food labels must list the exact amount of sodium and other contents. Dr. Espinel is also the creator of ArtMedicine, a medical education model integrating science, humanities and the arts.

creators.name: Dr. Louis de Jong
creators.description: Louis de Jong, MD, is a surgeon at the Franciscus Hospital in Rotterdam, the Netherlands. His research focuses on hip fracture outcomes, with a particular emphasis on developing and externally validating clinically relevant prediction tools to support decision-making in elderly and frail patient populations.

creators.name: Dr. Ansgar W. Lohse
creators.description: Ansgar W. Lohse, MD, is Chairman of the Department of Medicine at the University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf in Hamburg, Germany. He specializes in gastroenterology and infectious disease. Professor Lohse has authored over 300 peer-reviewed research papers in clinical and basic science hepatology.

creators.name: Dr. Matthew J. Maurer
creators.description: Matthew J. Maurer, Sc.D., M.S., is an associate professor of biostatistics and medicine at Mayo Clinic. He leads the Lymphoma Biostatistics and Data Science Laboratory and has more than 20 years of collaborative statistical experience across clinical research studies and trials. Dr. Maurer is an accomplished researcher investigating clinical endpoints, prognostic models, and decision tools in lymphoma outcomes research.

creators.name: Dr. Brian S. Katz
creators.description: Brian S. Katz, MD, is a vascular neurologist at OhioHealth Riverside Methodist Hospital in Columbus, Ohio. He has authored or co-authored several studies in stroke neurology. Dr. Katz completed residency at Mayo Clinic and fellowship at the University of Cincinnati.

creators.name: Dr. Chitra Hosing
creators.description: Chitra Hosing, MD, is a practicing oncologist and professor in the department of stem cell transplantation and cellular therapy at MD Anderson Cancer Center. She also serves as vice chair on the Clinical Safety and Effectiveness Committee at the MD Anderson Cancer Center. Dr. Hosing's research interests include stem cell transplantation, melphalan, graft vs. host disease, multiple myeloma, and fetal blood.

creators.name: Dr. Drahomir Aujesky
creators.description: Drahomir Aujesky, MD, MS, is an active clinician-investigator who predominantly researches venous thromboembolism. He was previously a full-time clinician at the University of Lausanne in Switzerland and completed the intensive Clinical Research Training Program (CRTP) under the direction of Dr. Michael Fine at the University of Pittsburgh.

creators.name: Dr. Edward Petsonk
creators.description: Edward Petsonk, MD, is a professor of medicine at West Virginia University. He is a practicing pulmonologist and critical care physician and has been published in the literature on occupational deficits due to lung disease. Dr. Petsonk is also a retired captain in the US Public Health Service.

creators.name: Dr. Eric Bateman
creators.description: Eric Bateman, MD, is a clinician-scientist at the University of Capetown in South Africa. He is the founder of the University of Cape Town Lung Institute and served as its director for 16 years until 2016. He is now a member of several editorial boards for international respiratory journals and has authored more than 300 papers.

creators.name: Dr. Hwai-I Yang
creators.description: Hwai-I Yang, PhD, is an associate research fellow at the Genomics Research Center in Taipei, Taiwan. He is also an adjunct associate professor at the Graduate Institute of Clinical Medicine at National Yang-Ming University. Dr. Yang’s primary research is focused on hepatitis epidemiology, translational epidemiology, immunoepidemiology of viral hepatitis, and immunoprevention of major cancers.

creators.name: Dr. Patrick J. McGrath
creators.description: Patrick J. McGrath, MD, is a professor of clinical psychiatry at Columbia University. He is currently co-director of the Depression Evaluation Service at the New York State Psychiatric Institute. Dr. McGrath’s current research focus is on pharmacogenetics and radiological imaging of brains to determine potential genetic response to antidepressant medications.

creators.name: Dr. Andrea O. Rossetti
creators.description: Andrea O. Rossetti, MD, is Director of the EEG/Epilepsy Unit and Sleep Center at the Centre Hospitalier Universitaire Vaudois (CHUV) in Lausanne, Switzerland. He is an active researcher on epilepsy and status epilepticus with multiple publications in peer-reviewed journals. Dr. Rossetti also brought vagal stimulation, a palliative treatment for refractory epilepsy, to the CHUV.

creators.name: Dr. Bert Brunekreef
creators.description: Bert Brunekreef, PhD, is a professor of epidemiology at Utrecht University in the Netherlands, where he is currently the director of the Institute for Risk Assessment Sciences. Dr. Brunekreef is co-author of more than 500 peer reviewed journal articles in the field of environmental epidemiology and exposure assessment.

creators.name: Dr. Daniel W. Lee
creators.description: Daniel W. Lee, MD, is a pediatric oncologist and leading researcher at the University of Virginia’s Pediatric Stem Cell Transplant Program. He has also worked as a researcher at the National Cancer Institute’s Center for Cancer Research. Dr. Lee’s research focuses primarily on pediatric immunotherapy.

creators.name: Dr. Carlo Bova
creators.description: Carlo Bova, MD, is an internal medicine physician at Annunziata General Hospital in Cosenza, Italy. He is also one of the investigators of the PESIT (Prevalence of Pulmonary Embolism Among Patients Hospitalized for Syncope) study. Dr. Bova's research interest is in venous thromboembolism, and he has published several papers in this field.

creators.name: Dr. C. Michael Gibson
creators.description: C. Michael Gibson, MS, MD, is a professor of medicine at Harvard Medical School in Massachussetts. He is also the Chief of Clinical Research in the Cardiovascular Division at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and the founder of PERFUSE, an academic research organization for a wide variety of cardiovascular studies. Dr. Gibson's primary research is focused on the pathophysiology of coronary artery disease and the efficacy of related therapies.

creators.name: Dr. Carole Maupain
creators.description: Carole Maupain, MD, is a cardiologist at Hôpital La Pitié Salpêtrière in France. She has also presented in coordination with ACTION Coeur, a research organization focused on cardiovascular disease research. Dr. Maupain’s primary research is focused on patient outcomes of cardiac events and risk stratification of cardiac arrest cases.

creators.name: Dr. David R. Matthews
creators.description: David R. Matthews, MD, is a Professor of Diabetic Medicine at the University of Oxford. He is the Deputy co-ordinator and member of the Executive and Policy Advisory Committees of the UK Prospective Study of Diabetes (UKPDS), as well as the founder of the Oxford Health Alliance. He is currently investigating the inter-relationships between insulin resistance and beta cell function, and the effects of a low carbohydrate diet in people with and without type 2 diabetes at Churchill Hospital with the Center of Diabetes, in the United Kingdom.

creators.name: Dr. Elena Sgarbossa
creators.description: Elena Sgarbossa, MD, is a board certified cardiologist and works as an independent medical and scientific writer/editor/translator. She is also a member of Editorial Board of the Journal of Electrocardiology. Dr. Sgarbossa previously worked in clinical cardiology and research at Rush-Presbyterian Medical Center and Cleveland Clinic.

creators.name: Dr. Jaime Prat
creators.description: Jaime Prat, MD, is an honorary professor at Autonomous University of Barcelona and a senior consultant in pathology at Hospital Sant Pau in Barcelona, Spain. He is also a member of the World Health Organization (WHO) Committee for Classification of Tumors of the Female Genital Tract and the International Federation of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (FIGO). Dr. Prat’s primary research is focused on gynecologic oncology.

creators.name: Dr. Michael Hallek
creators.description: Michael Hallek, MD, is an internist specializing in hematology and oncology in Cologne, Germany. He also serves as chair of the internal medicine department at the University of Cologne and director of the Center for Integrated Oncology. Dr. Hallek's primary research interests include the development of specific molecular therapies for leukemia.

creators.name: Dr. Orly F. Kohn
creators.description: Orly F. Kohn, MD, is an associate professor of medicine at the University of Chicago Medicine. She is also the medical director of the Home Dialysis Unit at the University of Chicago. Dr. Kohn’s primary research is focused on diabetic nephropathy, home dialysis, and electrolyte disorders.

creators.name: Dr. Daniel P. Davis
creators.description: Daniel P. Davis, MD, is an emergency medicine physician affiliated with Logan Health EMS in Kalispell, Montana, and has also held an appointment in the department of emergency medicine at UC San Diego. Dr. Davis is a prolific researcher whose work has focused on emergency airway management, resuscitation science, prehospital care, oxygenation after trauma, and other acute care topics.

creators.name: Dr. Bechien Wu
creators.description: Bechien U. Wu, MD is a gastroenterologist at Brigham and Women's Hospital in in Boston. He is also affiliated with Kaiser Permanente Los Angeles Medical Center. Dr. Wu is an active researcher, with interests in management of acute and chronic pancreatitis and care for patients with pancreatic cysts.

creators.name: Dr. Brian D. Steinhart
creators.description: Brian D. Steinhart, MD, FRCPC, dABEM, is an emergency physician at St. Michael’s Hospital in Ontario, Canada. He is also an associate professor in the department of medicine at the University of Toronto. Dr. Steinhart’s primary research is focused on acute coronary syndromes and cardiac biomarkers.

creators.name: Dr. Désirée van der Heijde
creators.description: Désirée van der Heijde, MD, is a professor of rheumatology at Leiden University Medical Center, the Netherlands and is affiliated with Diakonhjemmet Hospital in Oslo, Norway. She founded the Assessment in SpondyloArthritis international Society (ASAS) in 1995. Dr. van der Heijde is a principal investigator for clinical trials focused on rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis and axial spondyloarthritis.

creators.name: Dr. Giuseppe Bellelli
creators.description: Giuseppe Bellelli, MD, is a geriatric physician at the Azienda Ospedaliera San Gerardo in Monza, Italy. He is also an associate professor in the department of medicine and surgery at the Università degli Studi di Milano-Bicocca. Dr. Bellelli’s research interests include aging, delirium, and behavioral and psychotic symptoms of dementia (BPSD).

creators.name: Dr. Maureen Sampson
creators.description: Maureen Sampson, BSMT(ASCP), is a research clinical laboratory scientist in the chemistry service of the department of laboratory medicine at the National Institutes of Health Clinical Center. She has worked in laboratory medicine research at the NIH Clinical Center for decades and has authored more than 100 publications. Ms. Sampson is an experienced laboratory researcher focused on clinical chemistry and improving diagnostic testing methods.

creators.name: Dr. Daniel Strbian
creators.description: Daniel Strbian, MD, PhD, is a practicing neurologist at the University of Helsinki Central Hospital in Finland. He is an active researcher in the field of ischemic stroke.

creators.name: Dr. Douglas Drossman
creators.description: Douglas Drossman, MD, is professor emeritus of medicine and psychiatry at the University of North Carolina School of Medicine. He is founder, President Emeritus and Chief of Operations of the Rome Foundation. He is also the founder of the Drossman Center for the Education and Practice of Biopsychosocial Care and Drossman Consulting, LLC. Dr. Drossman has written over 500 articles and book chapters, has published two books, a GI procedure manual and a textbook of functional GI disorders (Rome I-IV), and serves on six editorial and advisory boards.

creators.name: Dr. Douglas T. Dieterich
creators.description: Douglas T. Dieterich, MD, FACP, is a professor of medicine in the division of liver diseases in the department of medicine at Mount Sinai Hospital in New York. He is principal investigator of the Hepatitis Outreach Network and an honorary lifetime member of the International Association of Physicians in AIDS for “Contributions in HIV Medicine.” Dr. Dieterich has authored or co-authored hundreds of peer-reviewed papers on hepatitis and hepatocellular carcinoma.

creators.name: Dr. Frank Herbstreit
creators.description: Frank Herbstreit, MD, is the head of intensive care medicine at the University Clinic of Essen in Germany. He is also a senior editor for Anesthesia and Analgesia. Dr. Herbstreit’s primary research is focused on anesthesia education and use for organ transplantation, as well as intensive care medicine and extracorporeal lung-assist (ECMO).

creators.name: Dr. Paul C. Davidson
creators.description: Paul C. Davidson, MD, FACE, was an endocrinologist at Atlanta Diabetes Associates in Atlanta, Georgia. He developed the original 1,500 Rule for estimating an insulin sensitivity factor and contributed to subsequent research evaluating correction-factor formulas for basal-bolus insulin dosing. Dr. Davidson’s work focused on practical approaches to insulin dosing and glucose management in patients with diabetes.

creators.name: Dr. Richard Theriault
creators.description: Richard Theriault, DO, is a professor in the breast medical oncology and critical care departments at the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center. He also is a trainer for the Tokyo-based Japanese TeamOncology Leadership Academy and J-HOPE Clinical Research Skill Advancement Workshop. Dr. Theriault has led multiple breast cancer research efforts and published over 180 peer reviewed articles, numerous book chapters and teaching publications.

creators.name: Dr. Seth S. Martin
creators.description: Seth S. Martin, MD, MHS, is a professor in the Division of Cardiology at the Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine. He is an attending cardiologist, a core faculty member at the Ciccarone Center for the Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease, and directs programs in advanced lipid disorders and digital health innovation. Dr. Martin is a nationally recognized researcher investigating preventive cardiology, lipids, cardiovascular risk, and digital health.

creators.name: Dr. Carl van Walraven
creators.description: Carl van Walraven, MD, is a professor of medicine and epidemiology at the University of Ottawa. He is also a senior scientist of the Clinical Epidemiology Program at the Ottawa Hospital Research Institute (OHRI) as well as a site director for the Institute for Clinical Evaluative Sciences at the University of Ottawa. He is an active researcher focusing mainly on quality improvement, continuity of care/information, and administrative database research.

creators.name: Dr. Christian C. Apfel
creators.description: Christian C. Apfel, MD, PhD, MBA, is the founder and CEO of SageMedic, a biotechnology company focusing on cancer therapy, and chair of the Life Science Committee at the Keiretsu Angel Investment Forum. Previously, he was a clinician and professor in the anesthesiology department at UCSF and led the Perioperative Clinical Research Core. Dr. Apfel’s primary research is focused on improving patient recovery and perioperative outcomes.

creators.name: Dr. Christopher L. Moore
creators.description: Christopher L. Moore, MD, is a professor of emergency medicine at Yale University. He is also Chief of the Emergency Ultrasound Section in the Department of Emergency Medicine. Dr. Moore’s research focuses primarily on diagnostic testing and diagnostic imaging in the emergency setting.

creators.name: Dr. David E. Kleiner
creators.description: David E. Kleiner, MD, PhD, is an anatomical pathologist at the National Cancer Institute. He is also director of clinical operations and chief of the postmortem pathology section at the NIH. Dr. Kleiner’s research focuses primarily on chronic liver disease and transplantation pathology.

creators.name: Dr. William Beaubien-Souligny
creators.description: William Beaubien-Souligny, MD, PhD, is a nephrologist and clinical researcher at the centre de recherche du centre hospitalier de l’Université de Montréal and Université de Montréal. He has received several research recognitions, including the KRESCENT New Investigator Award and the Canadian Society of Nephrology New Investigator Award. Dr. Beaubien-Souligny is an experienced researcher studying cardio-renal interactions, acute kidney injury, fluid balance management, renal replacement therapy, and point-of-care ultrasound in nephrology and critical care.

creators.name: Dr. Bruce Flamm
creators.description: Bruce Flamm, MD, is a clinical professor of obstetrics and gynecology at the University of California, Irvine, and has practiced obstetrics and gynecology at multiple Kaiser Permanente Medical Centers. He has published dozens of papers in peer-reviewed journals and four books, including Birth After Cesarean: The Medical Facts . Dr. Flamm also serves on the editorial board of several medical journals.

creators.name: Dr. C. Miller Fisher
creators.description: Charles Miller Fisher, MD, (d. 2014), was Professor Emeritus at Harvard Medical School, where he spent 50 years as a teacher and clinician. He was an active researcher in stroke neurology and is credited with identifying and naming transient ischemic attacks (TIA). He was a founder of the Massachusetts General Hospital Stroke Service and was inducted into the Canadian Medical Hall of Fame.

creators.name: Dr. Mikko Hallman
creators.description: Mikko Hallman, MD, is a physician-scientist in the Department of Pediatrics at the University of Oulu, Finland. His research focuses on neonatal and perinatal medicine, with a strong emphasis on the causes and prevention of spontaneous preterm birth. Dr. Hallman has led numerous multidisciplinary projects and has served as the supervisor for more than 30 PhD theses at the University of Oulu and the University of Helsinki. He has authored over 500 scientific publications throughout his career.

creators.name: Dr. Charles P. Hughes
creators.description: Charles P. Hughes, MD, (d. 2018) was the chief of staff of Erlanger Medical Center in Chattanooga, Tennessee. He also served as a faculty member at the University of Tennessee College of Medicine. Dr. Hughes’ primary research interests included Alzheimer’s disease and dementia.

creators.name: Dr. Edward H. Bishop
creators.description: Edward H. Bishop, MD, (d. 1995) was one of the biggest names in obstetrics and gynecology during his lifetime. He was a pioneer in research and clinical practice, working primarily at Pennsylvania Hospital. His research involved re-evaluating exam techniques and predicting delivery outcomes.

creators.name: Dr. Ghassan K. Abou-Alfa
creators.description: Ghassan K. Abou-Alfa, MD, is a medical oncologist at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center. He is also chair of the National Cancer Institute (NCI) Task Force for Hepatobiliary Cancers. Dr. Abou-Alfa’s primary research is focused on small molecule-based therapy for hepatobiliary and pancreatic cancers.

creators.name: Dr. James V. Quinn
creators.description: James V. Quinn, MD, MS, is a professor of emergency medicine at Stanford University School of Medicine. He is also the director of research in the emergency medicine department at Stanford University and serves as a member of the Scientific Advisory Board for iRhythm Technologies, Inc. Dr. Quinn’s primary research is focused on management of syncope.

creators.name: Dr. Lars R. Lundell
creators.description: Lars R. Lundell, MD, PhD, is a practicing surgeon and professor of surgery at Karolinska University Hospital in Stockholm, Sweden. He previously served as board member and president of the European Association for Gastroenterology and on the leadership of other societies including Endoscopy and Nutrition (EAGEN), European Society for Esophagology (ESE), the United European Gastroenterology (UEG) Education Committee, the International Working Group for Classification of Oesophagitis (IWGCO), and the International Society for Diseases of the Esophagus (ISDE). Dr. Lundell's primary research interest is GERD, and he has also studied cancer of the stomach and esophagus.

creators.name: Dr. Michael J. Proctor
creators.description: Michael J. Proctor, MD, is a faculty member at the University of Glasgow and practices at the Royal Infirmary. His research focuses on systemic inflammatory response in weight loss, poor physical function and quality of life and poor survival of the patient with cancer.

creators.name: Dr. Barbra Backus
creators.description: Barbra Backus, MD, PhD, worked as a junior cardiologist under Dr. Six prior to her work on the HEART Studies. After completing her PhD, she began a residency in Emergency Medicine at the Albert Schweitzer Hospital in Dordrecht in the Netherlands. Her main research focus is on risk stratification of ACS.

creators.name: Dr. Bradley S. Galer
creators.description: Bradley S. Galer, MD, is the executive vice president and chief medical officer of Zogenix Pharmaceuticals. Dr. Galer has also held numerous other industry positions, both academic and clinical in scope. He has published over 200 articles on pain management in peer review journals and textbooks.

creators.name: Dr. Christopher P. Derry
creators.description: Christopher P. Derry, MRCP, is a consultant neurologist in the department of clinical neuroscience and sleep medicine at the University of Edinburgh in Scotland. He is also an honorary clinical senior lecturer and NHS research fellow at the University of Edinburgh. Dr. Derry’s primary research is focused on sleep disorders and epilepsy.

creators.name: Dr. David M. Levine
creators.description: David M. Levine, MD, MPH, MA, is practicing primary care physician in the Division of General Internal Medicine and Primary Care at Brigham and Women’s Hospital in Massachusetts. He is also an investigator at Brigham and Women's Hospital and Harvard Medical School. Dr. Levine's primary research is focused on digital health, advanced home-based care, and improving the quality of delivered care.

creators.name: Dr. Guy M. McKhann
creators.description: Guy M. McKhann, MD, is a professor of neurology and neuroscience at Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore, Maryland. Dr. McKhann’s primary research is focused on neurodegenerative diseases.

creators.name: Dr. Oliver Blatchford
creators.description: Oliver Blatchford, MD, PhD, MPH, is a consultant in public health medicine working at NHS Health Protection Scotland. He is also honorary senior lecturer in public health at the University of Glasgow. Dr. Blatchford is the specialist lead for tuberculosis control and researches causes of healthcare associated infection (HAI).

creators.name: Dr. Geanina Popoveniuc
creators.description: Geanina Popoveniuc, MD, is a diabetes and metabolism endocrinologist that practices at the MedStar Washington Hospital Center.

creators.name: Dr. Ian Stiell
creators.description: Ian Stiell, MD, MSc, FRCPC, is Professor and Chair, Department of Emergency Medicine, University of Ottawa; Distinguished Professor and University Health Research Chair, University of Ottawa; Senior Scientist, Ottawa Hospital Research Institute; and Emergency Physician, The Ottawa Hospital. He is internationally recognized for his research in emergency medicine with a focus on the development of clinical decision rules and the conduct of clinical trials involving acutely ill and injured patients treated by prehospital services and in emergency departments. He is best known for the development of the Ottawa Ankle Rule , the Canadian C-Spine Rule , and Canadian CT Head Rule and as the Principal Investigator for the landmark OPALS Studies for prehospital care. Dr. Stiell is the Principal Investigator for 1 of 3 Canadian sites in the Resuscitation Outcomes Consortium (ROC) which is funded by CIHR, NIH, HSFC, AHA, and National Defence Canada. Dr. Stiell is a Member of the Institute of Medicine of the U.S. National Academies of Science. To read more about Dr. Stiell's work, visit his website .

creators.name: Dr. Brian I. Rini
creators.description: Brian I. Rini, MD, is a professor of medicine at the Cleveland Clinic Lerner College of Medicine at Case Western Reserve University. He is also a physician in the medical oncology department at Cleveland Clinic. Dr. Rini’s primary research is focused on renal cell carcinoma and prostate cancer.

creators.name: Dr. Carmen Olmos
creators.description: Carmen Olmos, MD, is a clinical cardiologist at Hospital Clínico San Carlos in Madrid, Spain. She is also a researcher in the Endoval group. Dr. Olmos’ primary research is focused on cardiomyopathies, valve heart disease, and infective endocarditis.

creators.name: Dr. Charles R. Pound
creators.description: Charles R. Pound, MD, is the chief of urology in the department of surgery at the University of Mississippi Medical Center in Jackson, MS. He is also a professor of medicine at the University of Mississippi School of Medicine. Dr. Pound’s primary research is focused on urologic malignancy including prostate, bladder, and renal cancers.

creators.name: Dr. Seshagiri R. Mallampati
creators.description: Seshagiri R. Mallampati, MD, is a retired anesthesiologist. He practiced at Brigham and Women's Hospital throughout his clinical career. Dr. Mallampati is perhaps best known for his eponymous airway scoring system.

creators.name: Mr. Jeff Edmiaston
creators.description: Jeff Edmiaston, MS, CCC-SLP is a clinical researcher based in St. Louis, MO at the Barnes Jewish Hospital Stroke Center. His research is focused on understanding the effect of stroke and critical illness on the human swallow mechanism and on clinical decision support tools which allow clinicians to make more accurate predictions for recovery and develop effective methods of treatment.

creators.name: Dr. Michael W. Kattan
creators.description: Michael W. Kattan, PhD, MBA, (d. 2024) was chair of the Department of Quantitative Health Sciences at Cleveland Clinic. A pioneer in clinical nomograms, he was appointed by the American Joint Committee on Cancer to review and recommend cancer risk calculators for global use. Over his career, Dr. Kattan co-authored more than 1,200 peer-reviewed articles, with his work cited over 60,000 times, making him an influential figure in predictive analytics and outcomes research.

creators.name: Dr. Barry H. Rumack
creators.description: Barry H. Rumack, MD, is currently director emeritus of the Rocky Mountain Poison and Drug Center and director, Office of Professionalism at UC Denver. He is a retired professor emeritus of pediatrics at the University of Colorado School of Medicine.

creators.name: Dr. Corbin D. Jacobs
creators.description: Corbin Jacobs, MD graduated from UT Southwestern with a distinction in research and subsequently completed his radiation oncology residency training at Duke University. He currently practices in Washington and Idaho as a radiation oncologist with Cancer Care Northwest.

creators.name: Dr. Chani Traube
creators.description: Chani Traube, MD, is an assistant professor of pediatrics in the department of critical care medicine at Weill Cornell Medical College. She is also a pediatrician at New York-Presbyterian Hospital. Dr. Traube’s primary research is focused on pediatric respiratory failure, shock, and delirium.

creators.name: Dr. John L. Hankinson
creators.description: John L. Hankinson, PhD, is a biomedical engineer and consultant. He is also the course director for a National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health approved spirometry course and serves on the ATS Proficiency Standards for Pulmonary Function Laboratories Committee. Dr. Hankinson’s primary research is focused on respiratory diseases and spirometry.

creators.name: Dr. Marc Gorelick
creators.description: Marc Gorelick, MD, is an affiliate professor of pediatrics at the University of Minnesota Medical School. He is also president and CEO of Children's Hospitals and Clinics of Minnesota. Dr. Gorelick's primary research is focused on pediatric oncology and emergency assessment of pediatric patients.

creators.name: Dr. S. Claiborne Johnston
creators.description: S. Claiborne Johnston, MD, PhD is the Director of the Stroke Service at the University of California, San Francisco, where he is Professor of Neurology and Epidemiology and Director of the Clinical and Translational Science Institute (CTSI). He has published extensively in the prevention and treatment of stroke and transient ischemic attack. Dr. Johnston has been honored with multiple awards including the American Academy of Neurology’s Pessin Prize for Stroke Leadership.

creators.name: Dr. Vanja C. Douglas
creators.description: Vanja C. Douglas, MD, is a neurohospitalist and associate professor of clinical neurology at the University of California, San Francisco. He holds the Sara & Evan Williams Foundation Endowed Neurohospitalist Chair and is the director of the neurohospitalist division at UCSF. Dr. Douglas’ primary research interests are delirium and models of inpatient neurological care.

creators.name: Dr. Matthew J. Reed
creators.description: Matthew J. Reed, MA, MB, BChir, MD, is a p rofessor of emergency medicine at Edinburgh University, as well as a consultant and National Research Scotland Fellow at the Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh. He serves as the chair of the UK RCEM Research Committee and research director of emergency medicine research. Dr. Reed’s research focuses on syncope, palpitations, and aortic dissection, with a particular interest in integrating novel technologies into clinical practice.

creators.name: Dr. August Supervia
creators.description: August Supervia, MD, is a practicing physician in the emergency department at Hospital Universitari del Mar in Barcelona, Spain. He is an active researcher and a member of the European Respiratory Society.

creators.name: Dr. Brandon Webb
creators.description: Brandon Webb, MD, is a practicing infectious disease physician in the division of epidemiology and infectious diseases at Intermountain Healthcare in Utah. He has also served as an adjunct assistant professor at the University of Utah School of Medicine. Dr. Webb's research interests include bacterial pneumonia, antimicrobial stewardship, and transplant infectious diseases.

creators.name: Dr. Edwin D. Boudreaux
creators.description: Edwin Boudreaux, PhD, is a professor of emergency medicine at the University of Massachusetts Medical School in Worcester, MA. He is also the vice chair of research for the emergency medicine department. Dr. Boudreaux’s primary research is focused on suicide risk screening.

creators.name: Dr. Paul L. Enright
creators.description: Paul L. Enright, MD, is a retired research professor of medicine from the University of Arizona in Tucson. He reviews manuscripts for several pulmonary journals. Dr. Enright’s interests include pulmonary function testing, occupational lung disease, and diagnostic techniques for asthma and COPD.

creators.name: Dr. Reuven Pizov
creators.description: Reuven Pizov, MD, is a professor and chairman of anesthesiology and CCM at Hadassah Medical Center in Jerusalem, Israel. Dr. Pizov has authored several peer-reviewed studies in the field of anesthesiology.

creators.name: Dr. Robert L. Spitzer
creators.description: Robert L. Spitzer, MD, served as professor of psychiatry at Columbia University for 49 years before retiring in 2010. He was influential in the advancement of The Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM). He is recognized in many fields in psychiatry from severe mental illness to comparative diagnostics, such as the United States–United Kingdom Diagnostic Project, in which he helped author a paper comparing schizophrenia definitions in the US and UK.

creators.name: Dr. Amy A. Ernst
creators.description: Amy A. Ernst, MD, is an emergency medicine physician at the University of New Mexico department of emergency medicine. She has authored numerous publications in emergency medicine and acute care. Dr. Ernst’s research interests include emergency department operations, interpersonal violence, and patient-centered emergency care.

creators.name: Dr. Bruno Dubois
creators.description: Bruno Dubois, MD, PhD, is a professor of neurology at University Pierre and Marie Curie in Paris, France. He is also the director of the Institute for Memory and Alzheimer’s Disease at the Pitié-Salpêtrière Hospital in Paris, France. Dr. Dubois’ primary research is focused on Alzheimer’s disease, prodromal Alzheimer’s disease, and Parkinson’s disease dementia.

creators.name: Dr. Case K. Newsom
creators.description: Case K. Newsom, DO, is an emergency physician in the St. Luke's University Health Network in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania. Dr. Newsom’s primary research is focused on traumatic injuries.

creators.name: Dr. Mininder S. Kocher
creators.description: Mininder S. Kocher, MD, MPH, is a professor of orthopaedic surgery at Harvard Medical School, associate director of the Division of Sports Medicine at Children’s Hospital Boston. He has co-authored numerous articles and several books, most recently Operative Techniques: Pediatric Orthopaedic Surgery. Dr. Kocher has particular interests in anterior cruciate ligament injuries in skeletally immature patients, osteochondritis dissecans, articular cartilage injuries, tibial spine fractures, and many other topics.

creators.name: Dr. Paolo Prandoni
creators.description: Paolo Prandoni, PhD, is professor of the Department of Medical and Surgical Sciences, Thromboembolism Unit, at the University of Padua. He trained at the University of Padua from 1971 to 1979 before moving to Holland, where he studied for his PhD at the University of Amsterdam in 1992. Professor Prandoni’s research and professional experiences encompass the epidemiology, diagnosis, and management of thromboembolism. Of particular interest to him are studies addressing cancer-associated venous thromboembolism (VTE).

creators.name: Dr. Russell H. Wiesner
creators.description: Russell H. Wiesner, MD, is a professor of medicine at the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, MN, where he completed his postgraduate medical training in Gastroenterology. He currently practices within the Gastroenterology and Hepatology and Transplant Center. Dr Wiesner's research focuses on advanced liver diseases such as hepcatitis, biliary cirrhosis, primary sclerosing cholangitis, and hepatocellular cancer.

creators.name: Dr. Graham Teasdale
creators.description: Sir Graham Teasdale, MBBS, is an honorary professor at the Institute of Health and Wellbeing, University of Glasgow. He was previously the professor of neurosurgery, head of the department of neurosurgery, and associate dean for medical research at the University of Glasgow. Sir Teasdale was also the president of the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Glasgow (2003-2006), and was knighted in 2006 for his services to neurosurgery.

creators.name: Dr. Andreas M. Ganzoni
creators.description: Andreas M. Ganzoni, MD, is a physician and researcher in the internal medicine department at the University of Zurich in Zurich, Switzerland. Dr. Ganzoni’s primary research is focused on iron deficiency and plasma iron transport.

creators.name: Dr. David E. Newman-Toker
creators.description: David E. Newman-Toker, MD, PhD, is the director of the Division of Neuro-Visual and Vestibular Disorders at Johns Hopkins Medicine in Baltimore, MD. He is also a professor of neurology at Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine. Dr. Newman-Toker’s primary research is focused on diagnosis of stroke in patients presenting with acute, severe vertigo or dizziness.

creators.name: Dr. David Jiménez
creators.description: David Jiménez, MD, is associate professor at the University of Alcalá de Henares, Madrid and chief of the Venous Thromboembolism Program at the Ramón y Cajal Hospital in Madrid. He is also president-elect of the Vascular Sections of both the Spanish Society of Respiratory Medicine (SEPAR) and the Madrid Society of Respiratory Medicine (NEUMOMADRID) . Dr. Jiménez's research interests include venous thromboembolism, pleural diseases and malignant mesothelioma.

creators.name: Dr. Mark H. Ebell
creators.description: Mark H. Ebell, MD, MS, is a family practice physician and the director of epidemiology and biostatistics at the University of Georgia. He is a Robert Wood Johnson Generalist Physician Faculty Scholar and an editor at American Family Physician . Dr. Ebell is an expert on evidence-based medicine and point-of-care decision support, and has authored or co-authored over 200 peer-reviewed publications.

creators.name: Dr. Augustus John Rush, Jr.
creators.description: Augustus John Rush, Jr., MD, is professor emeritus at National University of Singapore. He is also adjunct professor of psychiatry at Duke University. Previously he was vice dean of clinical sciences at Duke-NUS Graduate Medical School Singapore. His research spans many areas of psychiatry including depression, cognitive therapy techniques and pharmacotherapy.

creators.name: Dr. Grace Rozycki
creators.description: Grace Rozycki, MD, MBA, is chief of surgery at Indiana University’s Methodist Hospital and the Willis D. Gatch Professor of Surgery and associate chair of the department of surgery at Indiana University School of Medicine. She previously served as chief of trauma and critical care at Grady Memorial Hospital in Atlanta. Dr. Rozycki has pioneered research on the application of surgeon-performed ultrasound in patients with post-trauma hemothorax, cardiac tamponade, hemoperitoneum, solid organ injuries, intra-abdominal abscesses, and femoral deep venous thrombosis.

creators.name: Dr. Jack L. Paradise
creators.description: Jack L. Paradise, MD, now retired, was the medical director of the Ambulatory Care Center at the Children’s Hospital of Pittsburgh. He was also a professor in the pediatrics department at the University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine. Dr. Paradise’s primary research was focused on indications for tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy, and on the diagnosis, management, and clinical significance of otitis media.

creators.name: Dr. Jeffrey J. Perry
creators.description: Jeffrey J. Perry, MD, is a professor in the department of emergency medicine at the University of Ottawa in Ottawa, Canada. His research interests include clinical decision rules, subarachnoid hemorrhage, and systematic review and meta-analysis. Dr. Perry is also a Senior Scientist with the Ottawa Hospital Research Institute and Research Chair of Emergency Neurological Research.

creators.name: Dr. Layla A. Al-Gwaiz
creators.description: Layla A. Al-Gwaiz, MD, FCAP is a practicing physician and researcher in Hematology Section of the Department of Pathology at King Khalid University Hospital in Riyadh, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

creators.name: Dr. Lin Chang
creators.description: Lin Chang, MD is responsible for the oversight and coordination of the Rome IV calculators on MDCalc. She is a Professor of Medicine at the Vatche and Tamar Manoukian Division of Digestive Diseases at UCLA and is a member of the Rome Foundation Board of Directors.

creators.name: Dr. Patrick Charles
creators.description: Patrick Charles, MBBS, FRACP, Ph.D, is a practicing infectious disease physician at Austin Health in Victoria, Australia. He is also the head of the general medicine unit and an honorary lecturer at the University of Melbourne. Dr. Charles researches the emergence of antibiotic-resistant pathogens, community-acquired pneumonia, and urinary bacteriotherapy, among other infectious disease topics.

creators.name: Dr. Vineet Chopra
creators.description: Vineet Chopra, MBBS, MSc, is an assistant professor of internal medicine and chief of the division of hospital medicine. He has published over 100 peer-reviewed papers and is associate editor of the American Journal of Medicine and the Journal of Hospital Medicine. Dr. Chopra's primary research interest is in identifying and preventing complications associated with central venous catheters, particularly peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs).

creators.name: Dr. Daniel Heng
creators.description: Daniel Heng, MD, MPH, is a staff medical oncologist at the Tom Baker Cancer Center in Calgary, Alberta, and a clinical professor of medicine at the University of Calgary. He holds a masters of public health from Harvard University and has a keen interest in outcomes, prognostic factors, and clinical trials research in kidney, bladder, prostate and testicular cancers. He is the chair of the Southern Alberta Genitourinary Tumor Group.

creators.name: Dr. Jeffrey E. Gershenwald
creators.description: Jeffrey E. Gershenwald, MD, FACS, is a professor in the surgical oncology department at the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center. He is also the medical director of the Melanoma and Skin Cancer Center at the University of Texas. Dr. Gershenwald’s primary research is focused on clinicopathological and molecular staging of melanoma.

creators.name: Dr. John A. H. Forrest
creators.description: John Arthur Hunter Forrest, MD, FRCP, (d. 2010) specialized in gastrointestinal and liver diseases at the Royal Infirmary and the Western General Hospital in Edinburgh, Scotland. He was also secretary of the Caledonian Gastroenterology Society, now called the Scottish Society of Gastroenterology. Dr. Forrest's research interests included gastrointestinal and liver disease, in particular around drug use, abuse, and metabolism.

creators.name: Dr. Yumin Jeon
creators.description: Yumin Jeon, MD, is affiliated with the department of emergency medicine at Korea University Ansan Hospital. His academic emergency medicine research focused on sepsis, shock, and emergency department risk stratification.

creators.name: Dr. Linda S. Franck
creators.description: Linda S. Franck, RN, PhD, FRCPCH, is a professor of family health care nursing at University of California, San Francisco (UCSF). She is also the co-principal investigator for the UCSF Preterm Birth Initiative. Dr. Franck’s primary research is focused on improving family-centered care.

creators.name: Dr. Daniel Aletaha
creators.description: Daniel Aletaha, MD, is an associate professor and consultant physician in the division of rheumatology at the Medical University in Vienna, Austria. His research focuses on clinical and translational science in inflammatory rheumatic disease.

creators.name: Dr. Gustavo Saposnik
creators.description: Gustavo Saposnik, MD, FRCPC, is an associate professor in medicine of neurology and St. Michael's Hospital in Toronto. He is also the chair and project leader at the Stroke Outcomes Research Center and a scientist at the Li Ka Shing Knowledge Institute. Dr. Saposnik’s research interests include stroke therapy and outcomes, and epidemiology of cerebrovascular disease.

creators.name: Dr. Martin H. Osmond
creators.description: Martin H. Osmond, MD, is a pediatric emergency physician at the Children’s Hospital of Eastern Ontario (CHEO). He is also the CEO and scientific director of the CHEO Research Institute. Dr. Osmond’s areas of research interest are the evaluation and management of pediatric head injuries and the use of pre-hospital care in the treatment of ill and injured children.

creators.name: Dr. Patrick S. Kamath
creators.description: Patrick S. Kamath, MD, is a professor of gastroenterology and hepatology at the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota. His research interests include acute-on-chronic liver failure, nonalcoholic fatty liver disease, polycystic liver disease, Budd-Chiari syndrome and hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia. Dr. Kamath is internationally renowned as a leading researcher in hepatology and has also won numerous awards as an educator.

creators.name: Dr. Pedro P. España
creators.description: Pedro P. España, MD, PhD, is clinical chief of pneumology at the Galdakao-Usansolo Hospital in Spain. His research has been utilized in many different hospitals to predict the risk of adverse outcomes in ED patients with community-acquired pneumonia. Dr. España’s primary research is focused on diagnosis of severe community-acquired pneumonia and the connection between the disease etiology and patient characteristics.

creators.name: Dr. Pierre Chopard
creators.description: Pierre Chopard, MD, MSc, is an associate professor at the University of Geneva, in Switzerland. He is also the chief medical officer of the Care Quality Division at Geneva University Hospitals. Dr. Chopard’s research interests include healthcare quality and risk management.

creators.name: Dr. Sabina Villalta
creators.description: Sabina Villalta, MD, is the medical director of internal medicine at the Cà Foncello Hospital in Treviso, Italy. She also serves as a member of the Commission for Venous Thromboembolism and the Bioethics Committee. Dr. Villalta’s primary research is focused on venous thromboembolic pathology.

creators.name: Dr. Venkatesh Thiruganasambandamoorthy
creators.description: Venkatesh Thiruganasambandamoorthy, MBBS, CCFP-EM, MSc, is an emergency physician and associate professor in the department of emergency medicine and epidemiology / community medicine at the Ottawa Hospital Research Institute in Ottawa, Canada. He heads the Venk Group, a research program that aims to reduce morbidity and mortality from syncope and pre-syncope using robust risk-stratification, particularly for identifying low-risk patients. Dr. Thiruganasambandamoorthy is a founding member of the Canadian Syncope Alliance, a national collaboration aiming to improve syncope care in Canada.

creators.name: Judith Tintinalli, MD
creators.description: Judith Tintinalli, MD, MS, FACEP, is editor-in-chief of the eponymous Tintinalli's Emergency Medicine series, the most widely-used and well-known emergency medicine textbook. She is Chairman Emeritus and a professor in the department of emergency medicine at the University of North Carolina School of Medicine, and also holds multiple associate and adjunct professorships. Dr. Tintinalli is one of the founders of the Emergency Medicine Residents' Association (EMRA) and has been named a Hero of Emergency Medicine by the American College of Emergency Physicians.

creators.name: Dr. Wee Shiong Lim
creators.description: Wee Shiong Lim, MBBS, MRCP, M.Med, MHPEd, is a d irector and senior consultant at the Institute of Geriatrics and Active Ageing in Singapore . He is also an associate professor at Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine and adjunct associate professor at Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine. His reserch revolves around the areas of sarcopenia and related disorders.

creators.name: Dr. Andre A. Kaplan
creators.description: Andre A. Kaplan, MD, FACP, FASN, is a nephrologist at UConn Health. He is also a professor of medicine at University of Connecticut School of Medicine. Dr. Kaplan’s primary research is focused on kidney disease and dialysis.

creators.name: Dr. R. Michael Tuttle
creators.description: R. Michael Tuttle, MD, is an endocrinologist at the Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center in New York, NY. He is also a consultant to the Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee of the FDA. Dr. Tuttle’s primary research is focused on thyroid and head and neck cancers.

creators.name: Dr. Bernard Rosner
creators.description: Bernard Rosner, PhD, is a professor of biostatistics at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, Harvard Medical School, and Brigham and Women's Hospital. His work has had cardiovascular, pulmonary, ophthalmologic, oncologic, and nutritional applications. Dr. Rosner's primary research interests involve statistical modeling of longitudinal data, analysis of clustered continuous, binary, and ordinal data, and methods for the adjustment of regression models to address measurement error.

creators.name: Dr. Robert S. Schwab
creators.description: Robert S. Schwab, MD, (d. 1972) was a neurologist and professor at Harvard Medical School. He contributed to a number of key advances in neurology, including the Schwab and England Scale and the Harvard criteria for brain death. Dr. Schwab is also well-known for his role as an expert witness in the Jack Ruby trial, testifying that Ruby was likely not insane when he shot Lee Harvey Oswald.

creators.name: Dr. Ron Pisters
creators.description: Ron Pisters, MD, PhD, is a cardiologist at Rijnstate Ziekenhuis Arnhem in the Netherlands. Previously, he worked as a clinical research fellow, focusing on atrial fibrillation, under the supervision of Harry JGM Crijns at the Department of Cardiology, University of Maastricht. Dr. Pisters' research interests include antithrombotic management of patients with atrial fibrillation and assessing the individualised risk of embolic and bleeding events.

creators.name: Dr. Steven Green
creators.description: Steven Green, MD, is a professor of emergency medicine and pediatrics at Loma Linda University, California. He currently is an attending physician in the emergency room and also conducts research on subjects like sedation and emergency protocols.

creators.name: Mark Pochapin, MD, FACG
creators.description: Mark B. Pochapin, MD, FACG, is director of the division of gastroenterology and hepatology at NYU Langone Medical Center and the Sholtz/Leeds Professor of Gastroenterology. He is also the vice chair for clinical affairs in the department of medicine. Dr. Pochapin is the former chief of endoscopy at New York-Presbyterian Hospital and founded the Jay Monahan Center for Gastrointestinal Health, and is the current president of the American College of Gastroenterology

creators.name: Dr. Joseph L. Mills
creators.description: Joseph L. Mills, MD, is professor and chief of the division of vascular surgery and endovascular therapy at Baylor College of Medicine. He has held leadership roles as president of the Peripheral Vascular Surgery Society, the Western Vascular Society, and the Association of Program Directors in Vascular Surgery. Dr. Mills' research focuses on noninvasive diagnostics, vein graft stenosis, intimal hyperplasia, and limb salvage in patients with diabetes mellitus. With over 450 peer-reviewed publications, he is an internationally recognized expert in chronic limb-threatening ischemia, diabetic foot ulcers, and limb salvage.

creators.name: Dr. Alok Khorana
creators.description: Alok A. Khorana, MD is a professor of medicine at the Cleveland Clinic Lerner College of Medicine, Case Western Reserve University, and the Sondra and Stephen Hardis Chair in Oncology Research. He is currently the vice-chair for clinical services of the Taussig Cancer Institute and director of the Gastrointestinal Malignancies Program at the Cleveland Clinic. His clinical and translational research program focuses on new therapeutics and outcomes prediction in gastrointestinal cancers and cancer-associated thrombosis.

creators.name: Dr. Andrew J. Armstrong
creators.description: Andrew J. Armstrong, MD, is an oncologist at the Duke Cancer Institute (DCI) in Durham, NC. He is a professor of medicine and surgery, and an associate professor in pharmacology and cancer biology at the Duke University School of Medicine, as well as the director of research in the DCI's Center for Prostate and Urologic Cancer. Dr. Armstrong’s primary research is focused on drug development, biomarkers, and assessing the efficacy of new therapies, as well as improving survival prediction and prognostication in metastatic prostate cancer.

creators.name: Dr. Scott E. Regenbogen
creators.description: Scott E. Regenbogen, MD, MPH, is an associate professor of surgery at the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor, MI. He is also the chief of the division of colorectal surgery and the associate chief clinical officer for surgical specialties at the University of Michigan Medical Group. Dr. Regenbogen’s primary research is focused on surgical management of colon cancer.

creators.name: Dr. Toshiaki Iba
creators.description: Toshiaki Iba, MD, PhD, is a professor in the department of emergency and disaster medicine at Juntendo University in Tokyo, Japan. Dr. Iba’s primary research is focused on coagulation disorder in sepsis, anticoagulant therapy for DIC, and venous thrombosis.

creators.name: Dr. Carl J. Buchholz
creators.description: Carl J. Buchholz, MD, is a general surgeon at the Northern Regional Hospital in Mount Airy, North Carolina. He takes a collaborative, patient-centered approach, tailoring care to the unique needs of each individual. Committed to advancing access to quality healthcare, Dr. Buchholz integrates innovative surgical techniques to improve outcomes and believes patients in his community receive the highest standard of care.

creators.name: Dr. Abdel R. El-Ganzouri
creators.description: Abdel R. El-Ganzouri, MD, is a practicing anesthesiologist and researcher at the Rush-Presbyterian-St. Luke's Medical Center in Chicago, Illinois. He is also a professor of anesthesiology at Rush Medical College. Dr. El-Ganzouri’s primary research is focused on tracheal intubation complications.

creators.name: Dr. Brahm Goldstein
creators.description: Brahm Goldstein, MD, is the senior medical director at Baxter Healthcare. He was formerly chief of pediatric critical care and the medical director of the pediatric intensive care unit at the University of Rochester Medical Center, where he also was a professor of medicine. Dr. Goldstein serves on the editorial board of many leading medical and scientific publications and has been on multiple advisory boards for healthcare companies.

creators.name: Dr. Sander Lefere
creators.description: Sander Lefere, MD, PhD, is a postdoctoral researcher in the department of internal medicine and pediatrics at Ghent University in Belgium. His research focuses on metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), with particular emphasis on pediatric MASLD, nuclear receptor signaling, and the hepatic effects of bariatric surgery.

creators.name: Dr. Eveline de Haan
creators.description: Eveline de Haan, MD, is a clinician-researcher in the Department of Surgery at Maasstad Hospital in Rotterdam, the Netherlands. Her research focuses on outcomes and mortality related to hip fractures.

creators.name: Dr. Alfred Jaretzki III
creators.description: Alfred Jaretzki III, MD (d. 2014) was a distinguished cardiothoracic surgeon affiliated with the Department of Surgery at the College of Physicians and Surgeons, Columbia University. He practiced at several prominent institutions, including Presbyterian Hospital, Mary Imogene Bassett Hospital, Bellevue, Delafield, and Harlem Hospitals. Dr. Jaretzki retired in 1992 and was honored with the title of Professor Emeritus of Clinical Surgery at Columbia Presbyterian Medical Center. His primary research focused on myasthenia gravis, and he contributed extensively to the literature on surgical thymectomy as a treatment for the disease. His work significantly advanced the medical community’s understanding of thymus anatomy and its role in autoimmune disorders.

creators.name: Dr. Anna S. Lok
creators.description: Anna S. Lok, MD, FAASLD, is a hepatology research professor and assistant dean for clinical research in the internal medicine department at the University of Michigan. She is also director of clinical hepatology at the University of Michigan Health System and the immediate past-president of the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases. Dr. Lok’s research focuses primarily on the history and treatment of hepatitis B and C, hepatocellular carcinoma, and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease.

creators.name: Dr. Anthony D'Amico
creators.description: Anthony D'Amico, MD, PhD, is professor of radiation oncology at Harvard Medical School. He is also chief of the Division of Genitourinary Radiation Oncology at Brigham and Women's Hospital and Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Dr. D'Amico's notable research involves the detection, staging, and treatment of prostate cancer, with over 140 peer-reviewed publications and four co-edited textbooks.

creators.name: Dr. Roman Zahorec
creators.description: Roman Zahorec, MD, CSc, is professor in the department of anesthesiology and intensive care medicine at the Institute of Oncology St. Alžbety in Slovakia. He is also the head of the department and is a member of the ethics committee. Dr. Zahorec's primary research is focused on anesthesia management in oncology cases and predictive outcomes in critically ill patients.

creators.name: Dr. Stephen Edge
creators.description: Stephen B. Edge, MD, FACS, FASCO, is an adjunct professor of surgery at Vanderbilt University and the current director of the Baptist Cancer Center. Dr. Edge has co-chaired the 2010 Breast Cancer Symposium and Guideline Panel for Postmastectomy Radiation and is serving on the editorial board of the Journal of Oncology Practice. His research focuses on staging systems and risk stratification for many types of cancers.

creators.name: Dr. Alexander Flint
creators.description: Alexander Flint, MD, PhD, is a neurologist and stroke specialist who practices via telemedicine in Northern California. His research focuses on stroke, neurological critical illness, and the use of ‘big data’ and machine learning in medicine. He was a co-founder of the medical imaging startup image32 (acquired by Citrix in 2015) and is currently working on novel technologies that enable machine learning and search directly on securely encoded datasets.

creators.name: Dr. Robert M.A. Hirschfeld
creators.description: Robert M.A. Hirschfeld, MD, MSc, (d. 2023) was a professor of psychiatry at Weill Cornell Medical College and previously served for many years as chair of psychiatry at the University of Texas Medical Branch. He also led major national efforts on bipolar disorder practice guidelines and held leadership roles in mood and anxiety disorders research. Dr. Hirschfeld was an influential researcher studying the diagnosis and treatment of depression, bipolar disorder, and anxiety disorders.

creators.name: Dr. Jason A. Trubiano
creators.description: Jason A. Trubiano, MD, is an Infectious Diseases Physician at Austin Health and Professor of infectious disease at the University of Melbourne in Australia. Dr. Trubiano’s primary research is focused on infectious diseases in immunocompromised patients, antibiotic allergy, and antimicrobial stewardship.

creators.name: Dr. Audrey De Jong
creators.description: Audrey De Jong, MD, PhD, is the head of the anesthesia resuscitation unit in the Department of Anesthesiology and Intensive Care Unit at the Saint Eloi Montpellier University Hospital in France. She is also an academic researcher at the University of Montpellier. Dr. Jong’s primary research is focused on intubation and pain medicine.

creators.name: Dr. Constantinos O’Mahony
creators.description: Constantinos O’Mahony, MD, is an honorary associate professor at the Institute of Cardiovascular Science at University College London and a consultant cardiologist at St. Bartholomew’s Hospital and Whipps Cross Hospital. He is a member of various cardiology societies, such as the British Cardiovascular Intervention Society and European Society of Cardiology. Dr. O’Mahony’s primary research is focused on clinical outcomes in cardiomyopathies and novel treatments.

creators.name: Dr. Jeffrey M. Testani
creators.description: Jeffrey M. Testani, MD, MTR, is an advanced heart failure specialist and associate professor of medicine (cardiology) at Yale School of Medicine. His primary research revolves around cardiac-renal interactions, fluid and sodium homeostasis, and diuretic resistance. Dr. Testani’s work is funded by the National Institutes of Health, as well as investigator-initiated grants from industry.

creators.name: Dr. Osama I. I. Soliman
creators.description: Osama I. I. Soliman, MD, is a professor of cardiology and director of the cardio-oncology research program at the University of Galway in Ireland. He is also the founder and director of the Euro Heart Foundation. Dr. Soliman’s primary research is focused on the application of precision medicine in the management of patients with heart failure.

creators.name: Dr. Andres F. Correa
creators.description: Andres F. Correa, MD, is an a ssociate professor and director of research in the Department of Urology at the Fox Chase Cancer Center. He also serves as the fellowship director and program director at the Society of Urologic Oncology. His research centers on clinical trials and translational studies in prostate, kidney, bladder, adrenal gland, testis, and penile cancers.

creators.name: Dr. Bryan Cotton
creators.description: Bryan Cotton, MD, MPH, is a professor in the department of surgery, division of acute care surgery at the University of Texas Health Center in Houston. He is an active researcher in the field of trauma and traumatic injury.

creators.name: Dr. Jose R. Maldonado
creators.description: Jose R. Maldonado, MD, FACLP, is the John & Terry Levin Family professor of medicine and a professor of psychiatry and behavioral sciences at Stanford University Medical Center. He is also the Chief of the Division of Medical Psychiatry and Medical Director of the Critical Care Psychiatry Service at Stanford University Medical Center. Dr. Maldonado’s research focuses primarily on solid organ transplantation, delirium, and neuropathophysiology of alcohol withdrawal syndrome. He is board certified in General Psychiatry, Consultation-Liaison Psychiatry, Forensic Psychiatry and Addiction Medicine.

creators.name: Dr. Jason G. Andrade
creators.description: Jason G. Andrade, MD, is an associate professor of medicine at the University of British Columbia in Canada. He is also co-chair of the Canadian Cardiovascular Society Atrial Fibrillation Guidelines committee. Dr. Andrade’s primary research is focused on atrial fibrillation and cardiac cryoablation.

creators.name: Dr. Atul Gawande
creators.description: Atul Gawande, MD, MPH, is a surgeon, writer, and public health researcher. He is most widely known as the critically acclaimed author of Complications: A Surgeon’s Notes on an Imperfect Science as well as several other bestsellers, including Being Mortal; The Checklist Manifesto: How to Get Things Right; and Better. He practices general and endocrine surgery at Brigham and Women’s Hospital and is professor in both the Department of Health Policy and Management at the Harvard School of Public Health and the Department of Surgery at Harvard Medical School. He is Executive Director of Ariadne Labs, a joint center for health systems innovation, and Chairman of Lifebox, a nonprofit organization making surgery safer globally.

creators.name: Dr. Gregg Fonarow
creators.description: Gregg C. Fonarow, MD, is a professor of medicine and the director of the Ahmanson-UCLA Cardiomyopathy Center. He also serves as the co-director UCLA Preventative Cardiology Program and co-chief of the UCLA Division of Cardiology. Dr. Fonarow has published over 800 research studies and clinical trials in heart failure management, preventative cardiology and outcomes research.

creators.name: Dr. Mathieu Pasquier
creators.description: Mathieu Pasquier, MD, is a medical senior lecturer at the University of Lausanne and a specialist in general internal medicine at Lausanne University Hospital in Switzerland. He is also affiliated with the International Comission for Alpine Rescue. Dr. Pasquier’s primary research is focused on accidental hypothermia and prehospital emergency medicine.

creators.name: Dr. Martin D. Cheatle
creators.description: Martin D. Cheatle, MD, is an associate professor of psychiatry, anesthesiology, and critical care at the University of Pennsylvania Perelman School of Medicine. He is also the director of behavioral medicine in the Penn Pain Management Center. Dr. Cheatle’s primary research is focused on the treatment of opioid use disorders in patients with chronic pain and improving pain care and risk of suicide in patients with pain and substance use disorders.

creators.name: Dr. Adam M. Licurse
creators.description: Adam M. Licurse, MD, MHS, is an internist at the Brigham and Women's Hospital in Boston. He is also an instructor in medicine at Harvard Medical School. Dr. Licurse’s primary research is focused on diagnostic radiology and nephrology.

creators.name: Dr. Joseph E. Tonna
creators.description: Dr. Tonna is an emergency physician and intensivist at the University of Utah. His primary research focuses on extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR), and clinical trials.

creators.name: Dr. Pimsiri Sripongpun
creators.description: Pimsiri Sripongpun, MD, is an associate professor of medicine working at the Gastroenterology and Hepatology Unit, Division of Internal Medicine, Faculty of Medicine, Prince of Songkla University, Hat Yai, Thailand. Dr. Sripongpun earned her MD degree with First Class Honors and Internal Medicine board from Prince of Songkla University and worked as a clinical fellow in Gastroenterology at Siriraj Hospital, Mahidol University, Bangkok, Thailand. She finished her research fellowship program in Hepatology at Stanford University School of Medicine, California, USA. She is currently involved in clinical practice as well as clinical research in gastroenterology and hepatology. She is also a member of the Gastroenterological Association of Thailand’s steering committee. Her research focuses on noninvasive tests in clinical hepatology, viral hepatitis, and nutrition in gastroenterology and hepatology.

creators.name: Yale Addiction Implementation Science Team
creators.description: The Creators Gail D’Onofrio Kathryn Hawk David Fiellin

creators.name: The EMBED Design Team
creators.description: The Creators Edward Melnick Gail D’Onofrio Jessica Ray Matthew Maleska Yauheni Solad Shara Martel Osama Ahmed Molly Jeffery Tim Platts-Mills Erik Hess Bidisha Nath

creators.name: Dr. Brandon C. Chapman
creators.description: Brandon C. Chapman, MD, is an assistant professor of surgery at the University of Colorado School of Medicine. He is also a member of the American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons. Dr. Chapman’s primary research is focused on oncology and surgery.

creators.name: Abdulrhman Alghamdi
creators.description: Abdulrhman Alghamdi, BS, MS, is a researcher and PhD candidate specializing in critical care and cardiovascular sciences at the University of Manchester in the UK. His primary research is focused on diagnosis of early acute coronary syndromes. ﻿

creators.name: Kimberly S. Hardin
creators.description: Kimberly S. Hardin, NP, is an acute care nurse practitioner at Denver Health in Colorado. Her primary research is focused on trauma and surgery.

creators.name: Dr. Aaron T. Beck
creators.description: Aaron T. Beck, M.D., (d. 2021) was a professor in the department of psychiatry at the University of Pennsylvania. He received numerous awards, including the 2006 Albert Lasker Award for Clinical Medical Research and the Gustave O. Lienhard Award from the National Academy of Medicine. Dr. Beck’s primary research focused on psychopathology, namely cognitive behavior therapy.

creators.name: Dr. Adam B. Raff
creators.description: Adam B. Raff, MD, PhD, is a dermatologist at Harvard Medical School. He is also an instructor in dermatology at Massachusetts General Hospital. Dr. Raff’s primary research is focused on infectious skin diseases, skin cancer, and eczema.

creators.name: Dr. Donna Przepiorka
creators.description: Donna M. Przepiorka, MD, PhD, is a chair of the Food and Drug Administration’s Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) and a former faculty member at the University of Tennessee, Memphis. She has expertise in transplantation immunobiology and cellular and gene therapy. Dr. Przepiorka's research primarily focuses on the development of oncology therapeutics and transplantation immunobiology.

creators.name: Dr. Brian E. Lacy
creators.description: Brian E. Lacy, MD, PhD, is a gastroenterologist and neurogastroenterologist at the Mayo Clinic in Jacksonville, Florida. He is the current co-editor in chief of the American Journal of Gastroenterology and former co-chairman for the Rome IV Committee on Functional Bowel Disorders. Dr. Lacy’s primary research interests are focused on disorders of gastrointestinal motility.

creators.name: Dr. Curtis Sessler
creators.description: Curtis Sessler, MD, is a professor at Virginia Commonwealth University (VCU) Health System. He is also director of the Center for Adult Critical Care and medical director of Critical Care and the Medical Respiratory ICU at the Medical College of Virginia (MCV). Dr Sessler’s research interests focus on ICU sedation, prevention of nosocomial infection, mechanical ventilation, and procedural competency.

creators.name: Dr. David Armstrong
creators.description: David Armstrong, MA, MB BChir, FRCP, FRCPC, FACG, AGAF, is a professor of medicine at McMaster University. His research interests include gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), dyspepsia, gastrointestinal (GI) motility, inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), nutrition, short bowel syndrome, colon cancer screening, and quality in endoscopy with 200 peer-reviewed publications, 100 invited reviews and letters, and 300 peer-reviewed abstracts. He has been a principal investigator for numerous clinical trials and taken part in many guideline consensus processes related to GERD, Helicobacter pylori, dysphagia, upper GI bleeding, gastroparesis, wireless capsule endoscopy and endoscopy quality. He is a past president of the Canadian Association of Gastroenterology (CAG), chair of the Canadian National Colon Cancer Screening Network (NCCSN), treasurer of the International Working Group for the Classification of Oesophagitis (IWGCO), chair of the guidelines committee for the World Gastroenterology Organization (WGO) and a board member of the Canadian Digestive Health Foundation (CDHF).

creators.name: Dr. Frank A. Chervenak
