creators.description: Leading expert on the Pregnancy Due Dates calculator: Frank A. Chervenak, MD, is a professor, chief OB-GYN and chairman of the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology at the New York Presbyterian Hospital. He is the author of “How Accurate Is Fetal Biometry in the Assessment of Fetal Age”, a comparative study of the gestational age prediction equation for singletons, twins and triplets with other pregnancy prediction formulas. Dr. Chervenak has published 250+ papers and co-authored/edited textbooks on topics including ultrasound and ethics in obstetrics and gynecology and physician leadership.

creators.name: Dr. Geert Verheyden
creators.description: Geert Verheyden, MD, is a professor of rehabilitation sciences at Katholieke Universiteit in Leuven, Belgium. He is also the secretary of POC Rehabilitation Sciences and Physiotherapy and is published in multiple academic journals. Dr. Verheyden's research interests include sensory and motor status, and noninvasive brain stimulation of patients who have suffered from a stroke.

creators.name: Dr. Joseph T. Flynn
creators.description: Joseph T. Flynn, MD, MS, is a professor of pediatrics at the University of Washington School of Medicine, where he holds the Dr. Robert O. Hickman Endowed Chair in Pediatric Nephrology. He is also chief of the division of nephrology at Seattle Children’s Hospital, and has served as president of the American Society of Pediatric Nephrology, on the Working Group of the National High Blood Pressure Education Program, and as co-chair of an American Academy of Pediatrics committee focused on childhood hypertension. Dr. Flynn’s research interests involve the epidemiology and treatment of childhood hypertension, as well as cardiovascular complications of pediatric chronic kidney disease.

creators.name: Dr. Paul M. Brennan
creators.description: Paul M. Brennan, FRCS, FRCSEd, MRCS, PhD, is a senior lecturer in neurosurgery at the University of Edinburgh in Scotland, UK. He is also an honorary consultant neurosurgeon at NHS Lothian. Dr. Brennan’s primary research is focused on management of brain tumors and enhancing the use of the Glasgow Coma Scale.

creators.name: Dr. Qasim Aziz
creators.description: Qasim Aziz, MBBS, FRCP, PhD, is a professor of neurogastroenterology at the Queen Mary University of London in the UK. He has been awarded the British Society of Gastroenterology Research Gold Medal and the American Gastroenterology Association Janssen Award for Basic and Clinical Research. Dr. Aziz’s primary research is focused on the neurophysiological basis of human brain-gut communication and neuromodulation for management of visceral pain.

creators.name: Dr. Aris Garro
creators.description: Aris Garro, MD, MPH, is an associate professor of pediatrics and emergency medicine at the Warren Alpert Medical School of Brown University in Rhode Island. He works clinically at Hasbro Children’s Hospital Emergency Department, and in 2013, he won the Outstanding Physician Award from the University Emergency Medicine Foundation. Dr. Garro’s research interests include Lyme disease, meningitis, and asthma in pediatric patients.

creators.name: Dr. George J. Schwartz
creators.description: George J. Schwartz, MD, is chief of the nephrology division in the department of pediatrics at the University of Rochester Medical Center. He is also an elected member of the American Society for Clinical Investigation. Dr. Schwartz's research interests include acidosis and renal tubular disorders.

creators.name: Dr. Animesh Pardanani
creators.description: Animesh Pardanani, M.B.B.S., M.D., is a hematologist and oncologist at Mayo Clinic. He is board certified in internal medicine, medical oncology, and hematology, with a special interest in myeloproliferative neoplasms, systemic mastocytosis, and hypereosinophilic syndrome. Dr. Pardanani is a distinguished researcher who has received several awards and grants for his clinical and research excellence, and has published over 200 peer-reviewed articles, book chapters, and reviews.

creators.name: Dr. Bishoy Zakhary
creators.description: Bishoy M. Zakhary, MD, is an assistant professor of medicine in the division of pulmonary & critical care medicine at Oregon Health & Science University. He directs OHSU’s ECMO program and serves as chair of education for the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization. Dr. Zakhary is an ECMO-focused researcher investigating membrane lung dysfunction, extracorporeal life support education, and critical care outcomes.

creators.name: Dr. Alasdair M.J. MacLullich
creators.description: Alasdair M.J. MacLullich, BSc(Hons), MB ChB, MRCP(UK), PhD, is a professor of geriatrics at the University of Edinburgh in Scotland. His primary research interest is delirium, and he leads the Edinburgh Delirium Research Group. Dr. MacLullich co-founded the European Delirium Association in 2006 and is a past president of the association.

creators.name: Dr. Arash Mostaghimi
creators.description: Arash Mostaghimi, MD, MPA, MPH, is the director of Dermatology Inpatient Service and co-director of the Complex Medical Dermatology Fellowship Program at Brigham and Women's Hospital. He is also an associate professor at Harvard Medical School. Dr. Mostaghimi’s primary research is focused on severe drug reactions, cutaneous oncology, and medical dermatology.

creators.name: Dr. Charles G. Child
creators.description: Charles G. Child, MD, (d. 1991), was a professor emeritus of surgery at the University of Michigan and Emory University and was chairman of the department of surgery at University of Michigan. He was a founder of the organ-transplant program at Michigan during his tenure there, and he was editor of the Journal of Surgical Research and chairman of the American Board of Surgery. He was an active researcher in his field, investigating portal hypertension and other hepatic and gastrointestinal diseases. He published numerous studies and was co-author on multiple books.

creators.name: Dr. David G. Swain
creators.description: David G. Swain, MD, is a physician in the department of geriatric medicine at Yardley Green Hospital in Birmingham, UK. He is best known for modifying the 10-item Abbreviated Mental Test Score. Dr. Swain’s other research interests include cardiac enzymes in myocardial infarction.

creators.name: Dr. Manjunath Pai
creators.description: Leading expert on the Ideal Body Weight calculator: Manjunath Pai, PharmD, is a professor in the Department of Pharmacy Practice at the Albany College of Pharmacy. He is the author of “The Origin of the 'Ideal' Body Weight Equations”, a comprehensive literature review on the creation of and iterations to the ideal body weight formula over time. Dr. Pai conducts research on the optimization of antimicrobial drug dosing, most recently in the obese population.

creators.name: Dr. Paul Georg Lankisch
creators.description: Paul Georg Lankisch, MD, is a professor of medicine in the Peter A. Banks Department of General Internal Medicine and Gastroenterology at the Clinical Centre of Lüneburg, Germany. He is an active researcher on treatment, outcomes and pathways of acute pancreatitis.

creators.name: Dr. Saulo Klahr
creators.description: Saulo Klahr, MD, (d. 2010) was formerly the director of the Renal Division at Washington University. He received an award in 1994 from the American Association for the Advancement of Science for his research on the causes of kidney diseases and his leadership in the field of nephrology. His research focused on kidney disease and metabolism and regulatory control of fluids and electrolytes.

creators.name: Dr. Carolyn Snider
creators.description: Carolyn Snider, MD, MPH, FRCPC, is an emergency physician with the Winnipeg Health Region and a scientist at the Children’s Hospital Research Institute of Manitoba. She is also an associate professor at the University of Manitoba and founded the Emergency Department Violence Intervention Program (EDVIP) there. Dr. Snider’s primary research is focused on trauma care, youth violence, and intimate partner violence.

creators.name: Dr. Cédric Lukas
creators.description: Cédric Lukas, MD, PhD, is an associate professor of rheumatology at University Hospital Lapeyronie in Montpellier, France. He is a member of the EULAR Research Center in Montpellier. Dr. Lukas’ primary research is focused on autoimmune disease, inflammatory disease, and clinical rheumatology.

creators.name: Dr. Fengning Chuan
creators.description: Fengning Chuan, MD, is an endocrinologist and researcher at the First Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University in Chongqing, China. Dr. Chuan’s primary research is focused on treatment of diabetes and infectious diseases.

creators.name: Dr. Gearoid M. McMahon
creators.description: Gearoid M. McMahon, MD, MB, BCh, is a nephrologist at Brigham and Women's Hospital in Boston. He is also one of the editors of the popular nephrology resource Renal Fellow Network . Dr. McMahon’s research focuses primarily on acid-base disorders, acute renal failure, glomerular disease, and kidney stones.

creators.name: Dr. Heber MacMahon
creators.description: Heber MacMahon, MB, BCh, is the section chief of thoracic radiology and a professor of radiology at the University of Chicago Medicine. He is also a leader in the University of Chicago Comprehensive Cancer Center's Advanced Imaging Program. Dr. MacMahon’s primary research is focused on thoracic diagnostic radiology, lung cancer detection, and computer-aided diagnosis.

creators.name: Dr. Jaap Fransen
creators.description: Jaap Fransen, MD, is a senior researcher in rheumatology and professor of clinical research at the Radboud University Medical Center Nijmegen, the Netherlands. His research focuses on improving prognostication and treatment for rheumatic diseases including rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, gout and systemic sclerosis.

creators.name: Dr. Joel Dunning
creators.description: Joel Dunning, FRCS, PhD, is a practicing cardiothoracic surgeon at James Cook University Hospital in Middlesbrough, United Kingdom. He developed the CHALICE Rule as part of his PhD as a junior doctor. Dr. Dunning is an associate editor of the European Journal of Cardio-Thoracic Surgery and co-editor in chief of CTSNet.org.

creators.name: Dr. John H.C. Ranson
creators.description: John H. C. Ranson, MD, (d. 1995) was a surgeon and director of the division of general surgery at the NYU. He helped improve the treatment of pancreatitis and developed a widely used system for predicting the outcome of pancreatic disease. Dr. Ranson was the co-author of Acute Pancreatitis.

creators.name: Dr. Patrick D. Lyden
creators.description: Patrick D. Lyden, MD is chair of the Department of Neurology, Director of the Stroke Program and holds the Carmen and Louis Warschaw Chair in Neurology at Cedars-Sinai. Previously, he was a professor and vice chairman for clinical neurology at UCSD and served as the Clinical Chief of Neurology and Director of the Stroke Center at UCSD Medical Center. Dr. Lyden has published more than 200 journal articles and abstracts and edited a textbook on stroke intervention.

creators.name: Dr. Roland E. Andersson
creators.description: Roland E. Andersson, MD, PhD, is a colorectal surgeon at County Hospital Ryhov in Jönköping, Sweden. He is also a guest professor in the department of clinical and experimental medicine (IKE) at Linköping University in Linköping, Sweden. Dr. Andersson's research interests are primarily related to epidemiology, immunology, and diagnosis of appendicitis, genes associated with colorectal cancer, necrotizing enterocolitis, and risk of cancer and fertility problems associated with chronic inflammatory bowel diseases.

creators.name: Dr. Stephen J. Swensen
creators.description: Stephen J. Swensen, MD, FACR, is a radiologist and professor of radiology at Mayo Clinic. He is also the medical director of professionalism and peer support at Intermountain Healthcare in Utah. Dr. Swensen's research interests include thoracic radiology with a specific focus on lung cancer screening with CT and radiologic analysis of lung nodules and masses.

creators.name: Dr. Alberto Carmona-Bayonas
creators.description: Alberto Carmona-Bayonas, MD, PhD, is a medical oncologist in the department of hematology and medical oncology at Hospital General Universitario Morales Meseguer in Murcia, Spain. Dr. Carmona-Bayonas’ research interests include gastrointestinal cancers and febrile neutropenia.

creators.name: Dr. Alex Sagie
creators.description: Alex Saige, MD, is a cardiologist at the Edith Wolfson Medical Center in Israel. Previously, he was a researcher for the Framingham Heart Study in Boston, Massachusetts. Dr. Saige’s primary research is focused on heart valve diseases and transesophageal echocardiography.

creators.name: Dr. Phillip Mason
creators.description: Phillip E. Mason, MD, MS, is a clinical professor of anesthesiology at The University of Texas Health Science Center at San Antonio and medical director of the cardiothoracic and transplant ICU. He completed fellowships in critical care medicine (UPMC) and extracorporeal life support (Houston Methodist), and previously led the adult ECMO program at Brooke Army Medical Center during his U.S. Air Force career. Dr. Mason is an ECMO-focused researcher investigating membrane lung/oxygenator dysfunction, fluid management with CRRT during ECMO, and outcomes in extracorporeal life support.

creators.name: Leen Vercaemst
creators.description: Leen Vercaemst, RN, ECCP, is a senior clinical perfusionist at University Hospitals Leuven (UZ Leuven) and is affiliated with the anesthesiology & algology unit at KU Leuven. She serves as EuroELSO’s perfusion liaison, has served on the European Board of Cardiovascular Perfusion, and coordinates the Perfusion School Leuven training program. Ns. Vercaemst is an experienced ECMO/ECLS specialist researching and teaching extracorporeal life support, including membrane lung/oxygenator dysfunction and advances in ECLS technology and practice.

creators.name: Dr. Alex C. Spyropoulos
creators.description: Alex C. Spyropoulos, MD, FACP, FCCP, FRCPC, is a professor of medicine at the Donald and Barbara Zucker School of Medicine at Hofstra/Northwell in New York. He is also co-chair of the Council on Leadership of Thrombosis at Northwell Health and a fellow of the American College of Physicians. Dr. Spyropoulos' primary research is focused on the development of outpatient-based treatment of venous thromboembolic disease and other disease management protocols.

creators.name: Dr. Attilio Del Rosso
creators.description: Attilio Del Rosso, MD, is in the department of cardiology at S. Giuseppe Hospital in Empoli, Italy.

creators.name: Dr. Céline Gélinas
creators.description: Céline Gélinas, RN, PhD, is an associate professor at the Ingram School of Nursing, McGill University and a nurse scientist at the Lady Davis Institute of the Jewish General Hospital in Montréal. She evaluates nursing interventions as a co-lead of the Réseau de recherche en interventions en sciences infirmières du Québec (RRISIQ). Dr. Gélinas’ research focuses on critical care nursing and pain assessment, measurement and management.

creators.name: Dr. Donald McMillan
creators.description: Donald McMillan, MD, is a professor of surgical science at the University of Glasgow and an associate academic at the Institute of Cancer Sciences. His research focuses on systemic inflammatory response in weight loss and poor physical function, quality of life and survival of cancer patients.

creators.name: Dr. Fernando Alvarez
creators.description: Fernando Alvarez, MD, is the Chief of the Division of Gastroenterology, Hepatology & Nutrition at CHU Sainte-Justine, University of Montreal. He studied medicine in his home country of Argentina, where he focused on hepatology and pediatrics. He currently practices pediatric hepatology, and he researches topics including autoimmune hepatitis, viral hepatitis, and liver immunity.

creators.name: Dr. Narendra Singh
creators.description: Narendra Singh, MBBS, FRCPC, is the Chief of Staff at the Humber River Regional Hospital in Toronto, Ontario and the Doctors Hospital at Renaissance in Texas. Dr. Singh completed pediatric training at the University of Western Ontario and a fellowship in pediatric critical care at the Hospital for Sick Children and the Children’s Hospital of Pittsburgh. Previously, as Chief of Pediatrics, Dr. Singh’s leadership played a vital role in the Humber River Hospital Pediatric Program being named one of the top performing hospitals in Ontario for Pediatric Patient Experience. Dr. Singh is also the founder and driving force behind Guyana Help the Kids (GHTK), a charitable organization based in Toronto and dedicated to reducing infant mortality in Guyana.

creators.name: Dr. Xinxin Zhang
creators.description: Xinxin Zhang, MD, PhD, is a professor of infectious diseases at Shanghai Jiao Tong University in China. She is also vice chairman of the Shanghai Hepatology Society and has published over 160 papers, with contributions to journals like Gut and the Journal of Clinical Microbiology . Dr. Zhang’s primary research is focused on the pathology and treatment of various infectious diseases such as hepatitis and viral pneumonia.

creators.name: Dr. Alasdair MacLullich
creators.description: Alasdair MacLullich, BSc, MB ChB, MRCP(UK), PhD, FRCPE, is Professor of Geriatric Medicine at the University of Edinburgh and leads the Edinburgh Delirium Research Group. He co-developed the 4AT, which is recommended by NICE and has been validated in more than thirty studies and translated into >20 languages. He is Editor-in-Chief of the journal Delirium and chairs the Scottish Hip Fracture Audit.

creators.name: Dr. Christian Bénichou
creators.description: Christian Bénichou, MD, (d. 1999) was a rheumatologist and advocate for drug safety. He served as the head of drug safety at Roussel Uclaf in France, expert reviewer for the World Health Organization's Uppsala Monitoring Centre, and on all drug safety working groups for the Council for International Organizations of Medical Sciences (CIOMS). Dr. Bénichou’s research interests were primarily monitoring of drug safety.

creators.name: Dr. Clem Imrie
creators.description: Clem W. Imrie, MD, is a retired professor of surgery, formerly working at the Glasgow Royal Infirmary. He has received numerous awards for his research and practice involving pancreatitis, most recently the George E. Palade Prize of the International Association of Pancreatology. His research interests include the diagnosis, treatment and surgical techniques of Pancreato Biliary surgery.

creators.name: Dr. Joerg Hasford
creators.description: Joerg Hasford, MD, PhD, is a Professor of Medical Data Processing, Biometrics and Epidemiology at the University of Munich in Germany. He is the chairman of the Ethics Committee of the Bavarian Medical Association and the Working Group Medical Ethics Commissions in the Federal Republic of Germany. In 2000, he was awarded the Paul Martini Prize of the German Society of Medical computer science, Biometry and Epidemiology, Dr. Hasford has also published numerous articles and serves as an editor for Pharmacoepidemiology and Drug Safety publication.

creators.name: Dr. John Saltzman
creators.description: John Saltzman, MD, is a professor of medicine at Harvard Medical School. He currently serves as the Director of Endoscopy at Brigham and Women’s Hospital. His research focuses on on ERCP and endoscopic ultrasound/FNA.

creators.name: Dr. Pavan K. Bendapudi
creators.description: Pavan K. Bendapudi, MD, is an assistant professor of medicine at Harvard Medical School. Together with Dr. Robert Makar, he is co-principal investigator of the Harvard Thrombotic Microangiopathies Research Collaborative, an interdisciplinary, multi-institutional consortium that studies TTP and allied disorders. Dr. Bendapudi’s primary research is focused on humoral coagulation factors and the mechanisms underlying hemostatic and thrombotic disease.

creators.name: Dr. Raymond L. Benza
creators.description: Raymond L. Benza, MD, is a professor of medicine at Temple University College of Medicine. He is also the James Magovern Chair of Cardiovascular Research and a member of the executive committee of the Allegheny Heart Institute at Allegheny General Hospital. Dr. Benza’s primary research is focused on advanced congestive heart failure, cardiac transplantation, and pulmonary arterial hypertension.

creators.name: Martha V. Antonini
creators.description: Marta V. Antonini, CCP, CCN, MSc, is an adjunct lecturer at the University of Modena & Reggio Emilia. She is a cardiovascular perfusionist and ECMO specialist with the AUSL Romagna ECMO Team and a PhD researcher in cardio-nephro-thoracic sciences at the University of Bologna. Antonini is an active ECLS scholar investigating neurological care in ECMO, peripartum ECPR and organ-donation practices, and membrane-lung/oxygenator dysfunction.

creators.name: Dr. Anchalee Techanivate
creators.description: Anchalee Techanivate, MD, is an associate professor in the Department of Anesthesiology at King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital of Chulalongkorn University in Bangkok, Thailand.

creators.name: Dr. Ashwani K. Singal
creators.description: Ashwani K. Singal, MD, MS, FACG, FAASLD, is an associate professor of medicine and director of the UAB Porphyria Center at the University of Alabama. He is a leading expert on alcohol-related liver disease and lead author of the American College of Gastroenterology (ACG) clinical guideline on Alcoholic Liver Disease. Dr. Singal's clinical and research interests also include non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, porphyria, and acute kidney injury in cirrhosis.

creators.name: Dr. Daniel B. Mark
creators.description: Daniel B. Mark, MD, MPH, is a cardiologist and tenured professor of medicine at Duke University Medical Center. He is the vice chief for academic affairs in the division of cardiology and the director of outcomes research at the Duke Clinical Research Institute. Dr. Mark's primary research interests include medical economics and quality of life outcomes.

creators.name: Dr. Donald A. Mahler
creators.description: Donald A. Mahler, MD, is a professor emeritus at Geisel School of Medicine at Dartmouth in Hanover, New Hampshire. Clinically, he is a practicing pulmonologist and the director of respiratory services at Valley Regional Hospital in Claremont, NH. Dr. Mahler's research focus is management of COPD.

creators.name: Dr. Igor Frank
creators.description: Igor Frank, MD, is a professor of urology at the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, MN. Currently, he is the head of the Mayo Clinic bladder removal (cystectomy) registry. His research focuses mainly on treatment and prognosis of survival in bladder and prostate cancer, though he also researches continuity and quality of care for cancer patients.

creators.name: Dr. Joel Gore
creators.description: Joel Gore, MD, is a cardiologist at the UMass Memorial Medical Center, where he is also the Director of the Anticoagulation Clinic. He is a professor of Cardiovascular medicine at the University of Massachusetts Medical School and specializes in cardiac prevention. Dr. Gore earned his medical degree from the University of Calgary, and completed residency and fellowship at UMass Memorial Center. He is also board certified in Addiction Psychiatry and Internal Medicine.

creators.name: Dr. John Fisk
creators.description: John Fisk, MD, is an associate professor of psychiatry in the Department Psychology and Neuroscience at Dalhousie University in Canada. He is also the chair of the Clinical and Population Health Research Review Committee of the MS Society of Canada. Dr. Fisk’s research focuses on the epidemiology, cognitive symptoms and health-related quality of life issues in neurodegenerative diseases including multiple sclerosis, dementia, systemic lupus erythematosus and Parkinson’s disease.

creators.name: Dr. Josser Delgado Almandoz
creators.description: Josser Delgado Almandoz, MD, is a consulting neuroradiologist at Abbott Northwestern Hospital in Minneapolis, MN. He is an active researcher on topics including stroke intervention and other intracranial disease. He was a contributing author to the Training Guidelines for Endovascular Ischemic Stroke Intervention: An International Multi-Society Consensus Document , a consensus on stroke treatment training of 10 neurological disease societies around the world.

creators.name: Dr. Mark S. Silverberg
creators.description: Mark S. Silverberg, MD, PhD, FRCPC, is a professor of medicine at the University of Toronto in Canada. He is also the director of the Advanced IBD Fellowship Program at Mount Sinai in Toronto, Canada. Dr. Silverberg’s primary research is focused on genetics of inflammatory bowel disease.

creators.name: Dr. Nathalie Rioux-Leclercq
creators.description: Nathalie Rioux-Leclercq, MD is the head of the Pathological Anatomy and Cytology Service, part of the Department of Pathology and a professor of medicine at Rennes University Hospital in France. Her research focuses on renal cell carcinoma. prostatic adenocarcinoma, proliferation and apoptosis in the tumor process, and was lead author on the validation and reclassification of the Fuhrman Grade.

creators.name: Dr. Roberto Lorusso
creators.description: Roberto Lorusso, MD, PhD, is a full professor of cardiac surgery and extracorporeal life support at Maastricht University. He is ECLS program director and deputy director of the department of cardio-thoracic surgery at Maastricht University Medical Centre (MUMC+), and holds international leadership roles including honorary secretary of EuroELSO and chair of the ELSO Research Committee. Dr. Lorusso is a leading ECMO/ECLS researcher investigating membrane-lung dysfunction, ventricular unloading during ECMO, and outcomes in extracorporeal life support.

creators.name: Dr. Daniel Brodie
creators.description: Daniel Brodie, MD, is a professor of medicine at the Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine. He serves as vice president and chief medical officer for critical care at Johns Hopkins Health System and is the current president of ELSO as well as chair of the ECMONet board. Dr. Brodie is an internationally recognized researcher investigating the use of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) for respiratory and cardiac failure.

creators.name: Dr. Colin K. Grissom
creators.description: Colin K. Grissom, MD, FASE, is the associate medical director of the Shock Trauma Intensive Care Unit and director of Critical Care Echocardiography at Intermountain Medical Center in Utah. He is also a professor of medicine at the University of Utah. Dr. Grissom’s primary research is focused on mechanical ventilation, ARDS, sepsis, and echocardiography and ultrasound for critical care.

creators.name: Dr. Erin E. Krebs
creators.description: Erin E. Krebs, M.D., MPH, is a professor of medicine at the University of Minnesota. She is also the chief of general internal medicine at the VA Health Care System in Minneapolis, MN and the core investigator in the Center for Care Delivery and Outcomes Research. Dr. Krebs’s primary research is focused on chronic pain management and opioid therapy.

creators.name: Dr. Azlisham Mohd Nor
creators.description: Azlisham Mohd Nor, MD, is a practicing neurologist at Plymouth Hospital in the United Kingdom. He is also the director of the Plymouth Stroke Research Network. Dr. Nor’s research focuses primarily on neurology and stroke treatment.

creators.name: Dr. Brett Ley
creators.description: Brett Ley, MD, is a clinical fellow in the pulmonology department at UCSF School of Medicine. He is an active researcher on lung pathology with 2 active NIH grants and multiple published and peer reviewed papers. Dr. Ley’s research interests include interstitial lung diseases and prediction modeling.

creators.name: Dr. Bryan Jennett
creators.description: Bryan Jennett, MD, (d. 2008) was a neurosurgeon, professor of neurosurgery, and dean of medicine at the University of Glasgow in Scotland. In 1992, he was named Commander of the Order of the British Empire (CBE). Dr. Jennett’s primary research was focused on prognosis after head injury and criteria for brain death.

creators.name: Dr. Christian Peter Subbe
creators.description: Christian Peter Subbe, MD, MRCP (London), is a practicing clinician in Respiratory, General Internal & Intensive Care Medicine. He is a senior clinical lecturer at Bangor University and a consultant at the Ysbyty Gwynedd, Bangor. Dr. Subbe's current research interests include recognition of acute illness, the interface of acute and critical care medicine, rapid response systems and smoking cessation in hospitalized patients.

creators.name: Dr. Christos Carvounis
creators.description: Christos Carvounis MD, is an internist working at the Department of Internal Medicine, Kyanous Stavros Medical Center in Greece. He previously conducted research at at Nassau University Medical Center in the nephrology department.

creators.name: Dr. Margaret L. Campbell
creators.description: Margaret L. Campbell, PhD, RN, FPCN, is a professor emeritus of nursing at Wayne State University. She was the American Association of Critical-Care Nurses’ 2018 distinguished research lecturer. Dr. Campbell is an internationally recognized researcher investigating dyspnea assessment and treatment, ventilator withdrawal, and breathing comfort for critically ill and end-of-life patients.

creators.name: Castleman Disease Collaborative Network (CDCN)
creators.description: Castleman Disease Collaborative Network (CDCN) is a global research and patient network dedicated to accelerating research and treatment for Castleman disease by uniting patients, clinicians, and scientists, and leading collaborative programs such as the ACCELERATE natural-history registry. CDCN was founded in 2012 by Dr. David C. Fajgenbaum (co-founder & president of the scientific advisory board) and Dr. Frits van Rhee (co-founder & co-chair of the scientific advisory board).

creators.name: Dr. Annette H. van der Helm-van Mil
creators.description: Annette H. van der Helm-van Mil, MD, PhD, is a professor in the rheumatology department at Leiden University Medical Center, Netherlands. She is also a professor at Erasmus Medical Center in Rotterdam, Netherlands. Dr. van der Helm-van Mil’s primary research is focused on early arthritis, arthralgia, and imaging.

creators.name: Dr. Antonio Palumbo
creators.description: Antonio Palumbo is chief of the Myeloma Unit of the Department of Oncology, Section of Hematology at the University of Torino. He is currently a member of the Board of Directors of the International Myeloma Society. Dr. Palumbo's research focuses on plasma cell dyscrasia, and the pathogenesis and treatment of multiple myeloma.

creators.name: Dr. Anupam B. Kharbanda
creators.description: Anupam Kharbanda, MD, is a pediatric emergency medicine physician and Chief of Critical Care Services at Children's Minnesota. He has published numerous articles and several textbook chapters in the field of pediatric emergency medicine and he is nationally recognized for his work on developing clinical pathways for the management of pediatric appendicitis. Dr. Kharbanda currently co-leads a federally-funded multi-center study to implement appendicitis care pathways into the HealthPartners and Kaiser Northern California health systems, and additional current research areas include developing and implementing evidenced-based care pathways in order to enhance patient experience, improve quality of care, and minimize health care expenditures.

creators.name: Dr. Chelsea S. Kidwell
creators.description: Chelsea S. Kidwell, MD, is Professor of Neurology and Medical Imaging, Vice Chair of Research in the Department of Neurology, and a member of the Sarver Heart Center. She is also Co-Medical Director of the University of Arizona Medical Center (UAMC) certified Primary Stroke Center. Dr. Kidwell's clinical research focuses on innovative neuroimaging approaches directed at understanding stroke pathophysiology and treatment, reducing health disparities in stroke care, and advancing novel treatments for acute stroke including intracerebral hemorrhage.

creators.name: Dr. Christian J. Streck
creators.description: Christian J. Streck, MD, is professor of surgery and pediatrics and chief of the division of pediatric surgery at the Medical University of South Carolina. He is pediatric trauma medical director and vice chair of surgical education at MUSC, with research interests in pediatric trauma, minimally invasive surgery, and injury prevention.

creators.name: Dr. Shinobu Ishihara
creators.description: Shinobu Ishihara, MD, (d. 1963) was an army opthamologist in Tokyo, Japan. He was also the chairman of the ophthalmology department at the Imperial University of Tokyo. Dr. Ishihara’s research interests included isochromatic vision and myopia.

creators.name: Dr. Brent Graham
creators.description: Brent Graham, MD, FRCSC, is an assistant professor of plastic and reconstructive surgery at the University of Toronto. He serves as head of the hand program at the University Health Network, and is editor-in-chief of the Journal of Hand Surgery. Dr. Graham is a clinician-scientist researching carpal tunnel syndrome, peripheral nerve disorders, and clinical epidemiology in hand surgery.

creators.name: Dr. Andrew J. Karter
creators.description: Andrew J. Karter, PhD, is a research scientist at Kaiser Permanente Northern California. He is also an adjunct professor in the department of general internal medicine at UCSF and affiliate professor in the department of epidemiology at the University of Washington. Dr. Karter's research interests are focused on diabetes and its complications, including impacts on care from medication adherence, literacy, provider communications, IT, and language barriers.

creators.name: Dr. Cynthia Kelly
creators.description: Cynthia Kelly, MD, is a professor of pediatrics at Eastern Virginia Medical School. She has been the primary investigator for research funded by the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation, U.S. Departments of Health and Human Services, and Housing and Urban Development. Dr. Kelly’s clinical practice and research focuses on pediatric patients with allergic and immunologic disorders, including asthma, allergic rhinitis and others.

creators.name: Dr. Elliott M. Antman
creators.description: Elliott M. Antman, MD, is a professor and associate dean for Clinical/Translational Research at Harvard Medical School. He is also a senior physician in the Cardiovascular Division of the Brigham and Women's Hospital in Massachusetts and President of the American Heart Association (2014-2015). As a senior investigator in the TIMI Study Group, Dr. Antman has published on the use of serum cardiac markers for diagnosis and prognosis of patients with unstable angina and acute myocardial infarction, cyclooxygenase and cardiovascular risk, and antithrombotic therapy for acute coronary syndromes.

creators.name: Dr. Pedro Brugada
creators.description: Pedro Brugada, MD, PhD, is head of the cardiac arrhythmia unit at Hospital Estepona and the Heart Rhythm Management Centre at Brussels University Hospital in Brussels, Belgium. He has received the Gold Medal of the European Society of Cardiology for his work in cardiac arrhythmias. Dr. Brugada's primary research interests involve rhythmology and electrophysiology, and he has published over a thousand peer-reviewed articles and abstracts.

creators.name: Dr. Rebecca Scherzer
creators.description: Rebecca Scherzer, PhD, is an academic administrator at UCSF School of Medicine. She is a research statistician for the Fat Redistribution and Metabolic Change in HIV Infection study and for UCSF's Kidney Health Research Collaborative. Dr. Scherzer research and publications span topics including body composition, metabolic changes, kidney disease and HIV infection-related cardiovascular risk.

creators.name: Dr. Xavier Parent
creators.description: Xavier Parent, MD, is a biochemist at Hôpitaux Civils de Colmar in France. He has published many articles on topics related to electrolyte and ionic reactions in the body.

creators.name: Mr. Alan Monaghan
creators.description: Alan Monaghan, MSc, is a senior lecturer at the University of Brighton in the United Kingdom. His current research focuses on implementation of pediatric early warning scores in the community setting and has completed research on pediatric critical care nursing.

creators.name: Dr. Caleb R. S. McEntire
creators.description: Caleb R. S. McEntire, MD, is an assistant professor of neurology at Harvard Medical School. He is an attending neurologist at Massachusetts General Hospital and Brigham and Women’s Hospital. Dr. McEntire is an emerging researcher investigating neuroinfectious disease and neuroimmunology, with a specific focus on Lyme disease and complications of CAR-T cell therapy.

creators.name: Dr. A. P. Manning
creators.description: A. P. Manning, MD, is a physician at the Bristol Royal Infirmary in the United Kingdom. He published the derivation study for the Manning Criteria on IBS diagnosis during his time as a research fellow at Duke University.

creators.name: Dr. Dafna D. Gladman
creators.description: Dafna D. Gladman, MD, FRCPC, is a senior scientist at the Krembil Research Institute in Ontario, Canada. She is also the deputy director of the Centre for Prognosis Studies in The Rheumatic Diseases at Toronto Western Hospital. Dr. Gladman’s primary research is focused on psoriatic arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, and rheumatoid arthritis.

creators.name: Dr. Douglas Lee
creators.description: Douglas S. Lee, MD, PhD is a senior scientist at the Institute for Clinical Evaluative Sciences, University of Toronto in Ontario, Canada, where he is also an associate professor of cardiology. He currently practices cardiology at the Peter Munk Cardiac Centre and University Health Network. Dr. Lee's research focuses include cardiovascular disorders, diagnostic testing/imaging, and health technology assessment.

creators.name: Dr. Mary Ann Howland
creators.description: Mary Ann Howland, PharmD, is an adjunct professor at the Ronald O. Perelman Department of Emergency Medicine at NYU Langone Health and a clinical professor at the College of Pharmacy and Health Sciences at St. John's University. She specializes in clinical toxicology, poison control, and clinical toxicological management. Dr. Howland's work has been published in many books and journals, including Goldfrank's Toxicologic Emergencies .

creators.name: Dr. Mitchell L. Halperin
creators.description: Mitchell L. Halperin, MD, is a professor of medicine at University of Toronto. He is also an attending physician at St. Michael’s Hospital in Toronto, Canada. Dr. Halperin’s primary research is focused on renal physiology, acid base homeostasis, and metabolic regulation.

creators.name: Dr. Samuel B. Nadler
creators.description: Samuel B. Nadler, MD, (d. 1969) was the first head of the biophysics and nuclear medicine department at Touro Infirmary, later named the Nadler-Bloch Nuclear Medicine Department. He also served as the fifth president of the Southwestern Chapter of the Society of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging (SWC-SNMMI). Dr. Nadler is best known for his work with radioactive iodine and the thyroid.

creators.name: Jon A. Bell
creators.description: Jon A. Bell, MSN, RN, VA-BC, is principal at JABell Consulting LLC and practices as an emergency nurse at Mount Desert Island Hospital. Mr. Bell’s research interest centers on vascular access, IV insertion success, and clinical decision support tools in acute care settings.

creators.name: Dr. Harvey A. Skinner
creators.description: Harvey Skinner, PhD, is a professor of psychology and global health at York University. He holds the title of professor emeritus at the Dalla Lana School of Public Health, University of Toronto. Dr. Skinner is a registered psychologist in Ontario and a certified trainer in motivational interviewing. Dr. Skinner's expertise extends to behavior change interventions, eHealth promotion, and global health initiatives, where he has made pioneering contributions.

creators.name: Dr. Howard Vernon
creators.description: Howard Vernon, Ph.D., is a full professor at the University of Glamorgan, Canada. Dr. Vernon is an influential researcher investigating the mechanisms of cervical and lumbar spinal pain, with a particular focus on neck-related headache disability and the effects of the menstrual cycle on spinal joint mobility.

creators.name: Dr. Andrew Francis
creators.description: Andrew Francis, MD, PhD, is a professor of psychiatry at Penn State College of Medicine in Hershey, Pennsylvania. He is also the director of electroconvulsive therapy and associate director of residency training at Penn State. Dr. Francis’ primary research is focused on delirium and catatonia.

creators.name: Dr. Caroline H. Shiboski
creators.description: Caroline H. Shiboski, DDS, MPH, PhD, is the Leland A. and Gladys K. Barber distinguished professor of dentistry and professor of orofacial sciences at the University of California, San Francisco. She serves as principal investigator for the Sjögren’s International Collaborative Clinical Alliance (SICCA). Dr. Shiboski’s research focuses on Sjögren’s syndrome, particularly its oral manifestations, immune dysfunction, and salivary gland pathology.

creators.name: Dr. Fabricio O. Lima
creators.description: Fabricio O. Lima, MD, MPH, PhD, is a neurologist and faculty member at the department of neurology, Universidade de Fortaleza, Brazil. He is an applied, outcomes-oriented researcher investigating prehospital stroke systems, large vessel occlusion detection, and optimization of regional stroke networks.

creators.name: Dr. David X. Jin
creators.description: David X. Jin, MD, MPH, is an instructor at Harvard Medical School and practices gastroenterology, hepatology, and endoscopy at Brigham and Women’s Hospital / Faulkner Hospital in Boston and Jamaica Plain, MA. Dr. Jin is an analytical researcher specializing in gastroenterology and pancreatic disease prediction modeling.

creators.name: Dr. Sadiya S. Khan
creators.description: Sadiya S. Khan, MD, MS, is an associate professor of cardiology and preventive medicine at Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine. She directs work in cardiovascular risk prediction and prevention and leads initiatives integrating heart failure prevention into primary care. Dr. Khan is an accomplished researcher studying epidemiology, risk modeling, prevention of heart failure and cardiovascular disease.

creators.name: David Seaberg, MD
creators.description: David Seaberg, MD, CPE, FACEP, is a professor and dean of the University of Tennessee College of Medicine, Chattanooga and a practicing emergency physician. He is also Senior Vice President of the Erlanger Health System. Previously, he was the residency director and chair of the Department of Emergency Medicine at the University of Florida and served as president and chairman of the Board of the American College of Emergency Physicians. Dr. Seaberg has over 130 publications, book chapters and abstracts and has received numerous teaching and research awards.

creators.name: Dr. Amy Justice
creators.description: Amy Justice, MD, PhD, is the CNH Long Professor of Medicine and of Public Health at Yale University and a Staff Physician at the VA Connecticut Healthcare System. As principal investigator of the Veterans Aging Cohort Study (VACS), she has more than 20 years of experience developing and validating predictive indices using electronic health record data.

creators.name: Dr. Andrew Shorr
creators.description: Andrew Shorr, MD, MPH, is an associate director of pulmonary and critical care medicine and the chief of the Pulmonary Clinic at MedStar Washington Hospital Center in Washington, DC. Dr. Shorr's research interests include resistant pathogens and healthcare-associated bacteremia, and he has published more than 140 original studies.

creators.name: Dr. David Nathan
creators.description: David M. Nathan, MD, is director of the General Clinical Research Center and of the Diabetes Center at Massachusetts General Hospital. He is also a professor of medicine at Harvard Medical School. He is an active researcher with over 200 published articles and focuses on the development of innovative therapies to treat type 1 and type 2 diabetes and to prevent its long-term complications.

creators.name: Dr. Ewan H. Forrest
creators.description: Ewan H. Forrest, MD, practices and researches alcoholic liver disease and portal hypertension in the Department of Gastroenterology at the Glasgow Royal Infirmary. He is also an honorary clinical senior lecturer at the University of Glasgow School of Medicine. Dr. Forrest completed a Fellowship at the Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh, researching haemodynamic derangement of chronic liver disease.

creators.name: Dr. Gabrielle Silver
creators.description: Gabrielle Silver, MD, is a practicing child and adolescent psychiatrist at New York Presbyterian Hospital. She is also a clinical associate professor of psychiatry at the Weill Cornell Medical College. Dr. Silver’s primary research is focused on screening critically ill children for delirium.

creators.name: Dr. Paul Y. Kwo
creators.description: Paul Y. Kwo, MD, is a professor of medicine and the director of hepatology at Stanford University. He co-authored the American College of Gastroenterology's clinical practices guidelines on Abnormal Liver Chemistries, and is on the editorial board of the Journal of Clinical Gastroenterology. Dr. Kwo has been named one of the best doctors in America in gastroenterology and hepatology for 15 years.

creators.name: Dr. Richard Body
creators.description: Richard Body, MB ChB, MRCSEd (A&E), FRCEM, PhD, is an emergency medicine professor and honorary consultant in emergency medicine at the University of Manchester in the UK. He is also the founder of the Manchester Acute Coronary Syndromes (MACS) Academic Group and the Manchester Emergency Medicine and Intensive Care Research Group (EMERGING). Dr. Body’s primary research is focused on early diagnosis of acute coronary syndromes.

creators.name: Dr. Sachin Vaid
creators.description: Sachin Vaid, MD, MS, MRCS, FACS, FASCRS, is a general and colorectal surgeon at the Christiana Institute of Advanced Surgery (CHRIAS). He is also a clinical assistant professor at Thomas Jefferson University Hospital. Dr. Vaid’s primary research is focused on laparoscopic and robotic colorectal surgery.

creators.name: Dr. Sattva S. Neelapu
creators.description: Sattva S. Neelapu, MD, is a hematologist-oncologist at The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center. He is a translational researcher focused on lymphoma immunotherapy, chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, and management of treatment-related toxicities. Dr. Neelapu is an internationally recognized investigator whose work has advanced the clinical application and safety of CAR T-cell therapies.

creators.name: Dr. Barbara Braden
creators.description: Barbara Braden, PhD, was the dean of the Graduate School (1995-2006) and the College of Professional Studies (2002-2011) at Creighton University in Omaha, Nebraska. She also established the Lois Turner and Odessie Taylor Endowed Scholarship in honor of two African American women who were pioneers in the field of nursing. Dr. Braden’s primary research focused on the development of the Braden Scale, a method for identifying patients at risk for pressure ulcers (bedsores).

creators.name: Dr. John F. Murray
creators.description: John F. Murray, MD, is professor emeritus of medicine at the University of California in San Francisco. He served as chief of the pulmonary and critical care division at San Francisco General Hospital. Dr. Murray’s research interests are focused on pulmonology.

creators.name: Dr. Michael Farris
creators.description: Michael Farris, MD, is a radiation oncologist at the Wake Forest School of Medicine in North Carolina. Dr. Farris’ primary research is focused on lung cancer as well as stereotactic radiosurgery for brain metastases.

creators.name: Dr. Qing Yu Christina Weng
creators.description: Qing Yu Christina Weng, MD, is an instructor in dermatology at Harvard Medical School and dermatologist at the Massachusetts General Hospital. Her primary research focuses on melanocyte biology and pigment dysregulation.

creators.name: Dr. Sherman A. Less
creators.description: Sherman A. Lee, PhD, is an associate professor of psychology at Christopher Newport University in Virginia. He is actively researching COVID-19 associated anxiety and has developed the first medical screening tools for the condition. Dr. Lee’s primary research is focused on negative feeling states and the influence of personality and religion on those experiences.

creators.name: Dr. Thomas Killip III
creators.description: Thomas Killip III, MD, is a professor of medicine and cardiology at Mount Sinai Beth Israel Hospital in New York City. He has published dozens of studies in cardiology since the 1960s. Dr. Killip is best known for the heart failure classification system that bears his name.

creators.name: Dr. Andreas Greinacher
creators.description: Andreas Greinacher, MD, is the head of the Institute of Immunology and Transfusion Medicine at the University Hospital Greifswald, Germany. He has interests in hereditary and acquired platelet disorders, bridging immuno-hematology and hemostasis. His recent work is on adopting nanotechnology and biophysical methods to investigate platelets and protein changes.

creators.name: Dr. David Leaper
creators.description: David Leaper, MD, ChM, DSc, FRCS, FACS, FLS, is an emeritus professor of clinical sciences at the Institute of Skin Integrity and Infection Prevention at the University of Huddersfield and emeritus professor of surgery at the University of Newcastle upon Tyne. He has served as president of the Surgical Infection Society of Europe and the European Wound Management Association. Dr. Leaper’s primary research interests include surgical site infection, sepsis and critical care, and wound healing.

creators.name: Dr. Frank A. Manning
creators.description: Frank A. Manning, MD, is a professor of obstetrics and gynecology and associate director of the maternal-fetal medicine division at New York Medical College. His research interests include fetal ultrasound and in utero fetal therapy. Dr. Manning is the author of seven books including Sonography in Obstetrics & Gynecology Principles and Practice .

creators.name: Dr. Ioannis Psallidas
creators.description: Ioannis Psallidas, MD, PhD, is an honorary consultant respiratory physician at Oxford University Hospital NHS Foundation Trust. He is also the medical science director at AstraZeneca. Dr. Psallidas’ primary research is focused on pleural disease and lung cancer.

creators.name: Dr. Jesse M. Cedarbaum
creators.description: Jesse M. Cedarbaum, MD, is the vice-president of neurology early clinical development at Biogen. He is also an adjunct professor of psychiatry at Yale School of Medicine. Dr. Cedarbaum’s primary research is focused on neuromuscular and neurodegenerative diseases, as well as psychiatric and ophthalmological disorders.

creators.name: Dr. Najib M. Rahman
creators.description: Najib M. Rahman, BM BCh, PhD, is a consultant and senior lecturer in respiratory medicine in the Nuffield Department of Medicine in Oxford, United Kingdom. His research interests are in pleural infection and pleural malignancy. Dr. Rahman leads pleural trials and trials methodology at the Oxford Respiratory Trials Unit (ORTU).

creators.name: Dr. Alexander C. Fanaroff
creators.description: Alexander C. Fanaroff, MD, is a cardiologist and chief fellow at the Duke Clinical Research Institute. He is a recipient of the American Heart Association (AHA) Fellow-to-Faculty Transition Award. Dr. Fanaroff’s primary research interests are in interventional cardiology and course of care for patients with cardiovascular illnesses.

creators.name: Dr. Oriol Roca
creators.description: Oriol Roca, MD PhD, is a critical care specialist at the Vall d'Hebron University Hospital in Barcelona, Spain. Dr. Roca’s primary research is focused on clinical predictors and respiratory support success in acute respiratory distress syndrome.

creators.name: Dr. Prateek Sharma
creators.description: Prateek Sharma, MD, is an associate professor of medicine in the division of gastroenterology and hepatology, and is affiliated with the University of Kansas Medical Center and Kansas City VA Medical Center. He is a fellow of the American College of Gastroenterology and the American College of Physicians, has served as the Chair of the American College of Gastroenterology Public Relations Committee and American Gastroenterology Association ABIM Subcommittee, and is a member of the American Society Gastrointestinal Endoscopy Research Committee. Dr. Sharma's research interests include upper gastrointestinal diseases, such as Barrett's esophagus, esophageal cancer, and gastroesophageal reflux disease, and he has received the American College of Gastroenterology Governors Award for Excellence in Clinical Research. He has published more than 80 original articles and book chapters in this field, and co-edited the book Barrett's Esophagus & Esophageal Adenocarcinoma.

creators.name: Dr. Shirley B. Lansky
creators.description: Shirley B. Lansky, MD, was a clinical oncologist and researcher at the University of Illinois. She was formerly the director of the Illinois Cancer Center. Dr. Lansky’s research focus was on improving functional status and ability of pediatric cancer patients.

creators.name: Dr. James V. Hennessey
creators.description: James V. Hennessey, MD, is a professor of medicine in the division of endocrinology at Harvard Medical School and practicing endocrinologist at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston. He has published extensively on thyroid hormone therapy, levothyroxine formulation, and bioequivalence issues. Dr. Hennessey is a dedicated researcher focused on optimizing hypothyroidism treatment, levothyroxine dosing strategies, and assessing generic versus brand-name thyroid replacement therapy.

creators.name: Dorothea W. Barthel, PT
creators.description: Dorothea W. Barthel, PT, (d. 2003) was an American physical therapist, best known for creating the eponymous Barthel Index with Dr. Florence Mahoney in 1965. The Barthel Index is one of the most widely-used assessments of functional independence.

creators.name: Dr. Adrian Haimovich
creators.description: Adrian Haimovich, MD, PhD, is a resident in the department of emergency medicine at Yale University in Connecticut. He is also a member of the Yale Emergency Scholars (YES) program. Dr. Haimovich's primary research is focused on machine learning and big data in the context of emergency medicine.

creators.name: Dr. Santiago Mintegi
creators.description: Santiago Mintegi, MD, PhD, is a pediatric emergency physician and quality manager at Cruces University Hospital in Bilbao, Spain. He also serves as a member of the Research in European Pediatric Emergency Medicine (REPEM) network. Dr. Mintegi's research interests include pediatric bacterial infections, febrile infants, and decision tools.

creators.name: Dr. Sylvie Bastuji-Garin
creators.description: Sylvie Bastuji-Garin, MD, PhD, is a dermatologist and epidemiologist affiliated with Hôpital Henri-Mondor / Université Paris-Est Créteil (AP-HP), France, working at the intersection of dermatology, public health, and prognostic modeling. She co-developed the SCORTEN severity-of-illness score for toxic epidermal necrolysis and has published extensively in prognostic analytics for severe cutaneous adverse reactions. Dr. Bastuji-Garin is a respected researcher in dermatologic epidemiology and clinical prognostic scoring in severe dermatologic disease.

creators.name: Amy C. Justice, MD, PhD
creators.description: Amy Justice, MD, PhD, is the CNH Long Professor of Medicine and of Public Health at Yale University and a Staff Physician at the VA Connecticut Healthcare System. As principal investigator of the Veterans Aging Cohort Study (VACS), she has more than 20 years of experience developing and validating predictive indices using electronic health record data.

creators.name: Dr. Robert Rodriguez
creators.description: Robert Rodriguez, MD, is a professor of clinical emergency medicine and the residency research director at UCSF School of Medicine. He is also an attending emergency room physician. Dr. Rodriguez's research interests include deriving decision instruments for imaging in blunt trauma, critical care in the ED, infectious disease presentations to the ED, homeless and immigrant population access and care in the ED, and defensive medicine.

creators.name: Dr. Andrew S. Levey
creators.description: Andrew S. Levey, MD, is the chief of the nephrology division at Tufts Medical Center and the Dr. Gerald J. and Dorothy R. Friedman Professor at Tufts University School of Medicine. His clinical interests include chronic kidney disease (CKD), diabetic kidney disease, and systemic lupus erythematosus. Dr. Levey’s research focuses on laboratory measures to estimate kidney function, new therapies, and the development of clinical practice guidelines for CKD.

creators.name: Dr. Armando Giuliano
creators.description: Armando Giuliano, MD, is a clinician and investigator appointed as the Linda and Jim Lippman Chair in surgical oncology. He is also co-director of the Saul and Joyce Brandyman Breast Center at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center. Dr. Giuliano’s primary research is focused on treatment of breast cancer.

creators.name: Dr. Sanjay Kakar
creators.description: Sanjay Kakar, MD, is the chief of GI-hepatobiliary pathology service and director of the GI-hepatobiliary pathology fellowship program at the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF). He is also a professor of pathology at UCSF. Dr. Kakar’s primary research is focused on GI, liver, and pancreatic pathology and staging of GI and hepatobiliary cancers.

creators.name: The Rome Foundation
creators.description: The Rome Foundation is an independent not for profit 501(c) 3 organization that provides support for activities designed to create scientific data and educational information to assist in the diagnosis and treatment of Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction (DGBI), also known as functional gastrointestinal (GI) disorders. Their mission is to improve the lives of people with DGBI. Over the last 3 decades, the Rome organization has sought to legitimize and update our knowledge of the DGBIs. This has been accomplished by bringing together scientists and clinicians from around the world to classify and critically appraise the science of GI function and dysfunction. This knowledge permits clinical scientists to make recommendations for diagnosis and treatment that can be applied in research and clinical practice. Diagnosis is based on the use of symptom-based criteria which are used in clinical trials and daily practice.
