creators.name: Dr. John Betteridge
creators.description: John Betteridge, BSc, MB BS, PhD, MD, FRCP, FAHA, (d. 2019) was an endocrinologist at University College London. He was a past chairman of HEART UK and past president of the Council on Lipids in Clinical Medicine at The Royal Society of Medicine. Professor Betteridge was an active researcher with over 300 publications in peer-reviewed journals, with a focus in diabetes and lipid management.

creators.name: Dr. Philip Urban
creators.description: Philip Urban, MD, is an interventional cardiologist at Hôpital de la Tour, Geneva, Switzerland, and medical co-director of the Centre Européen de Recherche Cardiovasculaire (CERC) in Massy, France. He has published extensively on coronary stenting in patients at high bleeding risk and led the consensus work for the ARC‑HBR Criteria. Dr Urban is a prominent researcher investigating bleeding versus thrombotic risk trade-offs after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).

creators.name: Dr. John Carl Hoefs
creators.description: John Carl Hoefs, MD, is a Professor of Medicine at University of California Irvine. He studied medicine at George Washington University in Washington DC. He currently practices and researches in the hepatology field, specifically regarding Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, Ascites, Chronic liver disease, Liver-spleen scan and Hepatic function.

creators.name: Dr. Francesco Costa
creators.description: Francesco Costa, MD, PhD, MSc, FESC, is an interventional cardiologist at Hospital Universitario Virgen de la Victoria in Málaga, Spain, and an honorary professor at IBIMA and the University of Málaga. He also serves as an assistant professor of cardiology at the University of Messina in Italy and is a member of the editorial boards of PCR Online and Circulation: Cardiovascular Interventions . Dr. Costa is a distinguished researcher investigating antithrombotic therapy, ischemic and bleeding risk assessment, and clinical outcomes following percutaneous coronary intervention.

creators.name: Heart Failure Association-International Cardio-Oncology Society (HFA ICOS)
Dr. Andrew Wang
creators.description: Andrew Wang, MD, is a Professor of Medicine (Cardiology) at Duke University Hospital and specializes in treating patients with heart valve disease, such as aortic or mitral valve conditions, as well as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. His clinical research is focused on the effect of therapies on outcome for these conditions. He has led multiple research studies on the use and effect of surgery in endocarditis, which have been supported by the American Heart Association. He is dedicated to educating future cardiologists and has served as the program director for the Duke Cardiovascular Disease Fellowship since 2007, and worked on educational initiatives with the American College of Cardiology and American College of Physicians.

creators.name: Dr. William Kannel
creators.description: William Kannel, MD, MPH, (d. 2011) was a professor of medicine and public health at Boston University. He was also director of the Visiting Scientist Program at the Framingham Heart Study. Dr. Kannel published hundreds of peer reviewed studies, and coined the term “risk factors”.

creators.name: Dr. Dennis G. Moledina
creators.description: Dennis G. Moledina, MD, PhD, FASN, is an associate professor in the department of internal medicine (section of nephrology) at the Yale School of Medicine. He is a board-certified physician-scientist in internal medicine with a sub-specialization in nephrology. Dr. Moledina is an innovative researcher focused on developing diagnostic tests and tools for various subtypes of acute kidney injury, particularly in improving non-invasive diagnosis of acute interstitial nephritis. He is an investigator in NIH-funded multicenter consortia including Kidney Precision Medicine Program (KPMP) and Care of Outpatients with Acute Kidney Injury (COPE-AKI). He directs the Yale Kidney BioBank which is a biorepository that has collected samples from over 1200 participants with kidney biopsy confirmed diagnoses.

creators.name: Dr. Grégoire Le Gal
creators.description: Grégoire Le Gal, MD, PhD, is a professor in the Division of Hematology at the University of Ottawa, a physician in the Thrombosis Program at Ottawa Hospital, and a Senior Scientist in the Ottawa Hospital Research Institute, Clinical Epidemiology Program. He has 330 peer-reviewed publications and research interests include the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism (VTE) and the derivation and validation of clinical decision rules for VTE.

creators.name: Dr. John F. Morgan
creators.description: John F. Morgan, MD, is a senior lecturer at St. George's University of London and a visiting professor at Leeds Met University, UK. He is an internationally recognized consultant psychiatrist specializing in adult psychiatry and eating disorders. Dr. Morgan is a distinguished researcher who has published over 70 peer-reviewed papers and six books, and his special interests include neuropsychiatry, adult autism spectrum disorders, and the psychological consequences of physical disorders.

creators.name: Dr. Andrea Sikora
creators.description: Andrea Sikora, PharmD, MSCR, BCCCP, FCCM, FCCP is an Associate Professor at the University of Colorado School of Medicine in the Department of Biomedical Informatics and adjunct faculty at the University of Georgia (UGA) College of Pharmacy. Dr. Sikora graduated from UGA College of Pharmacy, completed her PGY1 Pharmacy Residency and PGY2 Critical Care Pharmacy Residency at the University of North Carolina (UNC) Medical Center in Chapel Hill, NC, and completed her Master of Science in Clinical Research from Emory University. She has received several federal grants evaluating applications of artificial intelligence for optimized medication use in the intensive care unit (ICU) and is an author of the book Pay It Forward: A Map to Mentorship in Medicine and InteGREAT: How to make great healthcare teams. See other publications here .

creators.name: Dr. Sarayut Janmahasatian
creators.description: Sarayut Janmahasatian, PhD, is an associate professor in the Department of Biomedicine and Health Informatics at the Faculty of Pharmacy, Silpakorn University. He has been actively involved in various research projects, focusing on health informatics and pharmaceutical sciences. Dr. Janmahasatian's research primarily explores biomedicine, health informatics, and the development of innovative pharmaceutical solutions​.

creators.name: Dr. David E Leaf
creators.description: David E. Leaf, MD, MMSc, is an Associate Professor of Medicine at Harvard Medical School and Director of Clinical and Translational Research in Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) in the Division of Renal Medicine at Brigham and Women’s Hospital. Dr. Leaf’s primary research interests are in AKI, including its epidemiology, pathophysiology, and development of therapies for its prevention and treatment.

creators.name: Dr. Mohamed Hassanein
creators.description: Mohamed Hassanein, MD, is a senior consultant in endocrinology and diabetes at Dubai Hospital, Dubai, UAE. He also serves as the chair of the Diabetes and Ramadan (DAR) International Alliance. Dr. Hassanein is a prominent researcher focusing on diabetes and Ramadan, having co-authored recommendation papers for the American Diabetes Association and the British Medical Journal, and published over 100 papers with more than 50 presentations at national and international meetings.

creators.name: Dr. William H. Polonsky
creators.description: William H. Polonsky, PhD, is an associate clinical professor in psychiatry at the University of California, San Diego, and the president and founder of the Behavioral Diabetes Institute. Dr. Polonsky is a distinguished researcher focusing on behavioral diabetes, investigating topics such as quality of life in diabetes, diabetes-related distress and depression, hypoglycemic fear, and glucose monitoring behavior and attitudes.

creators.name: Dr. Thomas H. Lee
creators.description: Thomas H. Lee, MD, is the chief medical officer at Press Ganey, Inc., where he leads clinical and operational strategies to enhance patient experience by reducing suffering and improving care value. He is also an internist and cardiologist practicing at Brigham and Women's Hospital in Boston and serves as a professor of medicine at Harvard Medical School.

creators.name: Dr. John L. Cox
creators.description: John L. Cox, MD, is professor emeritus of psychiatry at Keele University and former president of the Royal College of Psychiatrists. Dr. Cox is a prominent researcher focusing on perinatal mental health and transcultural psychiatry, with international recognition for his work, including serving as Secretary General of the World Psychiatric Association​.

creators.name: Dr. John M. Guenst
creators.description: John Guenst, MD, is an internist and aviation medical examiner with the St. Thomas Medical Group in Nashville. Dr. Guenst is a dedicated researcher and clinician, focusing on preventative medicine and geriatrics, and has extensive experience in internal medicine and emergency care.

creators.name: Dr. Martin Aringer
creators.description: Martin Aringer, MD, is a professor of rheumatology at the University Hospital Carl Gustav Carus Dresden. He has received prestigious awards including the Young Investigators Award from the European League Against Rheumatism and the Austrian State Prize for basic research in rheumatology. Dr. Aringer is a distinguished researcher focusing on rheumatoid arthritis, systemic sclerosis, and systemic lupus erythematosus.

creators.name: Dr. Ben W. Sedrine
creators.description: Ben W. Sedrine, MS, is a researcher affiliated with the WHO Collaborating Center for Public Health Aspects of Osteoarticular Disorders, and the department of epidemiology and public health at the University of Liège, Belgium. Her research focuses on osteoarticular disorders, particularly osteoporosis, including the economic and health impacts of fractures.

creators.name: Dr. Walter F. Stewart
creators.description: Walter F. Stewart, PhD, is an adjunct professor at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health. He has a distinguished career in healthcare delivery research and development, with expertise in digital solutions, machine learning, and practice-based rapid learning. Dr. Stewart is an accomplished researcher on a variety of topics including analgesics, internal medicine, and psychiatry, including research on migraine and headache, with over 400 publications.

creators.name: Dr. Shruti Gupta
creators.description: Shruti Gupta MD, MPH, is an Assistant Professor of Medicine at Harvard Medical School and Director of Onconephrology at Brigham and Women’s Hospital and Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Dr. Gupta carries out epidemiologic, translational, and interventional studies aimed at preventing and mitigating kidney-related complications in patients with cancer.

creators.name: Dr. Jacob D. Soumerai
creators.description: Jacob D. Soumerai, MD, is an assistant professor of medicine at Harvard Medical School and an assistant in medicine in the Hematology/Oncology department at Massachusetts General Hospital. He is an active clinician-investigator at the Mass General Research Institute Cancer Center, focusing on lymphoma, cellular immunotherapy, and hematology/oncology. Dr. Soumerai is a leading researcher in clinical trials and targeted therapies for hematologic malignancies, with a particular interest in relapsed or refractory chronic lymphocytic leukemia.

creators.name: The CKD Epidemiology Collaboration (CKD-EPI)
creators.description: The CKD Epidemiology Collaboration ( CKD - EPI ) is a research group with interests in measurement and estimation of GFR ( CKD - EPI GFR) and evaluation of surrogate endpoints for clinical trials in CKD ( CKD - EPI CT). CKD - EPI was founded by Dr. Andrew S. Levey who served as Director from 2004 to 2018 and continues to serve as co-director. Dr. Lesley A. Inker has been the Director of the Data Coordinating Center (DCC) from 2004 and Co-Director since 2018.

creators.name: Dr. James D. Douketis
creators.description: Dr. James D. Douketis is a staff physician in general internal medicine and clinical thromboembolism at St. Joseph’s Healthcare Hamilton and a professor of medicine at McMaster University, where he holds the David Braley-Nancy Gordon Chair in Thromboembolic Disease. His expertise focuses on perioperative anticoagulant management and venous thromboembolism, with significant contributions to clinical guidelines and over 350 peer-reviewed publications. Dr. Douketis also serves in multiple editorial roles, including Editor-in-Chief of the Canadian Journal of General Internal Medicine and Deputy Editor of the Annals of Internal Medicine.

creators.name: Dr. John S. Cacciola
creators.description: John S. Cacciola, PhD, is an adjunct associate professor of psychology in psychiatry at the Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania and a senior scientist at the Treatment Research Institute (TRI). His expertise lies in substance abuse research, focusing on diagnostic and psychosocial assessment, treatment outcomes, and co-occurring disorders. Dr. Cacciola has played a key role in developing tools like the Addiction Severity Index (ASI) and the Treatment Services Review (TSR).

creators.name: Dr. Simon Kraler
creators.description: Simon Kraler, MD PhD FESC is a clinician at the Cantonal Hospital Baden and translational scientist at the University of Zurich with a specific expertise/interest in novel strategies to personalize the management of patients with acute coronary syndromes. He has identified several novel biomarkers and was centrally involved in the development of pioneering risk prediction models, including but not limited to the GRACE 3.0 and the SEX-SHOCK score.

creators.name: Dr. Navdeep Tangri
creators.description: Navdeep Tangri, MD, PhD, FRCPC, is a physician and medical researcher at Seven Oaks General Hospital in Winnipeg, Canada. He is also an associate professor in the nephrology division at the University of Manitoba in Canada. Dr. Tangri's primary research is focused on the epidemiology of chronic kidney disease and end-stage renal disease.

creators.name: Dr. Tom Hartley
creators.description: Tom Hartley, MD, is a consultant in respiratory and general medicine at Northumbria Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust. His clinical and research expertise focuses on interstitial lung disease (ILD), sleep-disordered breathing, and non-invasive ventilation (NIV), particularly in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

creators.name: Dr. Yifan Wang
creators.description: Yifan Wang, MD, is currently a PhD student at the University of Zurich, Center for Molecular Cardiology (CMC). Her research is primarily focused on clinical studies in cardiovascular diseases, with specialized expertise in applying machine learning to risk prediction modeling and the discovery of novel biomarkers.

creators.name: Dr. Francesco Passamonti
creators.description: Francesco Passamonti, MD, is the head of the hematology department at the Circolo Hospital and Macchi Foundation, in Varese, Italy. Previously, he was an assistant professor of hematology at the University of Pavia in Pavia, Italy. Dr. Passamonti’s research focuses primarily on Philadelphia-negative myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN), polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia, and myelofibrosis.

creators.name: Dr. Yoshifumi Saisho
creators.description: Yoshifumi Saisho, MD, PhD, is an adjunct lecturer of internal medicine at Keio University. He is also a clinical associate professor at Kyorin University School of Medicine and the director of Saisho Diabetes Clinic. Dr. Saisho is an accomplished researcher investigating diabetology, with a particular focus on beta cell dysfunction in diabetes, and has published over 160 papers.

creators.name: Dr. Alexander B. Wallace
creators.description: Alexander B. Wallace, CBE FRSE FRCSE, was a founding member and president of the British Association of Plastic Surgeons. He was also the first editor of the British Journal of Plastic Surgery and played a leading role in burns and plastic surgery. Dr. Wallace was a pioneering researcher in the field of burn classification and treatment.

creators.name: Dr. Björn Strander
creators.description: Björn Strander, MD, is an associate professor of obstetrics and gynecology at the University of Gothenburg. He has played key roles in national coordination and development of cervical cancer screening programs. Dr. Strander is a distinguished researcher investigating cervical cancer prevention, HPV vaccination, and colposcopy, and he continues to be an active gynecologist and researcher, leading international studies on HPV vaccination in the treatment of cervical cell changes.

creators.name: Dr. Adalgisa Condoluci
creators.description: Adalgisa Condoluci, PhD, is a postdoctoral research scientist at the Institute for Cancer Genetics at Columbia University. She is also a recognized researcher who received the ASH Global Research Award from the American Society of Hematology for her contributions to hematology. Dr. Condoluci’s research primarily focuses on utilizing liquid biopsy techniques to improve therapeutic outcomes in patients with early-stage Hodgkin lymphoma, aiming to reduce treatment toxicity and prevent relapse.

creators.name: Dr. Vance G. Fowler Jr.
creators.description: Vance G. Fowler Jr., MD, MHS, is the Florence McAlister Distinguished Professor of Medicine at Duke University and a professor in both the departments of medicine and molecular genetics and microbiology. Dr. Fowler is a leading researcher in infectious diseases, particularly focusing on the pathogenesis of bacterial infections, antibiotic resistance, and the determinants of outcomes in patients with Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia.

creators.name: Dr. John R. Knight
creators.description: John R. Knight, MD, is an associate professor of pediatrics at Harvard Medical School (HMS) and the founder of the Center for Adolescent Substance Use and Addiction Research (CeASAR) at Boston Children’s Hospital. He is renowned for his research on adolescent substance use screening and treatment, supported by major organizations including the National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism (NIAAA) and the National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA). Dr. Knight's prolific publications and numerous awards highlight his significant contributions to medical education and substance abuse research.

creators.name: Dr. David S. Greenes
creators.description: David S. Greenes, MD, is a distinguished pediatrician affiliated with Boston Children's Hospital and Needham Pediatrics in Massachusetts. He has held significant roles, including associate director of the pediatrics residency program and attending physician in the emergency department at Boston Children's Hospital. An accomplished researcher, he has authored numerous publications in medical literature, contributing extensively to pediatric emergency medicine.

creators.name: Dr. Omar Y. Bello-Chavolla
creators.description: Omar Y. Bello Chavolla, Ph.D., is an assistant professor at the National Institute for Geriatrics in Mexico City and an instructor in physiology and applied biostatistics at the National Autonomous University Faculty of Medicine in Mexico. He is also a Lown Scholar at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health. Dr. Bello Chavolla is a dedicated researcher investigating cardiovascular disease risk factor epidemiology in high burden settings, focusing on the intersection of these risk factors with aging in metabolic and endocrine systems.

creators.name: Dr. Jerome A. Yesavage
creators.description: Jerome A. Yesavage, MD, is a professor of psychiatry and behavioral sciences at Stanford University School of Medicine and a professor of neurology. Dr. Yesavage is a distinguished researcher focused on Alzheimer's disease, geriatric psychiatry, and cognitive decline, with his work significantly advancing the understanding of neurodegenerative disorders and improving treatment strategies for veterans and the elderly.

creators.name: Dr. William C. Mentzer
creators.description: William C. Mentzer, MD, is a pediatric hematologist-oncologist at UCSF Benioff Children’s Hospitals in San Francisco. Dr. Mentzer is an experienced researcher investigating diseases of the blood, spleen, and lymph glands in children, focusing on conditions such as anemia, clotting disorders, sickle cell disease, hemophilia, leukemia, and lymphoma.

creators.name: Dr. Katherine Berg
creators.description: Katherine Berg, PhD, associate professor emerita, is an expert in rehabilitation sciences and a fellow of interRAI. She is recognized for her leadership in post-acute and rehabilitation research, particularly within interRAI’s Instrument and System Development Committee. Dr. Berg's research focuses on outcome measurement and the development of tools for post-acute and rehabilitation care.

creators.name: Dr. Charles Antzelevitch
creators.description: Charles Antzelevitch, PhD, FAHA, FHRS, FACC, is a professor and executive director of cardiovascular research at the Lankenau Institute for Medical Research. Dr. Antzelevitch is a prominent researcher investigating the diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of arrhythmias, especially those found in inherited cardiac diseases, and methods to grow new hearts using stem cells.

creators.name: Dr. Arya M. Sharma
creators.description: Arya M. Sharma, MD, DSc, FRCPC, is professor emeritus of medicine & past-chair in obesity research and management at the University of Alberta, Edmonton, Canada. He is also the past-clinical co-chair of the Alberta Health Services Obesity Program. Dr. Sharma’s research focuses on the evidence-based prevention and management of obesity and its complications.

creators.name: Dr. Catherine Thieblemont
creators.description: Catherine Thieblemont, MD, PhD, is the head of the hemato-oncology department at Hôpital Saint-Louis and a professor at Université Paris Descartes. Dr. Thieblemont is a distinguished researcher investigating chronic lymphoproliferative syndromes, including Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma, and chronic lymphocytic leukemia and has more than 200 publications in the field.

creators.name: Dr. Mary L. McPherson
creators.description: Mary Lynn McPherson, PharmD, MA, MDE, BCPS, CPE, is a professor in the department of pharmacy practice and science at the School of Pharmacy and serves as the executive director for advanced post-graduate education in palliative care. She has gained worldwide recognition for her expertise in hospice and palliative care pharmacy and continues to make significant contributions through her research and educational initiatives. Dr. McPherson is a dedicated researcher focusing on pain management, palliative care, and improving clinical practices on national and international stages.

creators.name: Dr. Dennis M. Black
creators.description: Dennis M. Black, PhD, is a professor and division head of clinical trials & multicenter studies at the University of California, San Francisco. He has over 20 years of experience investigating osteoporosis and therapies to treat this disease, and his research has been widely recognized and published.

creators.name: Dr. Suzanne M. Cadarette
creators.description: Suzanne M. Cadarette, PhD, is an associate professor of pharmacy and epidemiology at the University of Toronto. She is also a fellow of the WHO Collaborating Centre in Governance, Accountability and Transparency in the pharmaceutical sector and a senior adjunct scientist at ICES. Dr. Cadarette is an accomplished researcher investigating the use, benefits, and harms of prescription medications, as well as the osteoporosis and fracture prevention.

creators.name: Ns. Sandra I. Merkel
creators.description: Sandra I. Merkel, MS, RN, is a clinical nurse specialist at the University of Michigan Health System. She has over forty years of experience in pediatric nursing, with a focus on pain management, quality improvement, and evidence-based practice changes. Her primary research interests include pain measurement, pain behavior, and pain assessment in acute pain management settings.

creators.name: Dr. Leonard K. H. Koh
creators.description: Leonard Koh, MD, is an endocrinology specialist currently practicing at Gleneagles Hospital, Singapore. He has held leadership roles, including president of the Endocrine & Metabolic Society of Singapore and the Osteoporosis Society of Singapore. Dr. Koh is an accomplished researcher investigating hormonal and metabolic disorders, including diabetes, thyroid disease, osteoporosis, and obesity.

creators.name: Dr. Kerry Siminoski
creators.description: Dr. Kerry Siminoski, MD, is a professor in the department of radiology and diagnostic imaging, and the division of endocrinology and metabolism at the University of Alberta. Dr. Siminoski is a dedicated researcher focusing on osteoporosis, bone density, and metabolic bone diseases, significantly contributing to clinical guidelines and practices in Canada.

creators.name: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
creators.description: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) is a federal agency tasked with enhancing and protecting the health and well-being of all Americans. HHS oversees programs that provide health and human services and fosters advances in medicine, public health, and social services. The department plays a crucial role in ensuring healthcare access, improving public health outcomes, and supporting research and innovation in health-related fields.

creators.name: Dr. Christopher B. Pierce
creators.description: Christopher Baxter Pierce, MHS, is a research associate at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health. He is affiliated with the department of epidemiology, specifically in the division of general epidemiology and methodology. His work focuses on chronic kidney disease, glomerular filtration rate, proteinuria, and other aspects of medicine and public health.

creators.name: Dr. Diana M. Thomas
creators.description: Diana M. Thomas, PhD, is a professor of mathematics at the United States Military Academy at West Point and serves on editorial boards for several nutrition journals, including the European Journal of Clinical Nutrition. She has held joint research appointments at prominent obesity research centers. Dr. Thomas's research explores exercise, nutrition, body weight regulation, and innovative methods for monitoring diet and predicting injury risk using mathematical approaches.

creators.name: Dr. Charles G. Fisher
creators.description: Charles G. Fisher, MD, MHSC, FRCSC, is a professor and former division head of the combined neurosurgical & orthopaedic spine program at Vancouver General Hospital and the University of British Columbia. He is the former president of the Canadian Spine Society. Dr. Fisher is a distinguished researcher with special interests in spine trauma, oncology, and evidence-based medicine, and he has authored nearly 350 peer-reviewed publications.

creators.name: Dr. Joseph D. Khoury
creators.description: Joseph D. Khoury, MD, is the Stokes-Shackleford professor and chair of the department of pathology and microbiology at the University of Nebraska Medical Center. He is internationally recognized as a leader in hematopathology, with extensive expertise in clinical diagnostics, teaching, and translational research. Dr. Khoury's primary interests include hematopathology, cancer biomarkers, and applying computational biology, artificial intelligence, and machine learning to cancer classification and reporting.

creators.name: Dr. Ayalew Tefferi
creators.description: Ayalew Tefferi, MD, is a consultant in the division of hematology at the Mayo Clinic. He is a distinguished researcher focusing on the pathophysiology, natural history, and treatment of chronic myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs), including diseases like polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia, and primary myelofibrosis. Dr. Tefferi's work has significantly contributed to developing genetic and clinical-molecular prognostic models, advancing novel therapeutics, and improving understanding and treatment guidelines for MPNs.

creators.name: Dr. Daniel A. Arber
creators.description: Daniel A. Arber, MD, is the Donald West and Mary Elizabeth King Professor of pathology and chair of the department of pathology. He is an internationally recognized expert in diagnosing and classifying hematopoietic tumors, including leukemia and lymphoma. Dr. Arber's research focuses on leukemia, lymphoma, and myeloid neoplasms, contributing significantly to the understanding and advancement of hematopathology.

creators.name: Dr. Maarten J. Titulaer
creators.description: Maarten Titulaer, MD, is an associate professor of neurology at Erasmus University Medical Center in Rotterdam, where he co-directs the Academic Center for Neuro-inflammatory Disorders. Dr. Titulaer is a distinguished researcher in autoimmune encephalitis, focusing on translational research, combining epidemiological studies with detailed patient analyses to develop personalized treatment options based on precise phenotypes and validated biomarkers.

creators.name: Dr. Francesco Rodeghiero
creators.description: Francesco Rodeghiero, MD, is the director of the department of cellular therapy and hematology at the Regional San Bortolo Hospital in Vicenza. He is also a professor in the post-graduate school of hematology at Verona University and teaches on haemorrhagic and thrombotic disorders. Dr. Rodeghiero is a prominent researcher conducting investigations on haemophilia, von Willebrand disease, thrombophilia, and other haematological conditions.

creators.name: Dr. Iván Álvarez-Twose
creators.description: Iván Álvarez-Twose, MD, is a staff physician and clinical coordinator at the Instituto de Estudios de Mastocitosis de Castilla La Mancha (CLMast) in Toledo, Spain. He is also the director of the Mastocytosis Unit at Blue Healthcare. Dr. Alvarez-Twose is an esteemed researcher specializing in the diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment of mastocytosis and related diseases, with a focus on translational research.

creators.name: Dr. Naseema Gangat
creators.description: Naseema Gangat, MBBS is a professor of medicine and a consultant in hematology at Mayo Clinic. She has received numerous awards for her research and teaching and has contributed to various committees and editorial boards in hematology and oncology. Dr. Gangat is a distinguished researcher focused on myeloid malignancies, particularly myelodysplastic syndromes and myeloproliferative neoplasms.

creators.name: Dr. Paola Guglielmelli
creators.description: Paola Guglielmelli, MD, is a researcher scientist in hematology at the University of Florence. She is a member of CRIMM and has contributed extensively to understanding the molecular and epigenetic mechanisms in myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN). Dr. Guglielmelli is a distinguished researcher studying the JAK-STAT pathway, Calreticulin, and PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathways, with a focus on developing novel therapeutic strategies for MPN.

creators.name: Dr. Julie C. Leonard
creators.description: Julie C. Leonard, MD, MPH , is a professor of pediatrics at Ohio State University College of Medicine and a board-certified pediatric emergency medicine subspecialist. She practices in the emergency department at Nationwide Children's Hospital, where she also serves as a principal i nvestigator in the Center for Injury Research and Policy at the Abigail Wexner Research Institute. Dr. Leonard has developed expertise in the emergency management of injured children throughout her career. She collaborates with the Pediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network (PECARN) and is the principal investigator for the Great Lakes Atlantic Emergency Medical Services for Children Research Node (GLACiER). She has published extensively on cervical spine injury and received NIH funding to develop a pediatric cervical spine injury risk assessment tool for prehospital and emergency department clinicians.

creators.name: Dr. Peter Valent
creators.description: Peter Valent, MD, is a distinguished hematologist and stem cell researcher at the Medical University of Vienna, where he leads a research group and serves as the scientific director of the Ludwig Boltzmann Institute for Hematology and Oncology. He coordinates the European Competence Network on Mastocytosis and has significantly contributed to the development of diagnostic criteria and the WHO classification of mastocytosis. Dr. Valent's research focuses on mast cell disorders, cancer stem cells, and various hematologic neoplasms, with the aim of developing more effective therapies.

creators.name: Dr. Roos J. Leguit
creators.description: Roos J. Leguit, MD, is a pathologist at the University Medical Center Utrecht. She serves as the chairman of the local organizing committee for the European Bone Marrow Working Group of the European Association for Haematopathology. Dr. Leguit's primary research focuses on bone marrow pathology, histopathology, and myelodysplastic syndromes​.

creators.name: Dr. Julian D. Gillmore
creators.description: Julian Gillmore, MD, PhD, is a professor of medicine at University College London and the centre head at UCL’s Centre for Amyloidosis & Acute Phase Proteins. He is the clinical lead for ATTR amyloidosis at the UK National Amyloidosis Centre and has published more than 250 peer-reviewed articles. Dr. Gillmore is a dedicated researcher focusing on the pathogenesis, diagnosis, and treatment of amyloidosis, with a particular interest in mechanisms of amyloid regression.

creators.name: Dr. Martha Grogan
creators.description: Martha Grogan, MD, is a consultant in the Department of Cardiovascular Diseases and the director of the Cardiac Amyloid Clinic at Mayo Clinic, Minnesota. She has served as the cardiovascular medical editor of MayoClinic.com for almost a decade and lectures widely on cardiac amyloidosis. Dr. Grogan is a renowned researcher focusing on cardiac amyloidosis, echocardiography, and heart failure.
